News.title: PC Harper’s widow calls killers’ early release ‘gut punch’ as his former police force considers joining legal action
News.content:
WIDOW'S FURY PC Harper’s widow calls killers’ early release ‘gut punch’ as his former police force considers joining legal action

PC HARPER’S widow has branded his killer’s release a “gut punch”, as his former police force considers joining legal action over early release.

Lissie Harper, 35, has slammed the government’s decision to push ahead with plans that could see Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers freed.



Both offenders could be let out just halfway through their 13-year sentences under Labour’s early release scheme, starting in October.

In 2019 PC Harper, 28, was fatally dragged by a car driven by Henry Long, 18, as it towed a stolen quad bike.



Long, Bowers and Cole, then 17, were found guilty of manslaughter. The younger pair got 13 years’ jail, Long got 16 and will stay in prison.

Today, Lissie slammed the pair’s potential release, saying: ” [The] Government has punched us in the gut.

“They should be ashamed of themselves.

“Hopefully we can make the current Government come to their senses and realise we cannot put people like this back on our streets.



“Justice should mean justice and serving the sentence given.”

It comes as Thames Valley Police Chief Constable Jason Hogg said he was receiving legal advice on whether the force could join a legal challenge mounted by the local Police Federation to prevent their release.

Mr Burnham, who is taking a holiday after two weeks in No 10, is facing growing fury over Labour’s early release scheme.

He launched an urgent review of Sir Keir’s plan which aimed to ease pressure on packed jails but the plans are now set to be enacted starting in October.

Some 5,000 people are expected to be released early under sentencing changes.



This is down from 6,000 after the review, which saw ministers exempt rapists and “serious” child sex offenders as part of the scheme to tackle overcrowding in jails.

Mr Burnham said: “I wanted to go even further as I know there will still be concerns about other offenders having their sentence shortened.

“But it’s not possible without the prison system reaching capacity and collapsing, which would put public safety at much greater risk.”



Cole and Bowers, who were sentenced for the manslaughter of PC Harper, remain eligible for early release under the current plans.

More than 230,000 people have signed a petition launched on Tuesday demanding the Government takes action to keep the killers in jail.

Aileen O’Connor, who chairs the Thames Valley Police Federation, vowed to: “Throw everything at this through a proper legal challenge from KCs, barristers, you name it.”

Asked if he would join the legal challenge to keep the two thugs locked up, Thames Valley Police Chief Constable Jason Hogg said it was something he “certainly would consider.”

He went on: “I do think that the public opinion is overwhelming in this matter, but I think it’s unfair and I do believe confidence in the criminal justice system risks being damaged.



“It’s right for the Government to have a look at this matter.”

Tory leader Kemi Badenoch condemned the PM’s move to plough ahead with early release, which adds to the 70,000 who have been released early under various Labour schemes.

She said: “Andy Burnham wants a round of applause for agreeing not to release rapists and child sex offenders.

“He’s not getting one. This is only a partial climbdown.

“Killers, violent offenders, men who have terrorised their partners and more will all still walk out of prison in October.”



Meanwhile, Justice Minister Jake Richards said the killers would remain subject to the early release scheme from October as he faced broadcasters this morning.

He said: “It would be wrong to pick out individual cases within different offending cohorts.

“That wouldn’t be right. It wouldn’t be lawful either.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I understand the strength of feeling from police officers generally, but of course within that force in particular after the awful incident with Pc Andrew Harper.

“If we do not have prison places available then the police, the good work that they do every day on the streets, finding perpetrators, locking them up, it would be impossible.”

News.title: Jailed pop star Gary Glitter appears in court on historic sex offence charges including assaults on girl under age of 14
News.content:
GLITTER IN DOCK Jailed pop star Gary Glitter appears in court on historic sex offence charges including assaults on girl under age of 14

POP star Gary Glitter has appeared in court on historic sex offence charges including three counts of indecent assault on a girl under 14.

Glitter – whose real name is Paul Gadd – was accused of the assaults in the late 1970s and early 1980s.



The ex-pop star, 82, has also been charged with unlawful sexual intercourse with a girl under 13.

The charges relate to one victim, Westminster Magistrates’ Court heard.



Prosecutor Jonathan Polnay KC said the alleged offences occurred between 1978 and 1981, when the complainant, who cannot be identified for legal reasons, was aged eight to 11.

The offences allegedly took place at Glitter’s home address in Kensington and Chelsea, west London.



Police said the allegations were first reported to the Met on January 9, 2025.

Prosecutors allege Glitter would give the girl chocolate and “invite her into his house where he then committed a number of serious sexual offences.”



He appeared at the court via videolink wearing a blue shirt, glasses and a cap.

After being asked to confirm his name, Glitter said: “Your honour, excuse me, I’m extremely deaf and unless I’m lip-reading I can’t hear.

“My name is Paul Gadd.”

Glitter added: “Sorry, your honour, may I make a suggestion?

“If the barrister turns the volume down a little bit, it wouldn’t be so distorting in my hearing aids.”



Glitter was charged with one count of unlawful sexual intercourse with a girl under the age of 13 last month.

He was also charged with three counts of indecent assault on a girl under the age of 14.

Glitter was first interviewed on July 22, 2025 in relation to the investigation.

The victim is currently being supported by specialist officers.

The probe could see the ex-glam rocker — who uses a wheelchair in jail — facing trial again and spending the rest of his life locked up.



He is held at category C HMP Channings Wood in Devon.

Chief Magistrate Paul Goldspring remanded Glitter into custody and he will next appear at the Old Bailey on September 2 – the judge added it was “to be determined” whether this would be via videolink or in person.

The judge told Glitter: “You face charges that include an offence which is indictable only, which means only the crown court can deal with it.

“The other three charges are related because it’s the same complainant.

“In that circumstance, all four charges are sent to crown court, the Central Criminal Court, known as the Old Bailey, where you will appear on September 2.”



Glitter’s current term expires in February 2031 when he would be almost 87.

Glitter is understood to have denied the accusations.

A source previously told The Sun: “Specialist detectives have spoken to Glitter in prison and he has denied the allegations.

“But he knows how serious this is and what it could mean for him.

“He’s very down and fears never tasting freedom again.



“He is pretty much on his last legs in jail and this could finish him off. But his alleged victim wants justice before he dies.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Glitter was first jailed in 1999.

The former pop star then got 16 years in 2015 and was released on licence halfway through his sentence in February 2023.

News.title: Fugitive Brit sex offender, 37, on UK’s most wanted list is arrested in Spain after ‘hiding out in Benidorm’
News.content:
A FUGITIVE British sex offender who was on the UK’s most wanted list has been arrested in Spain.

John Rocks, 37, was taken into custody in Madrid after a failed manhunt in Benidorm.



The Scottish criminal had been hiding out on the Costa Blanca to avoid arrest for several sex offences committed between 2012 and 2022.

Rocks was recently placed on the National Crime Agency’s Most Wanted list, with police publishing his photo alongside caption: “Do you know where John Rocks is?”



Footage of the arrest released by Spanish authorities showed two plain-clothed officers escorting Rocks to police patrol car after pouncing on him in a busy street on August 1.

He is now languishing behind bars in the Spanish capital after going before an extradition judge.



It remains unclear whether Rocks will be allowed to return to the UK, where he is wanted by Police Scotland.

Referring to him only by his initials, Spain‘s national police said: “National Police officers have arrested J.R., 37, in Madrid, who was wanted by the British authorities for several sexual assault offences.



“The detainee had fled justice in his home country and was the subject of an active International Arrest Warrant issued by the British authorities.

“He appeared in the campaign ‘The UK’s Most Wanted Fugitives,’ launched by the organisation CrimeStoppers.”

“The alleged perpetrator, a British national, was believed to be hiding in Spain,” they continued.

“The acts investigated by British officers involved serious sexual assaults against various victims, some of whom were in a romantic relationship with the suspect at the time of the incidents.

“The efforts to locate the target included several trips to Benidorm, as well as numerous surveillance operations and on-site checks at places he was known to frequent.



“These actions made it possible to establish behaviour patterns, obtain clues about his possible whereabouts, and identify third parties who might have been helping him.

“The investigation proved especially complex due to the concealment measures adopted by the wanted man.”

Speaking about the arrest, the police said: “During the operation, officers finally located the target, who was wearing a cap and glasses to partially conceal his face, and he was arrested.

“The detainee did not cooperate during the identification process, was not carrying any identification documents, and provided different personal details.

“However, an initial comparison of his visible tattoos made it possible to determine that he was the wanted individual. His identity was later confirmed through fingerprint analysis.



“The arrested man was brought before the Investigating Section of the Central Court of First Instance, Courtroom 3 in Madrid, pending a decision on his extradition.”

Rocks was one of two Scots named on a list of the UK’s most wanted fugitives.

The other was Derek McGraw Ferguson, 62, who is wanted in connection with the murder of Thomas Cameron in a Glasgow pub car park in 2007.

Spanish cops described Ferguson as “dangerous” and warned he could be armed.

Hours after Rocks was named as one of the UK’s most wanted fugitives, another man on the list was held in La Nucia just north of Benidorm.



Convicted drug smuggler Simon Dutton, 49, from Bolton, Greater Manchester, arrested in a bar in Greece in December 2015, was wanted for a re-call to prison.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Rick Jones, NCA Deputy Director International, said of Rocks’ arrest: “This arrest marks the 101st arrest in Operation Captura, a multi-agency campaign aimed at tracking down the UK’s most wanted individuals in Spain.

“I pay tribute to the excellent work of our colleagues in the Spanish National Police who made this possible. Working with them, and other law enforcement partners, we are determined to do all we can to ensure fugitives are returned to face the courts.”

News.title: Moment woman is tackled & arrested by taser-wielding cops after four stabbed outside theatre in London’s Covent Garden
News.content:
THIS is the moment a woman was arrested by taser-wielding cops after four men were stabbed in a horror broad daylight rampage at Covent Garden.

The victims were rushed to a major trauma centre following the attack in central London this afternoon.



Pictures showed an Air Ambulance helicopter landing in a packed Trafalgar Square with the incident believed to be “isolated ” and “mental health related”, according to cops.

The London Ambulance Service (LAS) confirmed crews were scrambled to the area shortly after midday as shocked tourists watched on.



Dramatic footage taken at the scene showed cops armed with tasers in a tense stand-off with a woman.

Officers were seen talking with her on the junction between Short’s Gardens and Neal Street.



They then tackle her to the ground and appear to restrain her as terrified bystanders kept their distance.

After being treated at the scene, the victims – aged 34, 39, 42 and 52 – were then rushed to hospital “as a priority”.

Two remain in hospital with injuries that are not believed to be life-threatening or life changing but the other two victims have since been discharged, emergency services said.

A 47-year-old woman has since been arrested on suspicion of possession of an offensive weapon and assault.



She was taken to custody while officers cordoned off a huge stretch on Endell Street, with an array of police cars parked along the road.

It is understood the stabbing was a mental health-related incident and a pair of scissors were recovered at the scene.

The Met Police said: “At around 12:27hrs on Wednesday, police were called to reports of stabbing on Endell Street, Covent Garden.

“Officers attended alongside the London Ambulance Service and London’s Air Ambulance.



“Four men – aged 34, 39, 42, and 52 – were found with stab wounds and assessed at the scene by paramedics.

“They have since been taken to hospital and we await an update on their injuries.

“A 47-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of possession of an offensive weapon and assault.

“She was taken to custody where she remains.



“Police remain in the area, with a scene in place on Endell Street and the surrounding areas in Covent Garden.”

A horrified witness at the Craft Beer Co claimed a woman approached members of the public outside a nearby theatre.

They told LBC she then she stabbed two men in the back, ran down Endell Street, then stabbed more people.

An LAS spokesperson added: “We were called at 12:29pm today (5 August) to reports of a stabbing on Endell Street, WC2H.

“We sent an ambulance crew, paramedic in a fast response car and an incident response officer. We also dispatched London’s Air Ambulance.

“We treated four patients at the scene and took them all to a major trauma centre as a priority by road”.

News.title: The bizarre conspiracy theory engulfing evil undertaker Robert Bush as MORE questions raised over his ‘suspicious’ past
News.content:
IT’S a scene of such horror that even hardened cops were sickened when they found rotting bodies at a funeral parlour.

Undertaker Robert Bush was jailed 20 years for stockpiling bodies and handing relatives ashes belonging to strangers. But the scandal has ignited bizarre rumours surrounding the man Bush bought his business from.



Bush opened Legacy Independent Funeral Directors after taking over the Hessle Road building from Simon Woolston, who operated another undertakers called Heavenly Services.

Heavenly collapsed in October 2021 and police launched an investigation into potential fraud at the firm after customers complained they had taken out pre-paid funeral plans and paid for non-existent burial plots.





Just two weeks before the police probe Woolston, a locally famous drag queen who also owned companies in Thailand, suddenly died, prompting suspicion from locals.

Now social media sleuths and families involved in Legacy are convinced that Woolston, 51, is alive and well and that Robert Bush handled his cremation – despite there being no evidence of the conspiracy.

Read More Features 'SICKENING' Evil funeral boss enjoyed days out as victims’ relatives waited for justice

One woman, whose mother-in-law was one of the 35 bodies found at Legacy, told The Sun: “It’s all too much of a coincidence that both Bush and Woolston were investigated for selling funeral plans that didn’t exist.

“We’re all suspicious that Woolston showed Bush how to con people. We’ve heard that Bush handled his cremation and, given his history, how do we know that he actually disposed of a body?



“We’ve also heard that Woolston’s death was reported late and by phone because it was during the pandemic which has led to questions about whether he is actually dead.”

There is no indication that Bush handled Woolston’s cremation or that the pair knew each other outside business transactions.

Records also show that Woolston died of sepsis and his death was registered in January 2022.



But it has not stopped a slew of conspiracy theories around Woolston’s death.

One Facebook commentator wrote: “The odd thing I find is how Simon died in October but then only two months later Legacy took over the premises. That’s a very quick turnaround.”

Another penned: “All this goes back to Simon.”

A third commented: “I don’t believe Simon is dead. It’s so suspicious that Rob apparently did his funeral.”

Woolston was once the director of Hull’s Pride event and ran several pubs around the city, including one of its most historic, the George. He had a drag queen alter ego called Lucy.



He courted controversy when he first opened Heavenly after putting up a cheeky billboard advertising cheap funerals opposite Hull Royal Infirmary.

When he first opened Heavenly, which also operated in Bradford, Scunthorpe, Grimsby and Leeds, Woolston offered journalists a chance to ‘tour’ the building.

But the business soon hit the headlines for the wrong reasons when employee Dana Twidale was convicted of fraud.



Wedding planner Twidale, 49, from Hull, fled to Spain after conning brides and grooms out of thousands of pounds. She was jailed for five years in 2021 after taking £15,000 from 24 couples.

She also defrauded more than £42,000 from a man she met on a dating site and conned a woman while working at Heavenly – spinning a lie with eerie parallels to Robert Bush.

Twidale tricked Nigel Wainwright, who she met on Tinder, after telling him her mother had died and her body was “rotting” at Heavenly.

She also conned grieving Fiona Barker, whose son had taken his own life, into giving her £300 after falsely claiming her brother tried to do the same thing.

Humberside Police has previously confirmed an investigation into Heavenly.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

A statement read: “An investigation was carried out in November 2021 after we received reports from members of the public regarding the fraudulent use of monies intended for pre-paid funeral plans through the company Heavenly Services.

“Heavenly Services operated at the same premise on Hessle Road, Hull, as a separate company, Legacy funeral Directors, who we received a report of concern about the storage and management processes relating to care of the deceased in these locations…we do not believe the two investigations to be connected.”

News.title: Royal fans convinced they’ve worked out Princess Eugenie’s baby name in major Instagram clue
News.content:
PRINCESS Eugenie and Jack Brooksbank announced the birth of their daughter yesterday – and royal fans think they’ve worked out her name.

The royal couple took to Instagram to share the news they had welcomed their third child but did not confirm what they’ve called her.



In a statement posted alongside a sweet snapshot of the newborn, Eugenie and Jack said: “Jack and I are so excited to announce Baby Girl Brooksbank!!

“We are beyond in love with our girlie,” they added.



While details of the baby girl’s name were not included in the upload, royal fans think the late Queen Elizabeth II‘s great-granddaughter and her husband may have added a hint.

Using Instagram’s music feature to add a backing track to the upload, Eugenie announced her daughter’s birth to the sound of Isn’t She Lovely by Stevie Wonder.

The iconic 1976 track was written by the music legend to celebrate the birth of his daughter, Aisha Morris.

Royal supporters have pointed out that Princess Eugenie and Jack may have used Aisha in their little girl’s full moniker and used the musical tribute to share a subtle hint at her name.

No details regarding the baby’s name were shared in the Royal Family’s official statement announcing her birth, either.

The announcement did, however, confirm that Princess Eugenie gave birth in the Portuguese capital of Lisbon and revealed the baby’s weight.



“Her Royal Highness Princess Eugenie and Mr Jack Brooksbank are delighted to announce the safe arrival of their daughter, born on Monday, 3rd August 2026, at 6.20pm, at a hospital in Lisbon, Portugal,” Buckingham Palace’s statement said.

“The baby was born weighing 6 pounds 9 ounces.

“Their Majesties The King and Queen and other members of The Royal Family were delighted to be informed of the news,” the announcement added.

Princess Eugenie and Jack are also parents to two sons – August Philip Hawke Brooksbank, born in 2021, and Ernest George Ronnie Brooksbank, born in 2023.

The names of both boys include sweet nods to Eugenie’s royal relatives, with August’s middle name paying tribute to the late Prince Philip and Ernest’s middle name given in honour of King George VI.



Eugenie and Jack’s daughter’s middle name will no doubt be given in honour of her great grandmother, Queen Elizabeth II.

It seems to have become tradition for the Queen’s grandchildren to give at least one of their daughters the middle name.

This includes Princess Beatrice, whose daughters are called Sienna Elizabeth Mapelli Mozzi and Athena Elizabeth Mapelli Mozzi.

Prince William’s daughter, Princess Charlotte, was also given the middle name, with a full moniker of Charlotte Elizabeth Diana.

Peter Phillips’ second-born daughter is Isla Elizabeth Phillips, while Zara Tindall’s second-born daughter is Lena Elizabeth Tindall.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

And, of course, Prince Harry’s daughter, Princess Lilibet, was famously named using the nickname that Queen Elizabeth II used throughout her life.

News.title: Woman sexually assaulted at Tube station during rush hour as cops release CCTV in hunt for man
News.content:
ATTACK PROBE Woman sexually assaulted at Tube station during rush hour as cops release CCTV in hunt for man

COPS have released CCTV of a man they would like to speak to after a woman was allegedly sexually assaulted at a tube station.

The alleged incident took place at around 5pm on June 15 at Bond Street Underground station, said British Transport Police.



A female passenger was reportedly sexually assaulted as she walked through the tunnel from the Elizabeth Line to the Central Line platform.

Cops launched an investigation and released a CCTV image of a man who they believe can help in connection with the incident.



Detectives would like to speak to the man pictured, as he may have information that could assist their investigation.

Anyone who recognises him is asked to text BTP on 61016 or call 0800 40 50 40, quoting reference 484 of 15 June.

Information can be given anonymously to Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

News.title: First pics of bomb drone found at German airport near Ukrainian cargo jets after another plane’s terrifying collision
News.content:
A BOMB drone that crashed near Ukrainian cargo jets at a German airport has been pictured after sparking a major security alert.

The explosive-laden drone was found as a second mystery object struck a DHL cargo plane climbing away from Leipzig/Halle Airport overnight.



Police deployed a bomb disposal robot to inspect the stricken drone, which was found near a fleet Ukrainian Antonov cargo planes shortly before midnight.

German airports have been on high alert after a string of unauthorised drone overflights have been spotted.



They have been seen worryingly near to military facilities, energy terminals, seaports and logistics companies.

Police said that these overflights may be connected to Russian agents.

Antonov planes have used Leipzig/Halle as an operating base since Russia‘s full-scale invasion in 2022.

The southern runway of the airport, a major hub for DHL and Ukrainian jets, remained closed while bomb experts examined the device.



X-ray imaging showed the drone was attached to a defective detonator.

The explosive may have been one that can be made easily from fertiliser and petrol, according to Bild.

Several planes, including a passenger flight, were diverted overnight.



While air traffic was being redirected, one cargo plane had to abort its landing.

It then reportedly hit an unknown object before landing in Hanover, where minor damage to the nose section was discovered.

European security agencies have been probing a series of incendiary devices concealed in parcels that caught fire in 2024.

These incidents raised concerns that malicious actors may be planning to sabotage air cargo operators.

Putin was even suspected of planting a parcel bomb on a flight headed to a depot in the UK.



Some of the devices were found at a DHL warehouse in Leipzig and in freight shipments in transit across Europe.

The Leipzig package started burning as it was being loaded onto a plane after it had come from Lithuania.

The head of the German domestic intelligence agency said if it had exploded on the plane it could have brought it down.

An Interior Ministry spokesperson said they could determine no connection between last night’s drone and these incidents.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Russia has denied any involvement in the 2024 incidents and the more recent overflights.



DHL Group CEO Tobias Meyer said the German logistics firm was still investigating the incident while trying to minimise the impact on customers.

News.title: Covent Garden stabbing live: Police arrest woman in London as four men stabbed
News.content:
A woman has been arrested after four men were stabbed in Covent Garden in central London - the men were taken to a major trauma centre

Covent Garden stabbing live: Police arrest woman in London as four men stabbed

A 47-year-old woman has been arrested after four men were stabbed in London's Covent Garden.

The London Ambulance Service was called at 12.29pm today to reports of stabbings on Endell Street. It treated four people at the scene before taking them to a major trauma centre.

The four men are aged 34, 39, 42 and 52, the Metropolitan Police said. Their injuries are not believed to be life-threatening.

The woman was arrested on suspicion of possession of an offensive weapon and assault. She was taken to police custody where she remains. Images show police detaining a woman at the scene.

A London Air Ambulance has been pictured landing in Trafalgar Square.

News.title: I returned home and saw my garden looked different - it was my neighbour's fault
News.content:
I returned home and saw my garden looked different - it was my neighbour's fault

The Reddit user shared how upset they felt after seeing the change

View 3 Images The Reddit user was not impressed by the changes they saw (stock image) (Image: Getty)

A homeowner has expressed their dismay after returning home to find their garden had suddenly changed, claiming it was due to their neighbour's actions. Taking to Reddit's popular 'GardeningUK' forum page, a user called @Slinkysoft said their "neighbours mowed and strimmed the garden without asking".

‌



Explaining the situation, the user said: "My partner and I just returned from visiting friends and a friend of ours has been house sitting and looking after the cat while we were gone. On the way back from the station he mentioned that the neighbours must have cut the grass because it was now suddenly shorter.

‌



"I was already on edge because we like to keep the grass longer for wildlife and the lawn looked absolutely beautiful recently. But when I got home and it was way worse than I thought it would be."

‌



Sharing what they saw upon arriving back home, they said: "ALL the grass had been cut so so short, one of my lovely potted ornamental grasses has been caught up in it and will probably never recover. And I’ve also been growing willow canes at the bottom of the garden and have been so excited about the growth on them, which has now all been sliced off, and the willow canes themselves completely destroyed."

Expressing how much the neighbours' actions affected them, the Reddit user said: "No this isn’t a ‘real’ problem but I use my garden as a way of dealing with the real problems and I’m certain the neighbours didn’t mean to do this but I’ve put time, money and effort into that garden... I’m so sad and angry."

View 3 Images The Reddit user claims a neighbour mowed the lawn without asking (stock image)

‌



In the comment section, one person asked: "How did they gain access?" The original author of the post replied: "Came in around the side. We’re in a semi-terrace."

A second put: "If you don't have fences/gates then now is the time to get them installed." A third wrote: "I am FURIOUS for you, OP. Just because someone thinks they’re making your place look better, doesn’t mean it’s not vandalism."

Offering reassurance, someone else said: "Everything will recover. Grasses are unbelievably resilient as they all grow from their base. Take a breath, console yourself that you’ve lost a couple of months growth and prepare for a rapid recovery. Nature will always recover if you give it time."

Article continues below

View 3 Images The Reddit user is worried their garden won't ever go back to how it was (stock image)

Can a neighbour mow your lawn without asking?

Your neighbour doesn't have the legal right to come onto your property, plant things, paint your fences, cut down your plants, or make any changes to your garden unless you give them clear permission. If they do any of this without your consent, it could be considered trespassing or criminal damage.

Legally speaking, going onto someone's property without their consent to mow their lawn may constitute trespassing. However, police are unlikely to intervene unless there is damage involved.

News.title: I'm A Celeb's Adam Thomas says he's 'proud' after bitter David Haye feud
News.content:
Displaying the ripped physique that’s made him a fitness magazine cover star, he has put the tensions which blew up between him and campmates David Haye and Jimmy Bullard firmly behind him. He tells The Mirror: “I've obviously had a bit of a year with the jungle and all that stuff. But I've never been better.”

A dramatic fall-out between Adam, 37, and former Fulham footballer Jimmy, 47, on the ITV show in April, saw the show hit with more than 1,000 Ofcom complaints. Accusations flew, with Jimmy saying Adam’s expletive-filled outburst was intimidating, while many of the complaints were about alleged bullying behaviour displayed towards Adam by former boxer David Haye, 45, and Jimmy.

But it’s clearly water under the bridge for Adam, who says, philosophically: “What doesn't kill you makes you stronger, hey?”

In the case of Waterloo Road star Adam, who plays teacher Donte Charles and played Adam Barton in Emmerdale for nine years, that certainly looks to be true.

‌



View 7 Images Adam has been working hard in the gym since and feels great (Image: adamthomas21/Instagram)

Determined to make the cover of Men’s Fitness mag, Adam - who lives in Cheshire with his wife Caroline, a dance school owner, and their children Teddy, 11, and Elsie-Rose, eight - has been seriously hitting the gym. He explains: “I just wanted to focus on myself, really, and get my head in a great space. This wasn’t just physical for me, but mental as well.

“I'm really proud of myself, and I don't really say that often. At the beginning of the year, I started this vision board. I’d never done a vision board before in my life, and I said I wanted to be on the front cover of a fitness magazine. I ticked that off.”

Adam, whose twin brother Scott was on Love Island in 2016 and whose brother Ryan,42, played Jason Grimshaw in Corrie, says one person was key to him learning how to take positive action after tricky situations like the camp rows - his former teacher.

‌



View 7 Images The Thomas Trio: brothers Adam Thomas, Scott Thomas and Ryan Thomas (Image: ITV/REX/Shutterstock)

According to Adam, who with his brothers co-hosts the popular podcast, At Home With the Thomas Bros., his former drama teacher Darren Gordon gave him the tools for success.

Recalling his early school days, growing up in Manchester, he says: “There were a few times that I could have got expelled. I was a bit of a tearaway, always causing mischief. I wasn't a bad kid but I was always being the class clown, I was always distracting other people.

“My son came home from school and was upset. He said, ‘the other kids in class are stopping me from learning, Dad.’ And I was like, ‘Oh my, I was one of those kids!’”

‌



School was tough, according to Adam, who says: “Being a twin brother, I went to public school and my twin went to grammar school. His nickname was ‘the professor’, he was very clever.

View 7 Images Adam with his family: wife Caroline and children Teddy and Elsie-Rose (Image: instagram/ @adamthomas21)

“Even at a young age, there was pressure for me to compete with my brother. I remember GCSE day. He got all A*s, I wasn’t expecting any. I remember being so nervous and feeling like I was going to let my mum down.”

Adam, who came ninth on Strictly in 2023, initially wanted to be a dancer. He says: “I wanted to do dance, but my school wouldn’t let me, because I was the only boy that wanted to do it in school. Maybe I would have won Strictly if I was able to do dance. I’d have had the training.”

‌



But it was drama that became his saviour. He continues: “The arts meant the world to me, because I just knew that was the one thing that I was good at. One thing my report card did say was ‘he's going to be a star. He's going to be on TV.’

“I never looked at school as a place to learn, because I think from such a young age, I always knew what I wanted to be.”

View 7 Images I'm A Celebrity champion Adam Thomas, with Declan Donnelly (Image: Jonathan Hordle/ITV/Shutterstock)

An ambassador for the Blue Light Card Teacher Impact Report, a newly released study that reveals how teachers shape pupils’ lives long after they leave the classroom, in an emotional video for the campaign, Adam reunites with Darren Gordon, who taught him at Mid Cheshire College, Hartford and Winsford.

‌



The Blue Light report reveals that 63% of Brits believe teachers deserve more recognition, while 53% say they still don't receive the credit they deserve.

Adam says: "Teachers are the unsung heroes of most people's lives. Darren was more than a teacher. He was a friend. He was one of those people that I could talk to about anything and everything.

“Those teachers are so important - they change and shape lives. Darren certainly did that for me. Darren created a space where I could be who I wanted to be. I felt so safe in those rooms.”

View 7 Images Adam Thomas was an Emmerdale regular for nine years (Image: adamthomas21/Instagram)

‌



With Darren’s encouragement, Adam won the part of Donte in Waterloo Road, which he played first time around from 2006 to 2009, then moving to Emmerdale, where he stayed until a conversation with EastEnders and Gavin and Stacey star Larry Lamb.

He was on I’m a Celebrity with Larry in 2016, when he came third, and recalls how the older actor encouraged him to jump ship. He says: “It's very difficult to leave a soap and go on to something else. After a time, you get very comfortable, and it becomes like your safety blanket

“I left Emmerdale because of the Jungle when I first did it in 2016. I remember having a conversation with Larry Lamb in there, and he was like, ‘you need to get out there, you need to do other stuff.’”

However, after handing in his notice, Adam struggled to get acting work, adding: “I left and then nothing happened, and I was like, ‘Oh, s*** - this is not how it's supposed to go. Larry lamb what were you thinking?’

‌



View 7 Images Adam hugs Darren Gordon, a director, agent and acting coach and his former drama college teacher

“I started working as an estate agent, working a nine-to-five. I was turning up at viewings, and showing people around houses. They were like, ‘what the f*** are you doing here?’ It was a very humbling experience.”

Then in 2023, Waterloo Road came knocking again and Adam reprised his role. But when the going got tough, Adam says it was Darren’s words of encouragement that kept him going. He says: “He always told me to believe in myself. And so I did. I try to teach my kids the same thing. You’ve got this. You can do it. It will all work out. And I truly believe that it will.”

Adam's teacher Darren says...

Darren Gordon, a director, agent and acting coach and formerly Adam Thomas' drama college teacher, says: "I first met Adam as a shy and reserved 14 year old. Brother to a soap star, he also had ambitions of a career as an actor. His polite and enthusiastic manner made him immediately appealing to work with, but as soon as he accessed strong emotion in performance, his work went to another level.

‌



“He has always been an absorbing and engaging artist, able to access any emotional state with stark authenticity, almost instantly, then drop it on 'cut', as quickly as it appeared. “Meeting him again thanks to Blue Light Card brought it all back. Adam is a formidable and irrepressible personality. To be thanked by him and reconnect properly was a truly special moment.”

*The reunion marks Blue Light Card's Teacher Impact Report, which reveals teachers’ lasting influence beyond the school years. Eligible teachers can renew for £4.99, unlocking savings at 15,000+ brands.

News.title: The four biggest Invisalign myths – busted by one man's 'incredible' smile transformation
News.content:
The four biggest Invisalign myths – busted by one man's 'incredible' smile transformation

From worrying about speaking to fears of tooth removal, here's what really happened during treatment

View 5 Images Our tester says the aligners were barely noticeable and treatment was finished in under a year (Image: Smiles + Smiles / Getty)

For years, Aman avoided smiling in photographs. Like many adults, he'd thought about straightening his teeth, but the idea of wearing traditional braces in his 30s while working in a professional role was enough to put him off.

‌



Then he discovered Invisalign. Seven months later, his before-and-after photos show a dramatic smile transformation– and, perhaps more surprisingly, none of the things he worried about actually happened. Before starting treatment at the London clinic Smiles + Smiles , Aman was convinced the clear aligners would affect his speech. "I thought I'd end up with a lisp," he admits.

‌



He also assumed treatment would drag on for years and that crowded teeth would mean having healthy teeth removed. Instead, his aligners were barely noticeable, treatment was finished in under a year and, rather than removing teeth, his dentist created the small amount of space needed using microfiling.

‌



View 5 Images Left, overlapping before treatment, right, after 7 months of Invisalign (Image: Smiles + Smiles)

View 5 Images Aman's teeth look nearly perfectly straight after 7 months of wearing the clear aligners (Image: Smiles + Smiles)

The aligners themselves quickly became part of his daily routine. Every 10 days or so, he swapped to the next set, with only a day or two of mild soreness each time as his teeth adjusted. Perhaps the biggest surprise was just how invisible they were.

‌



Despite wearing the aligners for up to 22 hours a day, nobody noticed unless Aman pointed them out. It wasn't until treatment finished that friends and family commented on how much his smile had changed. In fact, the results have proved so convincing that three of his friends have since started Invisalign treatment themselves.

According to Dr Yasmin Anaboussi, Co-Founder, Clinical Director and Principal Dentist at Smiles + Smiles , Aman's concerns are among the most common she hears.



‌



View 5 Images Patients can even see a digital simulation of how their smile is expected to look before treatment begins (Image: Getty)

"One of Invisalign's biggest advantages is that the aligners are clear and discreet, making them particularly popular with adults who may feel self-conscious about wearing fixed braces," she explains. "They're also removable, allowing patients to eat normally and maintain their usual brushing and flossing routine, which can make oral hygiene much easier throughout treatment."

Technology has also moved on considerably in recent years. "Digital treatment planning continues to evolve rapidly," says Dr Anaboussi. "High-resolution 3D scanning and increasingly sophisticated planning software allow us to map tooth movements with much greater precision, making treatment more predictable and helping us achieve the desired final result more efficiently."

‌



Patients can even see a digital simulation of how their smile is expected to look before treatment begins. Treatment times are often shorter than people expect, too.

View 5 Images Our testers' aligners were barely noticeable, treatment was finished in under a year (Image: Getty)

While particularly mild cases can sometimes be completed in just seven weeks, Dr Anaboussi says the average Invisalign journey takes between three and eight months, depending on the complexity of the case and how consistently the aligners are worn.

‌



She also addressed one of the biggest myths surrounding Invisalign – the claim that it leaves teeth permanently loose.

"All orthodontic treatment works by applying gentle, controlled pressure to move teeth through the bone," she explains. "It's completely normal to experience some mild tenderness or a slight increase in tooth mobility during treatment, but this is temporary and doesn't mean healthy teeth are becoming dangerously loose."

Today, Aman smiles confidently in photos without thinking twice. After years of assuming braces weren't an option for someone in his position, his experience proves just how much adult orthodontics has changed– and why more people are choosing clear aligners later in life.

News.title: Five million Brits harmed by wrong AI advice - including financial losses
News.content:
Five million Brits harmed by wrong AI advice - including financial losses

If an AI tool gives bad financial recommendations, you cannot claim compensation through the Financial Ombudsman Service - here are the steps to protect yourself

View 2 Images AI should not be relied on for financial advice (Image: Getty Images/Connect Images)

More than five million Brits have been harmed by wrong advice from an AI chatbot – including financial losses.

‌



New research from comparison website Uswitch.com also reveals how people have experienced health scares and even damaged relationships after confiding in the internet.

‌



More than two in five (43%) UK adults have asked a chatbot for advice on something personal – and almost half (48%) said they trust its advice as much as, or more than, a friend or family member. But nearly a quarter (23%) of AI users said incorrect chatbot advice has caused them a real problem.

‌



Almost one in five (18%) UK adults – nearly ten million people – have acted on a chatbot’s personal advice with no second opinion, climbing to two in five (40%) of Gen Z. If an AI tool gives bad financial recommendations, you cannot claim compensation through the Financial Ombudsman Service.

View 2 Images Young people are more likely to trust AI, according to research (Image: Francesco Carta fotografo via Getty Images)

‌



Chatbots will soon be included in the Online Safety Act, a law that makes social media companies and search engines responsible for user safety. Meanwhile, new EU rules require chatbots to remind users they are machines.

Uswitch recommends using AI as a starting point, and to always verify financial advice using free and impartial Government sites like MoneyHelper, a regulated financial adviser, solicitor or Citizens Advice. You should also always check its sources and never rely on out-of-date information.

Get the best deals and tips from Mirror Money WHATSAPP GROUP: Get money news and top deals straight to your phone by joining our Money WhatsApp group here. We also treat our community members to special offers, promotions, and adverts from us and our partners. If you don’t like our community, you can check out any time you like. If you’re curious, you can read our Privacy Notice. NEWSLETTER: Or sign up to the Mirror's Money newsletter here for all the best advice and shopping deals straight to your inbox.

Article continues below

Ernest Doku, Uswitch technology expert, said: “We’ve watched Britain’s internet habits change for 25 years, and this is the fastest shift yet. We used to type a question into a search bar and weigh up the results – now millions of us ask a chatbot and take its word for it, on some of the most personal things in our lives.

“Used well, AI is a brilliant sounding board – always awake, never judgemental, and often the first step for people who would struggle to ask anyone at all. But its greatest strength – that it always has an answer – is also its biggest risk. It sounds just as confident when it’s wrong as when it’s right, and this research shows the cost when that trust is misplaced.

“So keep talking to the bot, but treat its answers as a starting point rather than the final word. If the stakes are big – your health, your money or a big life decision – get a human second opinion before you act.”

News.title: Armed police officer who shot dead Chris Kaba will not face disciplinary action
News.content:
Armed police officer who shot dead Chris Kaba will not face disciplinary action

The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) confirmed today that it would not pursue disciplinary proceedings against Metropolitan Police firearms officer Martyn Blake

View 5 Images Chris Kaba was killed bu police during a stop in Streatham (Image: INQUEST/PA Wire)

The police officer that killed Chris Kaba will not face disciplinary proceedings, the UK's police watchdog has confirmed, after he was cleared of murdering the unarmed Black man.

‌



The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) has said it will not pursue proceedings against Martyn Blake, a Metropolitan Police firearms officer who shot and killed Mr Kaba after he tried to escape a police box in in Streatham, London, in 2022. Sargeant Blake, who was cleared of his murder following a trial at the Old Bailey in 2024, said he shot Mr Kaba through the window of his car because he believed the unarmed 24-year-old posed a threat to a fellow officer.

‌



Despite being cleared, he was due to face disciplinary proceedings which, due to the Government changing regulations around police use of force, will now not take place.

‌



Leader of Black and Asian police officers probed after raising concerns about racism READ MORE :

View 5 Images Martyn Blake shot Mr Kaba dead

Confirming the proceedings won't take place, IOPC director of engagement Amanda Rowe said Mr Kaba's family had been informed of the decision. She said: "Our thoughts remain with Chris Kaba's family and friends and everyone impacted by his death.

"We are acutely aware of the impact of proceedings for everyone involved in this case and have always sought to avoid any unnecessary delays, however it was right that we paused progressing disciplinary proceedings until the legislation change came into effect and its impact was clear.

‌



"Having considered both our policy and the representations from the Kaba family and Sergeant Blake, we have today notified them of our decision to withdraw disciplinary proceedings."

View 5 Images Kaba was shot dead in Streatham (Image: Andrew Quinn/PA Wire)

With the disciplinary action now longer taking place, a coroner must now decide whether to hold an inquest into the death of Mr Kaba. The 24-year-old was soon to become a dad when he was stopped by police in 2022, after the car he was driving was followed due to having links to a previous shooting in Brixton.

‌



He attempted to drive backwards after being boxed in by police, and then forwards whiel trying to ram himself free of the barrier created by the cars.

Mr Blake said it was those movements that made him believe one of his colleagues could be killed, and jurors hearing the case at the Old Bailey said he opened fire in response. Mr Kaba died from a single shot to the forehead. A fellow firearms officer said he would have taken the shot had Mr Blake not, with a second saying he was "fractions of a second" from doing the same.

View 5 Images The decision to drop the disciplinary action was hailed across the police service (Image: Vuk Valcic/ZUMA Press Wire/REX/Shutterstock)

‌



Paula Dodds, chairwoman of the Metropolitan Police Federation, said: "This is very much the right decision that will not only be welcomed by the officer and his family, but all police officers across London.

"It is imperative that there are policies in place for operational policing which support lawful decisions made by officers, based on their training, so that they should not be placed in fear of the loss of their liberty and livelihood. Police officers are of course - and rightly - highly accountable for their actions. But the officer has sadly suffered years of legal scrutiny following this incident.

"We are pleased this has all now concluded and that the officer can continue to serve the public without this hanging over him. We thank his legal team for their years of hard work on this case."

‌



View 5 Images Mr Kaba's killing sparked public protests in London (Image: Getty Images)

Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley welcomed the decision, saying: "Today's decision finally brings to an end almost four years of uncertainty for NX121, his family and the wider firearms command, with all the considerable worry and stress that has brought. We also recognise the profound impact on Chris Kaba's family, who continue to grieve their loss."

He said the IOPC's decision should be "a milestone moment to reset a police accountability system that is out of balance". He added: "No police officer is above the law, but we have been clear the system holding police to account is broken.

Article continues below

"I worry about the lack of support officers face for doing their best, but most of all I worry for the public. As I have said before, the more we crush the spirit of good officers, the less they can fight crime."

After Sgt Blake's acquittal, then-home secretary Yvette Cooper vowed to change laws around use of force for police officers, and as a result the test used by the IOPC over whether to bring misconduct proceedings has been raised to the level used in criminal law.

News.title: Mum hits out at 'horrible bin men' who catcalled her in front of 3 kids
News.content:
Mum hits out at 'horrible bin men' who catcalled her in front of 3 kids

Mum of three Imogen was out with her children, aged four, two, and 12 weeks, when she was harassed by a group of men in a council vehicle. But she didn't take it lying down

View Image Imogen Horton has more than one million followers across a range of social media accounts (Image: Getty Images)

A mum has shared her shock at being catcalled by a group of binmen - while she was out with her three young children. Imogen Horton has more than one million followers on social media, and regularly posts light-hearted looks at the ups and downs of family life, women's health, and other issues.

‌



But, in a recent clip, Imogen revealed an upsetting ordeal she had experienced while out with her two daughters, four-year-old Renaelia and two-year-old Oriavella, and 12-week-old baby boy Hero.

‌



In the clip, which features the overlaid caption "Not a good start to the day", Imogen can be seen walking down the street with Hero in a sling around her neck and her two girls in a double pushchair. Speaking out about her ordeal, she said: "Ok, that was the first time I've had men heckle me out of a van before with my three children in tow."

‌



She explained the men were in what she described as a Brighton and Hove City Council "bin truck", and had whistled at her while shouting things such as "hey mama", and "look at you mama".

Imogen continued: "I'd said 'no, you don't get to speak to me like that'. And I had to set an example for the girls, didn't I girlies?

"Because I said 'we don't accept people speaking to us like that. It's our body and they don't get to make comment and judgement on it'. And also we don't want to raise Hero to be like that do we?"

‌



She continued: "That was not ideal in the slightest, I'm not going to lie, because there were certain things I wanted to say, but obviously I'm not going to say in front of the kids."

She added: "And it was at a traffic light as well, so everyone was staring, everyone was looking, like 'why are they shouting it up?' It's just awkward and horrible and not nice, and I never, ever, ever want my daughters to feel like that.

"So I'm showing them we don't accept that behaviour by telling the men off didn't I? Mummy told the men off and we will never accept behaviour like that."

‌



People in the comments urged Imogen to report the incident to the council and the police.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

A Brighton and Hove City Council spokesperson said: “We take the concerns raised by this resident very seriously, have contacted them to gather further details, and will ensure the matter is fully investigated.

Article continues below

"We are committed to ensuring Brighton and Hove is a fair and inclusive city, where discrimination, harassment, and misogyny are not tolerated.

"While we are proud of the work our staff do to support diversity and inclusion, we will take appropriate action if behaviour falls short of our values and expectations.”

Catcalling and other forms of 'intentional sex-based public harassment' has been illegal in England and Wales since April 1 this year. Anyone directing harassment at another person because of their sex in public places such as streets, parks, public transport, taxis, shops, and other places can face up to two years in jail.

News.title: Anthropic AI used fake profiles to target people in hack then hid the evidence
News.content:
Two of the world's most powerful AI tools created fake human profiles to try and trick people in attempted cyber-attacks, the UK's AI Security Institute (AISI) has revealed.

In the most serious case, Anthropic's Mythos AI tried to gain access to a service by sending private messages, having set up fake accounts mimicking real people - then hid the evidence.

It comes shortly after the two companies involved in the AISI testing - Anthropic and OpenAI - separately revealed in recent weeks instances of their tech hacking into other companies.

The firms said, in this latest case, the AISI's test had reduced or removed normal safeguards.

The AISI said on that Tuesday Mythos - and OpenAI's Sol - AI models had engaged in a level of "autonomy and deception" it had not seen before.

It clarified most of the malicious actions were carried out by Mythos.

AISI evaluators first noticed "unusual data transfers leaving our research systems" during a test, then found that "some of the agents being tested had engaged in sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organisations".

In the most serious case, a Mythos agent followed the routine of a human cyber-attacker by trying to trick people into giving it access to GitHub, a large platform where technology developers store software code.

The agent was trying to insert "malicious code" into GitHub's system.

It identified and researched the people who maintained GitHub and created a series of fake accounts based on those real people.

It sent messages and files through a file-sharing service as part of an effort to pressure and trick the people into approving its malicious code.

When challenged, "it edited its earlier activity to appear harmless and considered adopting a fresh identity to continue," AISI said.

Throughout the attempts, it was human review that stopped the agent from succeeding in delivering the malicious code to GitHub.

While AISI said the Mythos agent had not been instructed specifically to avoid or carry out such behaviour, it was "the first time we have seen risks around autonomy and deception manifest this clearly, without specific prompting, in the real-world".

The rival AI companies, which are poised to be listed on the public stock market, have been in the headlines in recent weeks after announcing their tools were responsible for several cyber-hacking incidents.

News.title: Ex-MP urges Tories to block council candidate jailed for antisemitic abuse against her
News.content:
A former Labour MP has said the Conservatives should not allow a former neo-Nazi who was jailed for antisemitic abuse against her to stand as a local election candidate.

Joshua Bonehill-Paine was convicted of racially harassing Luciana Berger, who is Jewish, in 2016, while already serving a separate jail sentence for sharing antisemitic posts.

Tory leader Kemi Badenoch has defended the decision to select him as a candidate in Somerset, saying that while his crimes were "appalling" he had been rehabilitated and was now "part of the fight against antisemetism".

But Baroness Berger said he should be barred from standing for public office - and Jewish groups have rejected a Tory invite to meet him.

Baroness Berger said Bonehill-Paine's harassment "affected my life in lots of different ways because of the volume of the material that he was disseminating and putting out, the extremity of it in terms of just frankly how shocking and awful it was".

The Labour peer added: "I think that we need to have a bar when it comes to standing for public office.

"I strongly believe that this individual today falls very, very short of that."

Bonehill-Paine spent three years in prison after he was jailed in 2015 for posting antisemitic material ahead of a planned neo-Nazi rally.

A year later in 2016, he was convicted of racially harassing then-Labour MP Berger, a former shadow cabinet minister who is now a member of the House of Lords.

Baroness Berger attended court at the OId Bailey in London to give evidence in the trial of Bonehill-Paine.

In a Substack article, Baroness Berger said Bonehill-Paine had shown "no contrition" throughout the trial and claimed that at one point "he performed a full Nazi salute to his supporters in the public gallery".

"It told me everything I needed to know about how this individual saw the world, and about the utter contempt he held for the people he targeted," Baroness Berger wrote.

In sentencing remarks, the judge said it was "difficult to envisage a worse case than this of racially aggravated harassment of this kind", adding Bonehill-Paine had "sat in the dock smirking throughout the trial" and had "plainly enjoyed" Baroness Berger's discomfort.

The judge said in that in an online article, Bonehill-Paine described Baroness Berger as "a very evil woman" and doctored photographs of her into "sexualised images".

Baroness Berger resigned from Labour in protest at the handling of antisemitism allegations in 2019, before rejoining in 2023 after receiving an apology from former party leader Sir Keir Starmer.

News.title: Police chief considers joining legal action over PC Harper killers' early release
News.content:
The driver of the vehicle, Henry Long, received a 16-year sentence and is not eligible for early release.

Speaking on the Today programme, Thames Valley Police chief Jason Hogg urged the government to reconsider its position.

Only prisoners convicted of murder, rape, grooming, and serious child sex offences will be excluded from the scheme in England and Wales - while those convicted of manslaughter remain eligible.

"I fully understand the challenges around the crisis in the prison system," he said.

"But the decision made and where that line has been drawn, I do not believe that people responsible for taking the life of another citizen in our country should be released early."

He said on Wednesday: "I was informed yesterday that the Police Federation are considering legal action, I am in discussions with the Police Federation with regards to this matter".

Asked whether this meant he would join them, he said: "I think we need to get some legal advice in relation to this. This is something I certainly would consider."

After campaigning by PC Harper's wife Lissie following his death, Parliament passed "Harper's Law", which gives mandatory life sentences to the killers of emergency services workers. It doubles the maximum penalty from 12 months to two years for those who assault police or other emergency workers.

But the new rules - introduced in 2022 - did not apply in the sentencing of the police officer's killers, and so do not prevent them from being released early.

Hogg said: "The law isn't retrospective and we all understand that, but the fact that they are released early simply seems perverse."

Aileen O'Connor, branch chair of Thames Valley Police Federation also told the BBC her organisation was considering legal action.

"We are in talks this morning, I'll get an update this afternoon whether that is an avenue that we can explore and if it is an avenue we can explore then I'll get behind that 110%," she told BBC Breakfast.

As for what shape a potential legal challenge might take, she said: "Ultimately that's for the specialists, the barristers and those in that legal sector to make that decision whether there is a challenge there.

"If there is a challenge then we will look to take that challenge."

Sentencing Minister Jake Richards told the BBC it would be wrong to pick out individual cases and block two of PC Harper's killers from early release.

Although the government had reviewed what sentences would be excluded from the early release scheme, he confirmed "manslaughter is not one of those offences".

Richards said: "It would be wrong to pick out individual cases within different offending cohorts. That wouldn't be right. It wouldn't be lawful either. So it is correct that those two individuals will be subject to the new regime from October".

Any legal challenge would have to be heard in the High Court - that is where ministerial decisions are reviewed.

Judges would have to be convinced that the government's choice of who gets out and who remains inside was either totally unlawful because they did not have the power to decide - or so irrational that it failed a legal test for reasonable decision-making.

Crucially, judges do not rule against a minister just because they do not like the choice they have made - there has to be a clear legal flaw in how they went about it.

On Tuesday Justice Secretary Alex Norris warned that a prison capacity crisis would be likely if fewer prisoners were allowed early release.

Norris apologised to families who would be affected by the early release scheme and stressed that the government wanted to go further "but we cannot".

"We have to make this decision, we've been able to make some changes to it, but we have to have the rest of the sentencing act changes otherwise we run out of prison places in November and that can't happen," he said.

News.title: Traitors star Joe Marler to become BBC's first celebrity Gladiator
News.content:
Former rugby star Joe Marler is to become the first ever celebrity Gladiator on the BBC's popular entertainment series.

The 36-year-old, who also took part in the first series of Celebrity Traitors, will be known as Mauler and face contenders when the fourth series of Gladiators begins in 2027.

"Mauler will see you now," Marler said in a video posted on Instagram, external announcing the news, recorded in the Gladiators dressing room.

The BBC said Marler will make his debut with a series of "special appearances packed with power, personality and plenty of surprises".

Filming for the fourth series is currently under way in Sheffield, the BBC confirmed in a statement.

"Known for his uncompromising style of play and larger-than-life sense of humour, Joe has built a reputation as one of the UK's most entertaining sporting personalities," the corporation said.

"Now, he's taking on an entirely new challenge as he joins the ranks of the Gladiators, bringing his trademark physicality and competitive spirit to one of television's toughest arenas."

The former England rugby international star, who is from Heathfield, Sussex, will join fellow Gladiators such as Nitro, Viper, Diamond and Sabre in batle when the show returns next year.

Gladiators was a hugely successful show on ITV in the 1990s, and saw members of the public take on a group of elite athletes who each had their own on-screen persona.

Olympic swimmer Sharron Davies, who like Marler was already known as a famous sports personality, joined that iteration of the show in 1995 as the character Amazon.

The format was revived by Sky for two series in 2008, before the current iteration launched in 2024, quickly becoming a hit for BBC One.

A celebrity spin-off is separately in the works, featuring contestants including presenter AJ Odudu, comedian Sara Pascoe, podcaster Chris Ramsey and social media star George Clarke.

News.content:
He added: "Since NX121's unanimous acquittal by an Old Bailey jury, and in the absence of any evidence that he failed in his duties, we have been clear and consistent in our view that he should not face a misconduct hearing."

The commissioner said the decision "must be a milestone moment" to reset the police accountability system.

"No police officer is above the law, but we have been clear the system holding police to account is broken," he said.

"Your life being on hold for four years or more as you go through multiple accountability processes is a disgraceful way to treat brave men and women. I also see the profound effect these cases routinely have on officers' families.

"Criminals are held to account once by the courts - officers can be held to account four times through criminal, misconduct, civil and inquest processes that span years. That cannot be right."

Amanda Rowe, IOPC director of engagement, said they had "always sought to avoid any unnecessary delays" in Blake's case, but said it was right proceedings were paused until the impact of new legislation was understood.

"Having considered both our policy and the representations from the Kaba family and Sgt Blake, we have today notified them of our decision to withdraw disciplinary proceedings," she said.

A coroner will now decide whether an inquest will take place into Kaba's death.

The IOPC's decision was criticised by the Justice for Chris Kaba Campaign and the charity Inquest, with both groups calling it a "blow" to Kaba's family.

Temi Mwale, from the Justice for Chris Kaba Campaign, said decision sent a "dangerous message", and Deborah Coles, from Inquest, said it signified that "police can act with impunity".

Paula Dodds, chairwoman of the Metropolitan Police Federation, said the IOPC had made "the right decision".

"Police officers are of course â and rightly â highly accountable for their actions. But the officer has sadly suffered years of legal scrutiny following this incident," she said.

"We are pleased this has all now concluded and that the officer can continue to serve the public without this hanging over him."

In a statement, City Hall Conservative Leader Susan Hall AM welcomed the news.

She said: "This disgraceful investigation should never have begun in the first place.

"The Mayor and the ideologically-captured IOPC are failing our police officers, not least our firearms officers, every day by refusing to provide the political and organisational support to the brave men and women who put themselves in harms way to keep us safe."

She said the officer had been "let down at every stage and heads must roll".
