News.title: The cost of being single – and how friends are teaming up to beat it
News.content:
When Leanne split up with her partner in her late 20s she thought she'd have to put her dream of a buying a home in the area where she grew up on hold.

She was earning a good salary but the properties she was hoping for - with a garden and parking space - were too expensive on her own. While she'd just started seeing someone new, it was very early days - far too early to discuss living together.

Her friend since school, Sarah, was single and renting a room in a shared house in Brighton. She also wanted to move back home to Kent, but was worried about how she'd get on the housing ladder on her cabin crew salary.

When Sarah suggested they buy together, Leanne admits she "totally baulked". But after chatting with a mortgage adviser they went ahead - and say it's helped them avoid the so-called singles tax.

Not being partnered up can mean extra costs. It's tricky to quantify and varies by location - estimates suggest it could be anything from hundreds of pounds to Â£10,000 on average extra, external a year.

The cost of rent or a mortgage, household bills and subscriptions can't be shared. And a single person pays 25% less council tax than a couple - not half.

Many discounts involve pairing up - 2-for-1 cinema tickets, Two-Together railcards, couples gym memberships - plus solo travellers often pay a single person supplement.

This affects a lot of people. Some 18.5m people had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2024 â 36.8% of the population aged 16 and over, official figures show.

And overall 8.6m people were estimated to be living alone in the UK last year - that's nearly a third of all households.

News.title: From flip flops to fisherman's sandals: How to look after your feet this summer
News.content:
Flip-flops have always been a popular solution to sweaty, uncomfortable feet in scorching weather - and now they've had a revamp.

The most stylish way to wear them this summer is with a kitten heel, according to fashion expert and trend forecaster Angela Baidoo.

"It's not a high heel and it's really kind of easy to just slip in and slip out of," she says.

However, heel or not, the flip-flop has earned itself a bad rap for lack of support and damaging our feet. Is that fair?

News.title: Woman arrested after four stabbed in central London
News.content:
A 47-year-old woman has been arrested after four men were stabbed in Covent Garden in central London, the Metropolitan Police said.

The men, aged 34, 39, 42 and 52, were taken to hospital after emergency services were called to reports of a stabbing in Endell Street at about 12:30 BST.

The force said two men remain in hospital with injuries not thought to be life threatening or life changing while the other two have been discharged.

The woman was arrested on suspicion of possession of an offensive weapon and assault. The Met said it was believed to have been a mental health-related incident and that a pair of scissors had been recovered at the scene.

News.title: Miliband says re-opening Strait of Hormuz 'essential' as he meets Rubio
News.content:
Re-opening the Strait of Hormuz is essential to bringing down the cost of living in the UK, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has said ahead of talks with US counterpart Marco Rubio.

The Labour minister is in Washington for his first official one-on-one meeting with Rubio.

The pair are also expected to discuss the war in Ukraine and the humanitarian crisis in Gaza.

Miliband was invited to the US capital by Rubio after they met on the sidelines of a foreign ministers' summit in the Philippines, where the former Labour leader made his debut as foreign secretary.

The White House was reported to be concerned about Prime Minister Andy Burnham's decision to hand Miliband the Foreign Office brief, given his previous criticism of US President Donald Trump as a racist and a misogynist.

Trump is also a trenchant opponent of wind farms and supports the opening up North Sea oil and use of fossil fuels, whereas in his former role as UK energy secretary, Miliband championed net zero and renewables.

Burnham has signalled a shift in north sea oil policy, earning praise from the Oval Office, but the dynamic between Miliband and Rubio will be closely watched.

Last month, Washington's top diplomat in London, Warren Stephens, said Miliband had been "wrong" in 2016 to call Trump "a racist, misogynistic self-confessed groper" and added "hopefully his views have changed".

Speaking ahead of the talks, Miliband said: "The government is committed to nurturing our strong, enduring and essential alliance with the US.

"I am greatly looking forward to my second meeting with secretary of state Marco Rubio, in which we will discuss the ongoing work to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and secure a lasting ceasefire, which is essential to ease cost-of-living pressures on British families."

The strategic sea route, which had been open before the US and Israel launched the war in February, has been a flashpoint in the Middle East conflict and disruption to trade has driven up fuel and food prices.

Miliband added: "We will also discuss how we can continue to stand shoulder to shoulder with Ukraine against Russia's war â as well as the importance of addressing the dire humanitarian situation in Gaza and working towards a lasting peace for Palestinians and Israelis."

In the face of erratic US support, the UK foreign secretary is set to stress that Ukraine's security is inseparable from European and transatlantic security and restate the UK's commitment to stand with Kyiv for as long as it takes.

Miliband will be taking the UK's seat on the World Bank board, so he will also meet its president Ajay Banga during his visit to discuss development, climate change and strengthening global resilience.

News.title: Gary Glitter appears in court over historical sex offence charges
News.content:
Gary Glitter, the former singer whose real name is Paul Gadd, has appeared in court charged with four historical sex offences dating back to 1978.

Gadd appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Wednesday via video link from prison to deny the charges. He was remanded in custody and told to appear on 2 September at the Old Bailey in London, either by video link or in person.

The charges relate to one count of unlawful sexual intercourse with a girl under the age of 13, and three counts of indecent assault on a girl under the age of 14.

There is one alleged victim, with the offences said to have taken place between the years of 1978-1981 at a residential address in Kensington.

Dressed in a blue shirt and wearing sunglasses, Glitter appeared by video link from His Majesty's Prison Channings Wood for the 11-minute hearing.

Under his real name, Gadd was told of the charges against him and spoke only to confirm his name and date of birth.

The prosecutor, Jonathan Polnay KC, told the court that Gadd said in a police interview he did not know the complainant, and that the allegations against him were false.

He also told the court that the offences involved one person, and are said to have taken place between the years of 1978 and 1981 when the complainant was eight to 11 years old.

He said she lived near where Glitter lived and that was how he came to know her. She says he gave her chocolate and that he invited her into his house where the offences occurred.

The allegations were first reported to the Metropolitan Police on 9 January 2025 and an investigation into the circumstances was launched.

Gadd was first interviewed on 22 July last year in relation to the investigation.

The 82-year-old was one of the biggest pop stars of the 1970s with a string of number one hits.

The Met said in July that the alleged victim was being supported by specialist officers and had been made aware that Glitter had been charged.

The singer is currently being held in HMP Channings Wood in Devon.

News.title: Restrict sale of pet flea treatments, government urged
News.content:
Pet flea treatments should be banned from general sale, a Lords committee has urged, after an inquiry raised concerns about their impact on their environment.

Spot-on treatments to prevent parasite infestations in fur and on skin are currently widely available for pet owners to buy in supermarkets and online.

But the House of Lords environment committee said their sale should be restricted, adding widespread use posed a potential threat to natural ecosystems.

The government said it was continuing to assess the availability of the treatments in order to ensure "correct usage by owners".

Currently, dog and cat owners are frequently advised to use preventative spot-on treatments every month to avoid parasite infestations.

But in a series of evidence sessions, the committee heard such blanket usage is not supported by robust scientific evidence and is likely to be harming the environment.

Many vets do not treat their own pets monthly, the committee heard, instead regularly checking their pets' fur with flea combs and restricting use to when fleas were spotted.

The committee heard that high volumes of fipronil and imidacloprid, common active ingredients in spot-on treatments, have been found in UK streams and rivers, killing off aquatic life, with a knock-on effect on wildlife higher up the food chain.

These chemicals have already been banned for use as agricultural pesticides because of their impact on wildlife such as bees, while the committee said "very little is known" about the impacts of newer chemicals such as isoxazolines.

In a report, external, the cross-party committee recommended that only vets, pharmacists and other qualified professionals should be able to sell such treatments, with pet owners advised to take a precautionary approach to using them.

News.title: Man gets third-degree burns from hot sand after using disposable beach BBQ
News.content:
Warning: This article contains a distressing image

A man who suffered third-degree burns from hot sand after using a disposable barbecue on a beach has warned others to be aware of the dangers.

Sam Knight had been using it on Cefn Sidan Beach, Carmarthenshire, with his family and stepped on sand that was still hot.

The 27-year-old had to be carried off the beach after suffering badly blistered feet and needed weeks of treatment.

Experts at a burns centre say injuries such as this are becoming increasingly common and warned beach goers to take precautions.

Knight told Radio Wales Breakfast he was not aware that sand could be a "real hazard".

He had used tongs to move the barbecue to one side and extinguished it, so he thought it was safe.

"When I returned to the area, I stepped on a boiling hot patch of sand, and had to be carried off the beach," he added.

Knight was taken to Neath Port Talbot Hospital referred to a burns specialist.

"I couldn't walk for a couple of weeks so I had to take a fortnight off work," he added.

David Fligelstone and Menna Davies are physiotherapists who work with the burns centre at Swansea Bay University Health Board.

Fligelstone said the number of incidents they are seeing is "going up year on year".

"The key thing is that people don't understand is that sand stays hot for such a long time after a barbecue is moved," he said.

"When you look at the evidence it's always the sand that hasn't been cooled that ends up causing that injury."

Davies said injuries like this can be "quite painful" and need to be dressed for a "long period of time".

News.title: Dewormer and scabies drugs being sold as cancer treatments, BBC investigation finds
News.content:
Animal dewormer and a drug used to treat scabies are being sold and promoted as unproven cancer treatments, a BBC investigation has found.

Following a tip off, an undercover journalist was able to buy fenbendazole and ivermectin from a stairlift salesman in south Wales, and also found them for sale on Amazon.

Macmillan Cancer Support said it was concerned by the findings and that a growing number of people were asking about the medicines, despite "no clinical evidence" that they work.

Amazon removed the products after we contacted them, and said it had "proactive measures in place" to stop prohibited products being listed by third-party sellers.

Senior doctors are worried vulnerable patients could be put at risk by taking the medicines, as they say it could harm or delay conventional treatment.

Six months ago, Rebecca Holder contacted the BBC after a visit from stairlift salesman Jason Sarver.

She said Sarver and her father Bob, who had a brain tumour, lung cancer and needed help with his mobility, had been discussing stairlifts when the salesman changed the topic to talk about the drugs.

News.title: Afghan boxer appears in court in connection with death of Scottish woman
News.content:
The man suspected of killing a Scottish aid worker in Greece has appeared in court in Athens.

The body of Elisabeth Ross was found in a suitcase at an abandoned building on 18 July, days after she had been reported missing.

Sharif Ahmadzai, who is 26 and from Afghanistan, was told during the private court hearing that he faces charges of homicide with intent, robbery and weapons offences.

He made no comment and the case was deferred until Thursday, when it is expected that Ahmadzai will be formally charged.

Homicide with intent is equivalent to a murder charge in Scots law.

Ahmadzai was driven to court in a grey Hyundai i30 with blacked out windows for the hearing.

News.title: Temperatures to drop briefly ahead of potential new UK heatwave
News.content:
Temperatures are set to drop across the UK over the next few days, ending the latest heatwave that has affected some areas of southern and eastern England.

Humidity levels will fall too, which should cool down homes and make nights more comfortable for sleeping.

The change in conditions follows another historic day in a summer that has seen many long standing heat records toppled or tied. On Tuesday, the UK registered its 34th day of temperatures reaching 30C (86F) or higher in a calendar year, equalling the record set in 1995.

Forecasts suggest that this record is likely to be beaten as early as next week, with some showing the potential for a sixth heatwave to develop.

News.title: Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal agree cut-price Bruno Guimaraes fee, Salah’s new club confirmed, Liverpool get Barcola boost
News.content:
Why Arsenal Want Bruno Guimaraes So Badly

Bruno Guimaraes has received permission to travel to Arsenal and complete his £75m move from Newcastle United. The 28-year-old midfielder will undergo a medical at the Premier League champions within the coming days after both clubs agreed a fee.

The deal represents a key piece of business of Mikel Arteta ahead of Arsenal’s title defence - while Newcastle will be left to wave goodbye to another key player following the departures of Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali this summer.

Brazil international Guimaraes told Newcastle earlier this summer that he wanted to join Arsenal and a cut-price deal for the Brazil international was swiftly reached following negotiations between the clubs this week.

Arsenal will now turn to continuing their pursuit of Guimaraes’ international team-mate Vinicius Jr, although Real Madrid are said to have offered fresh terms to the Brazilian after his return to training on Tuesday.

Manchester United want to sign a left-back, meanwhile, with Lewis Hall reportedly now set on a move to Old Trafford, but Newcastle are determined to stop the exodus and insist he is not for sale.

Liverpool want to sign Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain, meanwhile, and the European champions may have already landed his replacement: Maghnes Akliouche is set to join PSG from Monaco.

News.title: Space NK beauty advent calendar 2026: All the latest news, price and launch updates
News.content:
At £275, the Space NK beauty advent calendar is £15 more expensive than last year's edition, but the retailer says its contents will be worth more than £1,200 (£50 extra than 2025’s), which still leaves you with an extra £35 of savings up for grabs. With the full line-up still hush hush until 19 August, it's too early to say whether this price and worth increase will definitely result in a higher value product. But I’m expecting more premium brands, additional full-size products and perhaps some bigger-ticket beauty buys.

So far, Space NK has only teased a mix of "iconic hero products" and "exciting discovery brands." Looking at its recent brand onboardings, it’d be great to see the likes of Prequel and Takami featuring alongside established beauty favourites – and in-keeping with Parkinson’s ‘discovery brand’ suggestion.

The calendar itself has been given a festive makeover, with pastel pink and blue nutcracker-splashed packaging that's – according to Space NK – also more environmentally conscious. It's made from 100 per cent recyclable FSC-certified paper, printed using vegetable-based inks and designed to be reused or recycled after Christmas.

Whether you’re waiting for the full list of contents or dead set on securing the Space NK advent this December, you’ll want to join the waitlist sooner rather than later. Rather than giving everyone access at once, Space NK has declared that “the sooner you join, the earlier you can shop on preview day,” which implies that links to the live calendar will be sent based on when signees joined the waitlist. So, an earlier place in the queue could improve your chances of getting hold of one before it sells out. And, in my experience, it definitely will sell out.

News.title: Multiple people stabbed in Covent Garden
News.content:

A woman has been arrested after four people were stabbed in Covent Garden in central London today, police have said.

The Metropolitan Police said they were called to reports of stabbing at 12.27pm on Wednesday afternoon.

Four men, aged 34, 39, 42, and 52, were found with stab wounds and taken to a major trauma centre.

A 47-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of possession of an offensive weapon and assault, the force added. She was taken to custody where she remains.

It is understood the stabbing was a mental health-related incident and a pair of scissors were recovered at the scene.

A large police cordon was put up from High Holborn to the St Mungo’s homeless centre in Endell Street, where officers were speaking to people before they entered the building.

Matt Bishop, 42, who works at a consultancy firm next to the cordon, said he had seen a woman having a “stand-off” with three police officers and waving a weapon around.

He added that he did not see the stabbing but saw the woman, who “looked quite old, short hair”, running towards the crossroads.

open image in gallery London’s Air Ambulance landed in the middle of a busy Trafalgar Square to respond to the incident ( BBC )

He said: “There was a bit of a stand-off with three police officers.

“She didn’t seem to be particularly coherent. She was pretty incoherent in what she was shouting, the officer was asking what language she was shouting.”

Arjan Gjorga, who manages a fish and chip shop on Endell Street, said the victims were “random people who were just walking by”.

open image in gallery Emergency services near the scene on Endell Street in Covent Garden after four people were stabbed ( PA )

A London Ambulance Service spokesperson said: “We were called at 12:29pm today (5 August) to reports of a stabbing on Endell Street, WC2H.

“We sent an ambulance crew, paramedic in a fast response car and an incident response officer. We also dispatched London’s Air Ambulance.

“We treated four patients at the scene and took them all to a major trauma centre as a priority by road.”

open image in gallery Police remain in the area and surrounding areas in Covent Garden ( PA )

A Met Police spokesperson said: “At around 12:27hrs on Wednesday, 5 August, police were called to reports of stabbing on Endell Street, Covent Garden.

“Officers attended alongside the London Ambulance Service and London's Air Ambulance.

“Four men – aged 34, 39, 42, and 52 - were found with stab wounds and assessed at the scene by paramedics. They have since been taken to hospital and we await an update on their injuries.

“A 47-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of possession of an offensive weapon and assault. She was taken to custody where she remains.

“Police remain in the area, with a scene in place on Endell Street and the surrounding areas in Covent Garden.”

Police previously said that three people had been stabbed in the incident, but in a statement they later confirmed four people were found with stab wounds.

Anyone with information is asked to call police on 101 quoting CAD3449/05AUG.

Manchester United Women have announced the appointment of Eva Olid as their new head coach on an initial two-year deal with the option of a further year.

The move follows Marc Skinner’s departure by mutual consent earlier this week, after five years at the helm.

Olid arrives at the Women’s Super League club fresh from leading Heart of Midlothian to their historic first Scottish Women’s Premier League title triumph in May, marking a significant achievement in her coaching career.

Expressing her enthusiasm for the new role, the Spanish coach stated: "The opportunity to become head coach of Manchester United Women is a dream come true. The club has outstanding infrastructure and everything we need to achieve our ambitions. We have an excellent training facility, an academy that is already producing players capable of performing in a competitive first team and an exceptional group of support staff."

She continued, highlighting her focus on player development: "There is already so much talent within our squad and I am excited to work with the players to support them to fulfil their immense potential. I am joining Manchester United at a really exciting time. There is a clear alignment in our shared vision for long-term success. I cannot wait to begin preparing a team that will make our incredible supporters proud."

open image in gallery Marc Skinner left Man United earlier this week ( PA )

Manchester United hailed Olid’s arrival as the "start of an exciting new era," aligning with the club’s stated "clear vision for long-term, sustainable growth and success."

Skinner’s tenure saw the Red Devils finish fourth in the WSL last season and reach the Champions League quarter-finals, achievements the club acknowledged as building "important foundations."

Matt Johnson, United’s director of women’s football, lauded Olid’s qualities: "Eva is an outstanding coach with an incredible determination to succeed. Her remarkable achievements at Heart of Midlothian showcased her ability to maximise the potential of individual players whilst also implementing an exciting style of football. We are delighted that she will now bring those qualities to Manchester United. Eva is the perfect coach to lead us into an exciting new era."

Johnson further emphasised the alignment of Olid’s philosophy with the club’s long-term strategy: "She shares our commitment to developing exciting homegrown and young players, a tradition deeply embedded in our club’s history and culture, as well as improving established senior internationals, both of which form an integral part of our vision for long-term, sustainable success."

Olid’s first competitive match in charge will be the WSL season opener against London City Lionesses on 4 September.

News.title: Pictured: Girl, 9, who died after being found injured during family camping trip
News.content:

Read our Privacy notice

A nine-year-old girl who died after she was found seriously injured on an industrial estate in Arbroath has been identified.

Minnie Merriman, from West Yorkshire, was found just after midnight on Monday at the Elliot industrial estate in the Angus town while her family were camping in the area.

She was taken to Ninewells Hospital in Dundee, where she later died.

In a statement released via Police Scotland on Wednesday, her family said: “We are devastated with the loss of our beloved, absolutely incredible, beautiful and brave Minnie Moo.

“Our family asks that our privacy is respected at this extremely difficult time.”

Christopher Rice, 35, of Wakefield, West Yorkshire, was charged with murder when he appeared at Forfar Sheriff Court on Wednesday.

open image in gallery Minnie Merriman ( Police Scotland )

He did not enter a plea and was committed for further examination and remanded in custody.

Rice will appear in court again within the next eight days.

Police have said Minnie and the 35-year-old were known to each other.

Minnie is believed to have been camping in the area with her family, who police say are being supported by specialist officers.

Detective Inspector Mike Ness of Police Scotland’s major investigation team said: “Our thoughts remain with those affected by these events.

“A police presence will remain in the area while our inquiries continue.

“Anyone with any concerns, or information, should approach these officers or contact Police Scotland on 101, quoting incident number 0008 of Monday, August 3 2026.”

It is understood that West Yorkshire Police are supporting Police Scotland’s probe.

open image in gallery Police at the Elliot industrial estate in Arbroath ( PA )

At the industrial estate on Monday, a blue forensic tent was set up on a grassy verge outside Halliburton Arbroath manufacturing facility.

The area was taped off, with two police vehicles still at the scene and officers guarding the area.

A bouquet of flowers was placed on the grass near the police cordon.

Lois Speed, who is a councillor for Arbroath East and Lunan, posted on social media, saying the news was “heartbreaking”.

She later told reporters that she wished to “express the shock within the community this morning”.

Ms Speed said: “Really just my thoughts are with the little girl and her family, and those closely affected.

“I don’t have much more that I can add or say, other than just express the shock and sympathies with everyone.”

News.title: Inside Iran’s ‘deal on the side’ with Oman to open new route in Strait of Hormuz
News.content:

More than five months since Donald Trump and Israel launched their war on Iran, the US president is struggling to solve the biggest problem the conflict helped create: the militarisation of the Strait of Hormuz.

After a cycle of failed negotiations and military strikes, Washington and Tehran cannot agree on whether negotiations are taking place at all. All the while, continued attacks on ships in the waterway are deepening chaos in the global economy and increasing the price of energy.

“They are going on right now,” said Trump on Monday, hours after Tehran said that no such talks were happening.

Instead, Iranian officials have said they are negotiating specifically with Oman over Hormuz. The extent of US involvement in these talks is unclear, but experts tell The Independent Trump is likely to seize the credit for any impending deal either way.

“Oman will not act alone and independently. Whilst they hold the pen on this issue, they will be coordinating with other Gulf partners and the US,” said Dr Neil Quilliam, professor on the Middle East and North Africa programme at Chatham House.

The US, he says, may end up agreeing a settlement under which Iran is paid “service” fees which are disguised as environmental payments.

open image in gallery Vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, as seen from Musandam, Oman, on Monday ( Reuters )

While Trump would likely claim credit for a deal and sell it as a success for Washington, it would ultimately be an embarrassment. The White House has repeatedly rejected Tehran’s demand that ships pay a toll to cross through the Strait.

Optimism in Washington

There are growing signs that Washington will claim responsibility for a deal to open the Strait, after senior members of the Trump administration suggested it was days away.

“There’s been progress made in those talks [between Iran and Oman], but not finality yet. We’re hoping that will happen very shortly,” US secretary of state Rubio told reporters on Tuesday.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent also struck an optimistic tone, claiming a deal on reopening the Strait could be reached on Wednesday or Thursday.

“There is no trust between Iran and the US at present. Given that Iran and Oman are the two parties to managing Hormuz, it makes perfect sense for them to work through the issues,” says Dr Quilliam. “But Oman needs the backing of its regional partners and the US.”

open image in gallery US Secretary of State Marco Rubio (left) and US Secretary of Treasury Scott Bessent (right) have stated their optimism that a deal is close ( AFP/Getty )

Last week, Oman submitted a proposal to Iran envisaging regional management of the Strait and only voluntary fees for transit, rather than Tehran’s vision of maintaining control of the waterway and charging for its use.

The proposal was for a joint regional mechanism to manage the strait with voluntary fees to help fund the cost of managing navigation, environmental protection, search and rescue and other services.

But a look at Tehran’s latest demands casts some doubt over the US optimism of an imminent – and lasting – deal.

Tehran’s demands hinder deal progress

During talks with Oman, Tehran has put forward a proposal that would give Iran full control over all inbound shipping, a senior Iranian official told Reuters.

Outbound shipping would follow a route between Iran and Oman, with exit clearance granted through Oman after notifying Iran.

Tehran is “unlikely to change its position” from this, the source told the news agency.

But experts suggest this another sign that Iran wants to create leverage in peace talks – and such a demand would be unacceptable to Washington.

“The US will not accept any post-war arrangement that would actually give Tehran more control over shipping in the region,” says professor Basil Germond, a professor of international security at Lancaster University and an expert in maritime affairs.

open image in gallery The US president has struggled to bring the five month war to a lasting close ( AP )

Iran’s negotiations with Oman are the regime’s latest attempt to build relationships with regional countries and drive a wedge between them and the US, according to Maziyar Ghiabi, the director for the Centre of Persian And Iranian Studies at the University of Exeter.

“By building a long-term friendship and collaboration with Oman, Iran and its diplomatic team is trying to show that security and economic order will be beneficial to countries that engage with them at the expense of Washington,” he said.

‘US may accept Iran’s demand for fees to transit Hormuz’

Washington could, experts believe, agree to a deal negotiated between Iran and Oman.

A deal which could be acceptable to the US would be one which results in paid “service” fees being paid to Iran, under the guise of “environmental fees”, Dr Quilliam says.

This would ultimately be a win for Iran, who for months have been demanding a toll for passage through the Strait of Hormuz. For the US, it could only be seen as a concession.

open image in gallery Before the war, around one fifth of the world's oil flowed through the strait (PA Graphics) ( PA Graphics )

Trump’s central concern is getting Hormuz open again, Dr Quilliam says. “Even with ‘environmental service fees’ he will claim it is a victory, and add that he has destroyed Iran’s nuclear programme, its navy and its airforce and so on.

“He just needs the Gulf Arab states to sign up and live with the service fees. And given the alternative is a continuous war of attrition, this looks increasingly likely now,” he adds.

Prof Ghiabi says Trump, who has “attempted to play the role of kingmaker in diplomacy”, may see the ongoing negotiations as a way out from the quagmire in Iran.

“The US and much of the world need a steady flow of oil resources from that region, and we have reached the point where whatever arrangement guarantees that may be somehow reluctantly welcomed.”

News.title: Will you see the full solar eclipse? All the countries where it will be visible
News.content:

For the first time in more than 100 years, a total solar eclipse is coming to mainland Spain.

Throw in a crescendoing meteor shower and a six-planet parade on the same day, and stargazers will be treated to a view like no other.

Daytime darkness will descend August 12 across the Iberian Peninsula close to sunset — plus slivers of Greenland and Iceland — as the sun, moon and Earth align perfectly in the sky.

Starting near the North Pole before tracking south, totality will last up to two minutes and 18 seconds, an appetizer for an even longer solar show next year — a 6 and a half minute extravaganza that will sweep from Spain to North Africa and the Middle East.

open image in gallery The path of the total and partial solar eclipse on 12 August 2026. ( ESA )

It will take 1 and a half hours for the umbra, or moon’s sun-blocking shadow, to race along the 5,130-mile (8,260-kilometer) course, most of it over an empty Atlantic. Maximum totality will occur off Iceland’s west coast. By the time it reaches a small patch of Portugal and then Spain with its massive crowds, totality will have dwindled to a minute or so. The spectacle will end in the Mediterranean.

Eclipse chasers gear up for the solar spectacle

Hundreds of millions more on the sidelines are in for a treat as well.

A partial eclipse will delight as far away as Alaska and Siberia, enveloping Canada, the northern U.S., and much of Europe and West Africa.

The closer to totality’s course, the more the sun will vanish behind the moon – 94% coverage in Dublin and 83% in Oslo, Norway. Montreal will see an 18% bite out of the sun, tapering to 9% in New York and 2% in Norfolk, Virginia.

Special eclipse glasses are crucial. even if a morsel of sun is showing.

open image in gallery A woman is looking at the sun through a pair of special cardboard glasses designed to protect her eyes while watching the solar eclipse on August 12 in Saint-Pol-de-Leon, in the Finistere department of Brittany in western France, on August 1, 2026. ( AFP/Getty )

Adding to the cosmic wonder, the day begins with six of our neighboring planets forming an arc in the sky before dawn and end with the Perseid meteor shower peaking after nightfall under the new moon. Streaking meteors could photobomb totality, with some of the brighter planets and stars visible in the background.

Eclipse mapmaker Michael Zeiler is chasing an even more elusive interloper: the northern lights.

For his 13th total solar eclipse, Zeiler will be on a cruise ship in a Greenland fjord, sailing as a guest lecturer. He’ll point a video camera toward the north to capture any aurora forming during totality. A massive outburst from the sun would be the icing on his eclipse cake.

“What gets me excited is viewing rare phenomena,” Zeiler said in an email.

He’s not the only one revved up.

See who's hosting solar eclipse watch parties and science experiments

The European Space Agency will host a live webcast from Spain’s Astrophysical Observatory of Javalambre and a public celebration in Leon. NASA will provide its own coverage, as will the Italian-based Virtual Telescope Project and others.

“For me, it’s not just a scientific moment. It’s not just an incredible alignment of heavenly bodies. It’s also a very human moment,” said ESA’s director of science Carole Mundell. “It’s a real human connection between us with our feet planted on the Earth and the cosmos.”

open image in gallery This image provided by NASA and captured by the Artemis II crew from lunar orbit, April 6, 2026, shows the Moon eclipsing the Sun. ( NASA )

Two of ESA’s space telescopes will observe the eclipsed sun and its corona, or outer atmosphere. Proba-3, the space agency’s artificial eclipse-making satellite duo, will be in the wrong part of its orbit during totality as seen from Earth, but will try to sneak in some before-and-after shots.

U.S. college research teams are also pitching in, launching more than 60 high-altitude balloons from Spain and Iceland to study Earth’s atmosphere and other changes during the eclipse when the temperature momentarily drops. They launched 10 times as many balloons during the 2024 total solar eclipse that captivated North America.

“A couple of minutes isn’t a lot of time, but it’s still plenty to affect the atmosphere and to make that cold, dark shadow of the moon on Earth,” said Montana State University’s Angela Des Jardins, who leads the NASA-funded balloon project.

Southwest Research Institute’s Amir Caspi also expects a scientific bonanza from his study aboard a NASA high-altitude plane. Four cameras will record the corona in nine wavelengths as the jet chases the eclipse at 460 mph (740 kph), extending totality to nearly three minutes in the air. Caspi anticipates thousands of images gathered from each camera during those precious 180 seconds.

"It’s true the eclipse is short, but it’s still incredibly valuable," he said.

And there's more to come

An exceptionally long total solar eclipse is in store for 2027, yielding nearly three times more observation time.

The southern tip of Spain will take center stage on Aug. 2, 2027, with up to six minutes and 23 seconds of totality extending into Morocco, Algeria, Libya, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Yemen and Somalia.

open image in gallery In this image provided by NASA the Artemis II crew, counterclockwise from top left, Mission Specialist Christina Koch, Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen, Commander Reid Wiseman and Pilot Victor Glover pose with eclipse viewers during a lunar flyby on April 6, 2026. ( NASA )

Then on Jan. 26, 2028, a ring-of-fire eclipse will round out Spain’s celestial trifecta — “a lucky coincidence,” according to ESA’s Mundell.

It’s all the more extraordinary considering Spain’s last full solar eclipse — not counting the Canary Islands — occurred two days before the Titanic’s sinking in 1912. Because that rare hybrid eclipse toggled between a ring-of-fire and just a few seconds of totality for Spain, some consider 1905 for the country’s last pull-out-all-the-stops solar eclipse.

The Royal Observatory of Belgium’s Andrei Zhukov can’t get enough of them regardless of their length or origin. His Proba-3 science mission has created more than 60 simulated total solar eclipses over the past two years, with the longest lasting five hours and 38 minutes from two satellites flying in formation.

“We’re looking forward to more eclipses,” Zhukov said, “natural or artificial.”

Devotees of one Dannon flavored yogurt were in for a rude awakening when the flavor disappeared from grocery store shelves without warning earlier this year.

Dannon’s coffee yogurt, known to fans as “DCY,” gained a cult following over the years due to its 32 milligrams of caffeine — roughly a third of an 8-ounce cup of coffee — and sweet flavor that gives a mild sugar rush to start each day.

Doron Zeif consumed the creamy, caffeine-filled yogurt every morning for 40 years, and told The Wall Street Journal: “It’s what I got out of bed for.”

He wasn’t the only loyal fan devastated when shortages of the creamy yogurt started in February. Distraught DCY consumers turned to a Dannon Coffee Yogurt Fanatics page on Facebook to commiserate and plot to convince the company to change its mind. Reddit users have complained of going through “withdrawal symptoms,” and questioned if any substitute could even come close to the original.

“I’m seriously going through withdrawal! Other coffee yogurts are not the same. And making our own version, while healthier, would also not taste the same. I have been having this particular Dannon for literally decades, every day!” one Redditor wrote.

open image in gallery Fans of Dannon’s coffee yogurt have been left scrambling looking for alternatives — and begging the company to bring the flavor back — after it was suddenly discontinued earlier this year ( Dannon Coffee Yogurt Fanatics/Facebook )

A petition begging Dannon to reconsider had gained nearly 900 signatures as of Monday morning. However, Rafeal Acevedo, the president of Dannon’s yogurt division, said the decision was final.

“While we understand the disappointment some may feel, we hope our loyal coffee yogurt lovers enjoy the many other delicious and nutritious alternatives,” Acevedo said. The Independent has contacted Dannon for more information.

However Acevedo gave DCY fans some hope, hinting at a new twist on the beloved classic, according to the WSJ report.

“Dannon Coffee Yogurt will come back,” Acevedo said. “In ways that reflect the taste preferences, flavor profile and nutritional benefits many consumers seek in the yogurt aisle today.”

In the meantime, without their beloved coffee yogurt, DCY fans have gone to great lengths to either secure the few final containers of the creamy treat — or find ways to replicate it. Longtime fan Lisa Signorelli told the Journal that she bought entire cases of the yogurt from her local supermarket to feed her own “50-year obsession.”

“I’d wipe out everything on the supermarket shelf, whatever I could get my hands on,” she said.

open image in gallery ‘While we understand the disappointment some may feel, we hope our loyal coffee yogurt lovers enjoy the many other delicious and nutritious alternatives,’ Dannon said ( AFP/Getty )

While Dannon produces other yogurt in flavors like vanilla, blueberry and strawberry, DCY lovers aren’t interested. “It was the taste, but it was also the consistency,” Longtime fan Marc Hollid-Ausset told the newspaper.

“I’d eat one or two spoonfuls, and then add the toppings,” he said. “It was just the perfect yogurt.”

Fans on the Facebook page have started sharing their own DIY concoctions to try and mimic the special coffee yogurt’s flavor.

“Mix Trader Joe's Organic Plain Nonfat Yogurt with Trader Joe's Coffee Ice Cream. Adjust the ice cream amount to the sweetness you remember. Not exactly the same flavor but texture and sweetness is the same as DCY,” one wrote in the Facebook group.

Coffee yogurt addicts workshopped their recipes under another post, sharing various combinations of yogurt and cold brew powders — though some users noted they have not yet been able to match Dannon’s sweetness.

“Working on a substitute also using cold brew mix. Not getting it right on the sweetness though,” one fan wrote.

Another chimed in: “I make my own coffee yogurt too! I use instant coffee crystals and Torani sugar-free coffee syrup. They’ve discontinued it unfortunately, so looking for a good substitute.” Dannon has also declined to share their recipe with fans.

Others said that since Dannon discontinued their beloved yogurt, they were done with the brand. “I make my own too. I just don’t buy dannon yogurt anymore,” another member of the group added.

News.title: Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat
News.content:
Chelsea 0 Juventus 1

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

News.title: The underground lab where ‘princess mosquitoes’ are treated like royalty
News.content:
Beneath the grand Art Deco headquarters of the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine lies a vast labyrinth inhabited by weird and wonderful creatures.

In this maze of subterranean labs, store rooms and corridors live colonies of disease-bearing insects and arachnids from all over the world, from bed bugs, sand flies and microscopic dust mites to the so-called kissing bugs that spread Chagas disease – a sinister condition that can cause its victims to drop dead of heart failure without warning, albeit decades after the first (silent) infection.

Behind a series of doors, contained in stacks of mesh boxes, you can even find the flies that spread trachoma, the Dickensian eye disease that is still a leading cause of blindness around the world. But be warned: entering the room is not for the faint of heart – the flies feed on human excrement and the smell is impossible to forget.

There are also many varieties of mosquito, including several species of the Anopheles genus that spread malaria, Culex and Aedes mosquitoes that are also vectors for human and animal diseases, and even Toxorhynchites, perhaps better known as the elephant mosquito, a friendly giant which doesn’t bite people but preys on other mosquitoes.

These animals have been studied intensely since the insectaries were established in the building’s vaults in the 1960s, underpinning many breakthroughs in the control, surveillance, and understanding of vector-borne diseases in the developing world.

LSHTM researchers are now looking closer to home. They have established the UK’s first laboratory colony of Aedes vexans mosquitoes, a species native to the British isles, to study whether they could harbour diseases like West Nile virus, Rift Valley fever, Zika or Japanese encephalitis.

News.title: What I saw in a week on the front line of Afghanistan’s hunger crisis
News.content:
May 15 and 16, 2026

It is the weekend, a small moment to rest, although there is still a lot of work waiting for me. A week in the field does not mean that work in Kabul stops. I try to catch up on my emails and have a planned online interview for an international staff position – since in Europe, Friday is a normal working day. I also review parts of new proposals for donors and our financial planning.

On Saturday, however, I take a short break. Together with the base management team in Helmand, we visit a historical site called Qala-e-Bost, believed to have been built around 3,000 years ago. It is a rare moment to step away from work, followed by lunch with the team.

May 17, 2026

Sunday morning, the first working day of the week, we visit Basrhan Sub Health Centre, run by one of our local partners. As a nurse and former nurse trainer, I feel very much in my element in these health centres. It allows me to engage easily with the team and discuss their work.

I speak with the outreach officer and the vaccinator. They explain that this facility supports 18 outreach locations, each visited at least once a month. They provide vaccinations, raise awareness, and connect communities to the health centre. These visits often take place in simple settings, like mosques.

Immunisation is now well accepted. In the beginning, there was some resistance, but trust has grown over time. Every child is tracked, and if a child misses a vaccination, community health volunteers follow up at home. For extra polio vaccinations, this is carefully recorded by marking a finger of the child – helping ensure that no child is missed. The goal is clear: a polio-free Afghanistan.

I also speak with a mother. She is wearing a burka, so I cannot see her face. She tells me she is 22 years old and holds her 12-month-old son on her lap. She came because he has a fever, but I see a healthy child – something that stands out after my time in the TFU.

She brings her child regularly for follow-up and growth monitoring and the child has never been in a treatment program for malnutrition. She speaks positively about the services. “We are lucky,” she says. “The staff treat us well, and we have access to care in our community.”

News.title: World’s first seahorse hospital fights to protect them from extinction
News.content:
With careful precision, marine biologist Linda Albonetti extracts a 10cm-long injured seahorse – a heavily pregnant male – from an aquarium tank to apply healing ointment to its wound.

Linda, 29, coordinator at the world’s first specialist seahorse hospital, is currently caring for around 50 of these tiny creatures, all of which were brought in by local fishing crews after becoming snagged in their nets.

The seahorse will be kept for a few more days before it is released back into the Adriatic Sea, giving it time to recover from the cut to the soft, bony plates that form its outer carapace.

What the team here are doing is a literal drop in the ocean, a small attempt to fight back against the potential extinction of these remarkable fish.

In Europe and around countries like Indonesia, they are being poached in their millions for sale to a voracious Asian traditional medicine market where they are consumed as an aphrodisiac and alleged cure for impotence, asthma and kidney problems.

“There is definitely a downward trend in the overall seahorse population because they are being collected for the Asian market,” says Linda. “Technically, they cannot be exported to countries such as China, but there is no specific law preventing that trade. They do not have the same protections as sea turtles, for example.

“It is not happening in this part of Italy yet, but it is further south, off the Mediterranean coast. That is why it is so important that we monitor their numbers and maintain a good relationship with the local fishermen.”

News.title: The 13 best castle hotels in England
News.content:
Few places capture the imagination quite like a castle, and England is home to some of the most remarkable places to spend the night. If it’s not the romance of waking up in a canopied four-poster bed, or losing ourselves in centuries-old tapestries and visceral oil paintings, we are lured by tales of brave knights and plotting dignitaries, duplicitous royals and ghosts parleying secrets in the hallways.

Part of the magic is spending an afternoon wandering grounds and gardens followed by evenings in front of a roaring fire, or dining in a banquet hall that may have hosted medieval kings and queens. While not every castle has crenellated battlements, glistening moats or royal connections, each stony stronghold on our list has something special that makes it worth travelling for. In this modern age that might include a spa, fine-dining restaurant or extra touches like free admission to exhibitions and museum tours. Here’s our pick of the best castle hotels in England.

News.title: Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds
News.content:
Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Oil plummets as Trump calls off Iran strikes
News.content:
Oil prices have plunged after Donald Trump called off strikes and said the US and Iran would hold further peace talks.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, sank as much as 9.5pc early on Monday to less than $82 a barrel after the US president said he had halted plans for “disastrous” strikes.

Mr Trump said: “Obviously, they don’t want to be attacked. They knew the extent of the attack because they saw it forming.

“Now what we’re doing is we’re talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon.”

Mr ‌Trump also ordered oil companies to lower petrol prices for American ‌consumers ‌and criticised ⁠Chevron’s chief executive for not crediting his administration for supporting the fossil fuel industry.

The president said that he had been asked by Iran as well as US partners Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar to hold off on strikes. He halted plans for a major attack against Iran on Saturday, which he said would have been the biggest since the Second World War.

Mr Trump claimed the sides were on the “perimeter” of a peace deal.

Oil’s sharp fall also sent the cost of government borrowing lower on Monday over hopes that it would ease inflation.

The yield on 10-year UK gilts, a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money, dropped from 5.05pc to 4.98pc, while the equivalent US bonds dropped from 4.74pc to 4.69pc.

Stock markets in Europe also rose, with the FTSE 100 up 0.2pc, the Cac 40 in Paris up 0.3pc and the Dax in Frankfurt climbing 0.1pc.

News.title: Inside the trial for a vaccine to end malaria
News.content:
A small group of brave volunteers were given an experimental vaccine in Oxford this week in a bid to bring to an end the centuries-old scourge of malaria.

“I’m on my second vaccine now. Then I’m due to have my third vaccine soon, and then in November, I’ll be given malaria,” said an upbeat Mike Luciw, a 32-year-old local who works in recruitment.

“The hope is to help find something that could save millions of people.”

There are already two licenced vaccines for malaria but the new Oxford “RH5” shot is not like anything that has come before.

The existing jabs only act against malaria as it moves towards the liver in the early stage of infection, and provide only partial protection.

The new combination vaccine, in contrast, is designed to fight it off both at the liver stage and in the wider bloodstream, effectively knocking it out altogether.

The project is being run by the husband and wife team of Simon Draper, Professor of Vaccinology and Translational Medicine at the University of Oxford, and Professor Angela Minassian, an infectious disease specialist and clinical lead for their malaria programme in Oxford’s Department of Paediatrics.

“The dream for malaria … has been to have these two lines of defence, liver and blood, so if the first line fails, you’ve got a second,” says Prof Draper, who leads on the science.

“Our dream is to have a vaccine that gives over 90 per cent efficacy in African children,” adds Prof Minassian, who heads the clinical trials for the new jab.

Chelsea suffered the second defeat of their pre-season tour as Serie A side Juventus ran out 1-0 winners at the Kai Tak Stadium in Hong Kong. A second-half strike from Edon Zhegrova was enough for the Serie A side in a game that lacked any real quality - aside from the finish for the goal.

The Blues dominated possession, but Juventus had the better of the opportunities. The Italian side forced Robert Sanchez into a number of decent first-half saves before eventually finding the breakthrough in the second half.

Zhegrova curled in a brilliant effort from outside the box into the top corner, leaving substitute goalkeeper Mike Penders with no chance of saving it. Alonso's side beat Western Sydney Wanderers 6-4 before a 2-1 defeat to Tottenham Hotspur last week.

It's now back-to-back defeats for the Blues, with Mykhailo Mudryk making his long-awaited return during the match. Here are the player ratings from Hong Kong...

The goal came down his side and needed to be closer to Zhegrova for the Juventus opener

Offered less than Palestra going forward, but was solid defensively.

Olutayo Subuloye - 5 (65 for Fofana)

Needed to get out to Zhegrova quicker and close him down for the Juventus opener.

Sports.title: Vinicius Jr final transfer decision imminent as Arsenal players 'think deal is done'
Sports.content:
Vinicius Jr final transfer decision imminent as Arsenal players 'think deal is done'

Vinicius Jr to Arsenal is gathering serious momentum with the stance of Mikel Arteta's squad suggesting that a sensational move for the Real Madrid star is firmly on the cards

View 2 Images Arsenal's players think a deal for Vinicius Jr is at an advanced stage (Image: (Photo by Antonio Villalba/Real Madrid via Getty Images))

The Arsenal squad are of the belief that Vinicius Jr joining from Real Madrid is a 'done deal', according to reports in Spain.

‌



The Brazil international is of concrete interest to those at Emirates Stadium with decisive talks over his future in the Spanish capital taking place. A meeting between his agents and the club reportedly took place on Wednesday which suggests a final decision on his future is set to be made.

‌



As he only has 12 months left on his current deal, confidence is growing at Arsenal over what would be a sensational transfer. Sporting director Andrea Berta is working on the deal with the players already accepting it as more than likely he joins, according to AS, having also been convinced of a move to the Gunners by Mikel Arteta.

‌



How Arsenal could line up after signing Bruno Guimaraes and completing Vinicius Jr transfer READ MORE :

Their report states that the Arsenal boss has already spoken with Vinicius to explain what his role would be. Such conversations have filtered into the dressing room with Berta reportedly stating to players that the club are trying to secure what would likely be the most expensive Premier League signing ever.

The funds for such a seismic deal are seemingly available, however, with it specifically stated that there is a strong desire, perhaps more so than in Madrid, within Arsenal to finalise an agreement. There is a gap of €8million (£6.4m) per-year between what Real are willing to offer and what Vinicius wants in order to extend, even after reports of a fresh proposal being made.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Vinicius re-joined training with Los Blancos earlier this week following his mandatory three-week break after the World Cup with the plan for Wednesday being that he would train at 10am before a meeting with his agents and Real took place at 11am.

View 2 Images Arsenal have already finalised a deal for Vinicius Jr's fellow Brazilian Bruno Guimaraes

Exactly what was discussed or even agreed upon is unknown but the most recent updates certainly suggest it could be good news for Arsenal.

‌



While Arsenal players may believe the Vinicius Jr deal is done, Bruno Guimaraes' switch to the Premier League champions from Newcastle United has been finalised.

The 28-year-old is set to cost £75m and thus take Arsenal's spending into the triple-figures following Christos Tzolis and Piero Hincapie joining permanently. Illan Meslier was also signed as a free agent.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford primed for Ruben Amorim reunion after Man Utd transfer twist
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford primed for Ruben Amorim reunion after Man Utd transfer twist

Marcus Rashford has returned to Manchester United after his Barcelona loan ended and the forward could play against former boss Ruben Amorim later this month

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford and Ruben Amorim's issues at Man Utd were well documented (Image: Getty Images)

Marcus Rashford could be poised to make his long awaited Manchester United return against AC Milan - now managed by Ruben Amorim.

‌



The forward has not played for the Red Devils since the Portuguese boss was in charge. It was under Amorim that Rashford's struggles began as the pair clashed, which saw him twice head out on loan.

‌



Initially he moved to Aston Villa for the second half of the 24/25 campaign and then secured a switch to Barcelona, where he spent last season. The Spanish side opted against signing him permanently and Rashford has returned to Old Trafford with ambitions of becoming a regular again.

‌



If his return to United is in line with the club's other World Cup players, who have been afforded an extended break, then he is likely to be involved in next week's training camp in the Republic of Ireland. If so Rashford could find himself coming up against Amorim's Milan side with a friendly scheduled to take place on August 15.

Man Utd overhaul accelerates with another transfer agreed after booking medical READ MORE :

There is a chance that Rashford could appear against Leeds at Croke Park on 12 August, but if so that would come with just a couple of days training behind him.

Amorim was axed by the Old Trafford bosses in January and, at his unveiling at Milan, apologised for his dire time in charge of the club. His style never took off at United and within weeks of being appointed it became obvious that he and Rashford had an issue as he continued to snub the forward.

‌



When he eventually opened up on their divide he confessed: "I couldn't get Marcus to see the way you're supposed to play football and to train the way I see it. Sometimes you have one player that is really good with one coach, and the same player with another coach is different."

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford is due back for Man Utd pre-season once his post-World Cup break is over (Image: Getty)

The 28-year-old returns to Manchester off the back of a season that saw him score 11 times and come up with 14 assists as Barcelona won the La Liga title, the Spanish Super Cup and reached the last eight of the Champions League. Rashford still has a contract until 2028 and his weekly salary of £325,000 makes him the club's top earner.

‌



Rashford's biggest challenge will be forcing his way back into an attacking line that had £200million worth of talent added to it last summer. Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha and Benjamin Sesko all came in and were pivotal in the team's upturn in form, leading them to finish third.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino faces lengthy ban and disciplinary action as crisis meeting held today
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino faces lengthy ban and disciplinary action as crisis meeting held today

A crisis meeting has been called as pressure continues to mount on FIFA president Gianni Infantino

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino's future as FIFA president is under serious threat (Image: Getty)

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has summoned his top chiefs to a crunch crisis meeting today as he fights to save his job following the explosive fallout from his botched private equity deal. The embattled FIFA boss has called an emergency summit with senior leadership in Morocco in a desperate bid to shore up his position.

‌



It comes after he secretly hatched a highly controversial scheme to spin off the governing body's commercial operations into a new subsidiary called FIFA Forward Enterprise.

‌



The project aimed to sell a 20 per cent stake in the commercial and tournament rights of the World Cup to private investors. Although a fierce global backlash and threats of a massive boycott from UEFA forced Infantino into a humiliating climbdown to scrap the proposal last week, furious football leaders insist the damage is done.

‌



While Infantino uses today's crisis talks in Rabat to try and stabilise his reign and cling to power, an outraged European football establishment is at open war with him and exploring two distinct legal avenues to force him out.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Inside the murky world of FIFA lobbying as Jamie Carragher reveals World Cup request READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino calls FIFA crisis meeting in desperate attempt to cling to power READ MORE :

The first option being discussed is triggering an emergency vote of no confidence. Under official FIFA statutes, an extraordinary Congress can be called if requested by at least 20 per cent of member associations - equating to 43 of FIFA's 211 global members.

‌



View 2 Images Infantino has called a crisis meeting as he scrambles to save his job (Image: Getty Images)

With UEFA alone boasting 55 member associations, European football easily clears that threshold on its own to force a congress within three months.

However, actually ousting Infantino at the meeting would still require a simple majority of all 211 global members, where every nation holds a single vote regardless of size.

‌



The second option - and a far more explosive route to remove Infantino - is through formal disciplinary action. FIFA's independent Ethics Committee has the authority to investigate alleged breaches of the FIFA Code of Ethics and hand down severe sanctions, including lengthy bans from all football-related activities.

This is the exact mechanism that brought down former president Sepp Blatter in 2015. Whilst no official ethics investigation has been opened yet, a lengthy ban remains the ultimate nuclear option to force him out immediately.

If Infantino is ousted before his term ends, FIFA's Governance Regulations state the longest-serving vice president would take temporary charge until Congress elects a replacement.

The next official presidential election is scheduled for March 18, 2027, with nominations closing on November 18. Infantino had previously been expected to win by a landslide but after pushing the game to the brink, he may find today's crisis summit marks the beginning of the end.

Sports.title: Man Utd overhaul accelerates with another transfer agreed after booking medical
Sports.content:
Man Utd overhaul accelerates with another transfer agreed after booking medical

Manchester United are ready to sanction the exits of two goalkeepers in Altay Bayindir and Radek Vitek having signed two this summer to back up Senne Lammens

View 2 Images Altay Bayindir is set for a move to La Liga

Manchester United continue to overhaul their goalkeeping ranks with Altay Bayindir set to depart for Spain and Radek Vitek on the verge of a move to the Championship.

‌



The situation between the sticks at Old Trafford has kept changing over the past three years with Senne Lammens establishing himself as the club's new No 1 last term. Underneath him players have left in search of more minutes, which has ultimately led Bayindir to head overseas.

‌



The Turkish goalkeeper spent the majority of his time at Old Trafford as a back-up, starting just six times in the Premier League last term, and a deal has now been agreed with Celta Vigo.

‌



He will join on a season-long loan with his wages covered by the La Liga side. Celta Vigo have the option to make the move permanent for £3.5million and it is understood United have a high sell-on clause attached in the deal.

Vitek, the 22-year-old Czech who impressed last season at Bristol City, is on his way back to the second tier as he prepares to join Middlesbrough, subject to a medical, in deal worth up to £14m. United retain a buy back option as well as a sell on clause that, Sky Sports claim, is a hefty 35 percent.

To cover for those departures United have signed Karl Darlow from Leeds after he became available on a free. He played 24 times for the Whites last term as they retained Premier League status. United also bought in teenage goalkeeper Kit Margetson from Swansea at the end of July.

‌



The moves continue to see United's goalkeeping landscape change. Lammens came in this time last year as an unknown quantity from Royal Antwerp but within months of arriving was promoted to become the team's first choice, keeping eight clean sheets as United finished third.

View 2 Images Radek Vitek is closing in on a move to Middlesbrough

His rise came after Andre Onana's surprise departure. The Cameroonian had endured a difficult time in Manchester having arrived from Inter Milan with an impressive reputation, but he continued to make notable errors that cost the team. He was allowed to leave on loan for Trabzonspor, who paid his wages in full.

‌



He has since returned to the Super Lig outfit for another year. Onana was ultimately signed by Erik ten Hag to replace David de Gea, who was allowed to leave on a free after spending more than a decade as the team's undisputed No 1.

Sports.title: Mohamed Salah spotted in new shirt for first time as Liverpool icon mobbed after transfer
Sports.content:
Mohamed Salah spotted in new shirt for first time as Liverpool icon mobbed after transfer

Mohamed Salah is joining a new club after weeks of speculation over his future having left Liverpool this summer following nine years at the club

View 2 Images Liverpool icon Mohamed Salah has landed in Turkey ahead of a move to Trabzonspor (Image: Cemal Yurttas/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Mohamed Salah has arrived in Istanbul wearing Trabzonspor's shirt, having agreed to join the Turkish side after leaving Liverpool at the end of last season. The 34-year-old will pen a two-year deal, according to reports.

‌



The Egyptian had been heavily linked with a move to Saudi Arabia but clubs in Turkey also pushed hard for his signature. Talks with Besiktas over a transfer took place last month, only for the move to break down.

‌



But it's now Trabzonspor who have won the race for his signature, with the club announcing they were in transfer talks with Salah on Tuesday night and that he would arrive in Trabzon on Wednesday.

‌



Virgil van Dijk transfer lined up as club chiefs 'gutted' at missed Liverpool opportunity READ MORE :

Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola offer delay explained as PSG clear way with medical booked READ MORE :

They stated: "Professional footballer Mohamed Salah, with whom we have begun transfer negotiations, will be at Istanbul Atatürk Airport General Aviation Terminal at 12:00 on Wednesday, August 5. The player is scheduled to arrive in Trabzon on the same day in the evening hours.

"The time and other details regarding the welcome program in Trabzon will be shared with the public through our club’s official communication channels during the day."

Salah was greeted by several journalists outside of the airport as well as fans.

‌



Salah will link up with Manchester United goalkeeper Andre Onana, who has returned to the club on loan for a second season. Former Manchester City defender Stefan Savic is another ex‑Premier League player currently plying his trade with the Super Lig side.

View 2 Images Mohamed Salah pictured in a Trabzonspor shirt (Image: Cemal Yurttas/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Salah bid an emotional farewell when his plan to exit the Reds was announced in March. ""Liverpool is not just a football club, it's a passion, it's a history, it's a spirit," he said. "I can't explain in words to anyone not part of this club.

Article continues below

"We celebrated victory, we won the most important trophies and we fought together through the hardest time in our life.

"I want to thank everyone who was part of this club throughout my time here, especially the teammates past and present.

"And to the fans, I don't have enough words. The support you showed me through the best time of my career and you stood by me in the toughest times. It's something I will never forget and something I will take with me always."

Sports.title: How Arsenal could line up after signing Bruno Guimaraes and completing Vinicius Jr transfer
Sports.content:
How Arsenal could line up after signing Bruno Guimaraes and completing Vinicius Jr transfer

Arsenal are closing on their first major signing of the summer in Bruno Guimaraes whilst they're tracking Vinicius Junior's situation as the Premier League champions seek to add more quality

View 3 Images Bruno Guimaraes is set to swap Newcastle for Arsenal (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

Arsenal are closing in on the signing of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle as they look to land their biggest coup of the summer so far.

The Premier League champions are already favourites to defend their title and have gone after proven talent with the Brazilian set to move for £75million. It became clear weeks ago that Guimaraes wanted out of St James' Park and had cited Arsenal as his ideal destination.

Bolstering midfield was not necessarily a priority at the Emirates, but when a player of his quality became available a swoop was always on the cards. Declan Rice is the only guaranteed starter in the Arsenal midfield, leaving Mikel Arteta to fit pieces of the jigsaw around him.

Guimaraes has been the driving force behind Newcastle's rise - and the club were linked with him when he moved to England from Lyon back in 2022.

The 29-year-old will battle with the likes of Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi for a starting role, whilst Arsenal could equally look to play with a flat three, as opposed to two sitting and one playmaker. Zubimendi and Guimaraes have shown themselves more than capable of picking passes between the lines and stretching defences.

Arsenal set to agree blockbuster Bruno Guimaraes transfer as Newcastle demands finally met READ MORE :

One man who may well suffer a knock-on effect should Guimaraes head south is Martin Odegaard. Once the team's unchallenged playmaker, the Norwegian has seen more and more individuals join who can challenge him for his spot. He was injured for periods last term but he may not enjoy the untouchable status he once did.

Arsenal, in the wake of their Champions League final loss, where they were dominated from a footballing point of view, were urged to add more quality in the final third.

They could yet bring in one of the world's best as they continue to track Vinicius Junior's situation at Real Madrid. The winger is about to enter the final year of his contract at the Bernabeu and Los Blancos want to avoid losing him for nothing.

View 3 Images Vinicius Jr is locked in a contract standoff with Real Madrid (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Their negotiations centre on the player's image rights and where he sits in the financial pecking order. Vinicius wants to earn the same as Kylian Mbappe, Real's top earner, but the club are reluctant to do so - and Arsenal could yet swoop in as reports claim they would make him the Premier League's highest-ever earner.

That would see him pocket weekly wages that are north of £500,000-a-week. Such an investment would see Vinicius go straight in on Arsenal's left side with Bukayo Saka still the team's main man on the right, even if his form has dropped off over the last 12 months.

The central figure of their attack remains an issue, despite the £64m investment they made in Viktor Gyokeres last summer. The Swede scored 20 times in his debut season but question marks remain and he was ultimately left out for the Champions League final against PSG.

Kai Havertz, who scored that night in Budapest, was picked instead and whilst the German links play better than anyone in the Arsenal side, his lack of goals have been cited as an issue when compared to some of Europe's heavyweights. It leaves Arteta with a decision on who to back - or whether to dip back into the market.

View 3 Images Arsenal would likely have to shell out £200m in order to land Bruno Guimaraes and Vinicius Jnr

Arsenal's frontline is already heavily congested with Noni Madueke, Gabriel Martinelli, Eberechi Eze, new signing Christos Tzolis and academy graduate Ethan Nwaneri all eyeing minutes. The latter was forced to head out on loan last term after being continually overlooked.

Defensively Arsenal remain one of Europe's best - if not the best. Their world class centre-half pairing of Gabriel and William Saliba has been the cornerstone of their rise in recent years, although the Frenchman will spend a period on the sidelines, leaving someone to fill the void initially.

Piero Hincapie was signed permanently this summer and has impressed at left-back whilst Jurrien Timber, when fit, is perhaps the most versatile defender in the team and equally impressive at centre-half or on either flank.

David Raya, off the back of having to accept not being Spain's No 1, continues to prove himself as one of the world's best for Arsenal. The club have signed Illan Meslier to serve as a back-up option.
