Sports.title: Liverpool explore deal for PSG winger Mbaye
Sports.content:
Liverpool have explored the conditions of a deal for Paris Saint-Germain's teenage winger Ibrahim Mbaye.

The 18-year-old, who predominantly plays off the right, is believed to be interested in moving to Anfield.

The Senegal international is one of a number of targets Liverpool are looking at to strengthen in wide attacking areas, which is their priority in this transfer window.

Liverpool also have a strong interest in Mbaye's PSG team-mate Bradley Barcola, but are yet to make a formal offer for either player.

Their interest in Mbaye is completely independent of any potential move for Barcola.

It is possible that Liverpool could sign Mbaye and another more experienced option. As things stand, PSG's £145m valuation of Barcola makes that a difficult deal to do.

Liverpool are planning to have five wingers at the end of the window, with an additional one being a younger player they want to develop.

New Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola sees his wide men as being key to his philosophy, which is why this area of the squad is the big focus in his first window on Merseyside.

Youngest African to score at the World Cup

Sky Sports' Dev Trehan:

Mbaye, 18, primarily plays on the right wing, which is an area of the pitch that Liverpool have been looking to strengthen following the departure of club legend Mohamed Salah at the end of last season.

Victor Munoz has already arrived at Anfield this summer, while Liverpool have also shown interest in Mbaye's PSG team-mate Bradley Barcola.

Mbaye has come through the PSG youth system and made his debut in August 2024 as a 16-year-old.

Image: Mbaye scored against France at the 2026 FIFA World Cup

The teenager is a Senegal international, making his bow in November 2025, having previously represented France at youth level.

Mbaye made history at the 2026 World Cup when he became the youngest African to score in the tournament, aged 18 years and 143 days old, in Senegal's 3-1 loss to France.

Sports.title: Arsenal agree fee for Guimaraes
Sports.content:
Arsenal have agreed a £75m fee with Newcastle for their captain Bruno Guimaraes.

He has been given permission to travel for a medical.

Guimaraes told Newcastle bosses earlier this summer that he wanted to join Arsenal if a suitable offer arrived.

Arsenal's opening bid was rejected but the 28-year-old now looks set to join the Premier League champions.

Guimaraes, who joined the Magpies in 2022 from Lyon for £40m, has made 195 appearances for Newcastle, scoring 31 goals.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News takes a closer look at how Bruno Guimaraes stacks up against Arsenal's current midfield

Newcastle had been keen to ensure Guimaraes, who has two years left on his contract plus a club-held option for a third, remained at the club but if this deal goes through as expected, they will have made more than £240m from player sales this summer.

Anthony Gordon joined Barcelona in a £69.3m deal and Spurs signed Sandro Tonali for £100m, while manager Eddie Howe also departed in what has been a turbulent summer at St James' Park.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at Bruno Guimaraes' best league goals for Newcastle

Newcastle were desperate to keep Guimaraes

Sky Sports News reporter Keith Downie:

Newcastle were desperate to keep Bruno Guimaraes and if he had said he wanted to stay, Newcastle would have refused any offer from Arsenal or any other club.



Attempts to persuade Guimaraes otherwise were made and positive conversations were held, but he was insistent he wanted to leave because he felt this was his last big opportunity to win titles.



The deal could only go ahead if two things happened: Guimaraes said he wanted to leave (which he has respectfully) and Newcastle sold on their terms, similar to Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon.



Newcastle insisted it was their valuation or no deal. They would only sell Guimaraes at a fee that would become one of the highest paid for a player aged 28 or over.



In addition, a deal would only be sanctioned if the situation was handled properly - for example, Guimaraes attending Newcastle's training camp in Spain, which he reported to on Monday.

Newcastle feel Guimaraes has complied with their demands immaculately. They did not want a repeat of the Alexander Isak situation, where he refused to train before joining Liverpool last summer.



Agents were in between the clubs from the outset but Newcastle refused all pushes, which had began with mentions of a deal worth £40-£45m in June.

Newcastle were left frustrated because they felt Arsenal elongated the transfer by refusing to contact them for weeks.



Newcastle insist there have been no fall outs and good relations remain between player and club.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Catch up with the latest transfer stories from Sky Sports News including the news that Arsenal have a greed a fee with Newcastle for Bruno Guimaraes

'A statement signing for Arsenal'

Sky Sports' Oliver Yew:

This is a statement signing for Arsenal.

Guimaraes is one of the best midfielders in the Premier League, if not the world, and from a position of strength, Arsenal have taken him from Newcastle.

Midfield is already an area of the pitch where Arsenal are strong but Guimaraes' arrival is certainly an upgrade with Christian Norgaard set for a move to Everton. Myles Lewis-Skelly was playing incredibly well at the end of last season and started the Champions League final. Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino are World Cup winners and after some rest will be ready to go. There's Martin Odegaard and Eberechi Eze in the No 10 position alongside the two potential starters in Declan Rice and Guimaraes.

The Brazilian gives Arteta even more options and it also allows for the possibility for Declan Rice to get a breather in certain games after his exploits last season.

It's a world class midfield and if Arsenal weren't favourites for the title already, they are now.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jay Bothroyd thinks Bruno Guimaraes is an upgrade for Arsenal's midfield and will play alongside and fill in for Declan Rice

Question marks were being raised over the fee Newcastle wanted for a player that will be 29 in November but the deal has been done nowhere near the reported £100m fee that was wanted. At the start of the transfer window, you'd have probably said this is a fair fee but with the last few weeks we've had in the window with big money spent on midfielders Elliot Anderson and Morgan Rogers, anything under £100m looks good value.

Guimaraes is a little older but this is Arsenal's strategy, they want to win now. They have signed some younger players but last summer's deal to sign Viktor Gyokeres was to win now. He won't need any time to settle in. He is one of the most consistent Premier League midfielders.

Arsenal won't necessarily make money on him in the future but his arrival might get them closer to winning a first Champions League and he might help them retain the Premier League.

If they can add a left winger and some star quality in that position, which looks like the last piece of the puzzle, it looks like bad news for their title rivals.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jay Bothroyd says Declan Rice and Bruno Guimaraes would be the best partnership in the Premier League

It is easy to understand Arsenal's interest in Guimaraes.

The Newcastle captain is one of the Premier League's most complete midfielders, capable of dominating and destroying but also scoring and creating, with passing ability to match his physicality.

If the Gunners do secure his signature, he would be joining a group of midfielders which includes Declan Rice, Martin Zubimendi, Martin Odegaard, Mikel Merino and Myles Lewis-Skelly. So where and how would he fit in?

Sports.title: Yokota targets 'special memories' as he seals Rangers move
Sports.content:
Rangers have completed the signing of winger Daisuke Yokota from Hannover 96.

The 26-year-old has moved to Ibrox for an initial fee of £2.75m plus add-ons, and has signed a three-year deal, with the option of an additional 12 months.

Yokota - who scored five goals and provided four assists in Germany's second division last season - could be included in Rangers' Europa League squad as they prepare to face Jagiellonia Białystok in the first leg of their third-round qualifier on Thursday.

He is Rangers' ninth summer signing, following Ivor Pandur, Vanja Dragojevic, Olwethu Makhanya, Ross McCrorie, Dan Neil, Lawrence Shankland, Cammy Devlin and Ben Godfrey.

Speaking after signing for the club, Yokota said: "I'm really excited to be joining Rangers. This is a massive club with a fantastic history, passionate supporters and high ambitions, so it's a proud moment for me.

"My aim is to help the team achieve success this season, and I hope we can create some special memories together. I'm looking forward to meeting my teammates, the staff and getting started."

Yokota's journey to Ibrox

Image: Yokota scored five goals and provided four assists last season

Starting his career in Tokyo, Yokota moved to Germany when he was 18 years old, first joining the academy of FSV Frankfurt and then FC Carl Zeiss Jena.

In 2021, he signed for Latvian club Valmiera and helped them win their first ever championship title in 2022 with eight goals and 10 assists that season.

Yokota spent a season in Poland with Górnik Zabrze before he joined Gent in 2024. He went on to have a successful loan spell at Hannover 96, before the deal was made permanent last season.

Manager Derek McInnes added: "We are really pleased to bring Daisuke to the club. He is a player we have been aware of for some time, and he brings qualities that we believe will really strengthen our attacking options.

"At 26, he has gained valuable experience across a number of different leagues in Europe. He is quick, direct and has the ability to make things happen in the final third.

"We are continuing to strengthen the squad in key areas, and I am looking forward to welcoming Daisuke to Rangers and working with him."

Sports.title: Alcaraz withdraws from Cincinnati Open
Sports.content:
Carlos Alcaraz has withdrawn from the Cincinnati Open due to an ongoing wrist injury, increasing worries over his US Open title defence, which begins on August 30, live on Sky Sports.

"We ⁠know Carlos is doing everything he can to get back to playing tournaments as soon ‌as possible," Cincinnati Open tournament director Bob Moran said.

Sports.title: Chelsea set to clinch deal to sign Rayo Vallecano left-back Chavarria
Sports.content:
Chelsea are set to clinch a deal to sign Rayo Vallecano left-back Pep Chavarria for a fee of around £16.3m (€19m) plus add-ons.

Both clubs are finalising the last details of the transfer. Negotiations between the two clubs have been ongoing for more than a month, with Chelsea identifying Chavarria as the replacement for Marc Cucurella following his move to Real Madrid.

At 28, Chavarría offers the experience Chelsea have been looking to add to their youthful squad this summer.

Image: Radar comparing Chelsea's Marc Cucurella and Rayo Vallecano's Pep Chavarria in the 2025/26 season

The full-back featured in 44 games in all competitions for Rayo Vallecano last season.

Chavarria started for Rayo Vallecano in last season's Conference League final, where they suffered a 1-0 defeat to Crystal Palace.

Rising up with Rayo Vallecano

Analysis by Sky Sports' Adam Bate:

It is perhaps telling that Andoni Iraola was in charge at Rayo when Chavarria was brought to the club in 2022. He is a coach who values players who can bring real intensity to a team's performance. Iraola loves his full-backs to overlap and Chavarria can do that.

He has since shown that he can do more than just get up and down the flank, becoming more comfortable underlapping or stepping into midfield, adding elements to his game. But that reputation as one of the hardest-working full-backs in LaLiga is what underpins it all.

Image: Chavarria competing with Lamine Yamal

Inigo Perez has helped bring more from Chavarria during their three seasons together at Rayo. The player naturally describes him as the best coach that he has worked with, allowing him to flourish as a modern full-back involved in all aspects of the team's play.

Stats that show what he can do

Analysis by Sky Sports' Adam Bate:

Chavarria was a key outlet for Rayo Vallecano last season, having over 2000 touches in LaLiga and supplying a stream of crosses from the wing.

Image: Crystal Palace's Daniel Munoz (left) and Rayo Vallecano's Pep Chavarria battle for the ball during the UEFA Conference League Final

Chavarria ranked among the top dozen players in the competition for crosses from open play and corners won. But it was a dual role for Rayo because he was also among the top dozen players for blocking crosses and winning possession in the defensive third.

Are we talking about a player with a wand of a left foot who can be Chelsea's creator in the way that Alex Grimaldo was for Xabi Alonso's Bayer Leverkusen out on the left? Probably not. But as a willing runner who stretches the play, his could still be an important role.

Sports.title: Silca Bay and Sea Suite face off as Brighton Festival begins
Sports.content:
Slica Bay, Sea Suite and Ben Nevis line up for the Brighton Mile this afternoon, live on Sky Sports Racing.

3.30 Brighton - Silca Bay and Sea Suite fancied for Brighton Mile

Silca Bay and Sea Suite feature among a field of nine for the Sapporo Japanese Premium Lager Brighton Mile Challenge Handicap on the opening day of the Festival of Racing at Brighton.

Silca Bay arrives on the back of a narrow Newmarket success last month and should improve having scored with more than the winning margin would suggest. His trainer Eve Johnson Houghton has landed the past two renewals too.

Sea Suite, twice a winner this year, has finished runner-up on his previous two starts and could continue to hold his form despite another 4lb rise in the weights. Ceren Fallon regains the ride for James Owen, whose team is on an upward trajectory at present.

Glen Nevis drops in grade, while course and distance victor Play Me warrants respect for Jim Boyle and Donagh Murphy. Having had a wind operation following two disappointing efforts since switching to Oli Rix, Here I Bow goes for top honours off a mark of 80.

6.40 Yarmouth - Dubai Charm and Dowman contest trappy nursery

Dubai Charm and Dowman contest a trappy edition of this Strawberry Fields Stud Nursery Handicap at Yarmouth.

Top weight Dubai Charm represents Richard Hughes and Neil Callan and looks to hold excellent claims. A dominant winner at this track and trip twenty-eight days ago, she looks capable of stepping up on that form and this daughter of Blackbeard might be tough to beat.

Dowman finished strongly when opening his account over this trip at Windsor back in June and has his first start having undergone a gelding operation. An opening mark of 73 looks fair and he can go well under Billy Loughnane, who is chasing winners as he attempts to land the jockeys' championship for the first time.

Beauty Box makes her handicap debut with a hood added, while Wait Geordie ran with credit in the Super Sprint Stakes at Newbury and cannot be ruled out.

6.10 Yarmouth - Lady Of Hay and Speed Of Sound headline

Lady Of Hay and Speed Of Sound headline ten runners for a competitive British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes at 6.10pm.

Richard Spencer's Speed Of Sound has run two cracking races in defeat, finishing a close third on debut at Newmarket before chasing home Sorrengail in a warm event at Ascot. That form should be good enough to win a race, and he will be popular under Saffie Osborne.

Lady Of Hay made a pleasing debut when sixth at Newbury on racecourse debut last month and her trainer Andrew Balding reaches for a hood. A half-sister to the useful Anna Swan, she should be sharper for that initial experience and rates a big danger.

Babzini and Minkaas complete the shortlist, with the latter hampered when going well on her first start for TJ Kent last time out.

Best of the rest

Back at Brighton, recent winners It's Life and Buckland Belle clash in the Monty Bennetts 18th Birthday Handicap (4pm) before attention shifts Stateside to the Saratoga's Grade 1 A. P. Smithwick Memorial Handicap Hurdle (6.10pm). Fil Dor and McTigue line up here, alongside Roja Redemption.

Sports.title: Draper in tears amid injury concern during defeat in Montreal
Sports.content:
Jack Draper was left in tears after losing to Terence Atmane as the Brit's long-term arm injury appeared to resurface and hamper him on his return to action at the Canadian Open.

Playing in just his sixth tournament of the year, and a first since pulling out of Wimbledon, Draper was beaten 6-3 2-6 6-2 by France's Atmane.

After a rusty start, Draper appeared to have found form as he dominated the second set, but his performance suddenly dropped off in the decider as the power in his serves and groundstrokes reduced massively.

When trailing 4-1, Draper sat down and spent the entire changeover crying, apparently uncontrollably.

The 24-year-old carried on and almost claimed a break before spiritedly holding serve one more time, before Atmane closed out victory in an hour and 52 minutes.

Draper had established himself as one of the biggest challengers to Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner's dominance of the men's game as he moved up to a career high No 4 ranking in June 2025.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the first round match at the Canadian Open between Terence Atmane and Jack Draper.

It was around that time that Draper began suffering from a bone bruise in his left arm, an injury that has continued to hamper him ever since.

In 2026, he put together runs to the quarter-finals at Indian Wells in March and the semi-finals at Eastbourne in June, but has been unable to stay on the court consistently.

Sir Andy Murray has been part of Draper's coaching team since May, but Montreal was just the second tournament he has been able to play in during their partnership.

Draper has a wild card into next week's Cincinnati Open, but his defeat in Montreal is likely to raise fresh doubts over his participation there and at the US Open.

Sports.title: ‘Dream come true’: Eva Olid delighted after being named Manchester United’s new head coach
Sports.content:
Eva Olid has described being appointed as the Manchester United Women head coach as a dream come true, after signing a two-year contract until 2028 with the option of a further year.

The Spanish coach will replace Marc Skinner, whose surprise departure was announced on Monday morning.

Olid had been out of work since guiding Hearts to their first Scottish Women’s Premier League title last season and leaving the Edinburgh club by mutual agreement, after a five-year spell during which she oversaw a remarkable period of progress.

The 40-year-old’s arrival comes as United are understood to be prioritising developing their own young, homegrown players rather than spending large transfer fees. In a statement the club said: “Olid’s appointment marks the start of an exciting new era for Manchester United Women as the club embarks on a clear vision for long-term, sustainable growth and success.

“Important foundations have already been put in place to further support the development of homegrown talent and young players, as well as senior internationals, and establish a clear football identity. Significant investment has been made into the academy infrastructure and facilities, underlining the ambition to build the leading youth development system in the country.”

Olid told the club’s website: “The opportunity to become head coach of Manchester United Women is a dream come true. The club has outstanding infrastructure and everything we need to achieve our ambitions. We have an excellent training facility, an academy that is already producing players capable of performing in a competitive first team, and an exceptional group of support staff.

View image in fullscreen Eva Olid signs up for Manchester United. Photograph: Manchester United/Getty Images

“There is already so much talent within our squad and I am excited to work with the players to support them to fulfil their immense potential. I am joining Manchester United at a really exciting time. There is a clear alignment in our shared vision for long-term success. I cannot wait to begin preparing a team that will make our incredible supporters proud.”

United finished fourth in the Women’s Super League last season and reached the quarter-finals of the Women’s Champions League, as well as the League Cup final.

Matt Johnson, United’s director of women’s football, said: “Eva is an outstanding coach with an incredible determination to succeed. Her remarkable achievements at Heart of Midlothian showcased her ability to maximise the potential of individual players, whilst also implementing an exciting style of football.

“Eva is the perfect coach to lead us into an exciting new era. She shares our commitment to developing exciting homegrown and young players, a tradition deeply embedded in our club’s history and culture, as well as improving established senior internationals, both of which form an integral part of our vision for long-term, sustainable success.”

Sports.title: ‘Trabzon, are you ⁠ready?’: Mohamed Salah lands in Turkey to sign for Trabzonspor
Sports.content:
Mohamed Salah arrived smiling at an Istanbul airport on Wednesday wearing Trabzonspor’s burgundy and blue kit ahead of ⁠his expected move to ⁠the Turkish Super Lig ​side, as hundreds of fans jostled for a glimpse of the Egyptian forward.

Trabzonspor announced on Tuesday they were in negotiations with ⁠Salah and the club chairman, Ertugrul Dogan, said they expected to sign the 34-year-old on a free transfer at a ceremony in the Black Sea city on Thursday.

“Trabzon, are you ⁠ready? I can hear you. See you very soon,” Salah said in a video posted by the club ​on X. “Everywhere is Trabzon to us,” he added ‌while wearing a Trabzonspor kit, referring ‌to the club’s motto.

Upon arriving at Ataturk Airport, Salah was met by hundreds of fans. He waved ‌at supporters and initiated a traditional chant with them, before departing for a medical check and a later planned flight east to Trabzon.

Salah left Liverpool this summer after nine ‌years, having scored 257 goals in 442 appearances, where he won the Premier League twice and the Champions League once.

In the 2024-25 season Salah scored 29 Premier League goals and provided 18 assists, equalling the league record for most goal involvements in a season and setting the record for a 38-game campaign. He was named Premier League Player ‌of the Season and won the Golden Boot and the Playmaker Award, becoming the first player to take all three in one campaign.

His output ​waned last season, with seven goals and seven assists in 27 league matches and he was left on the bench in Champions League games, leading to a public spat with Liverpool’s then-manager Arne Slot.

The 34-year-old began his career in Europe at Swiss side Basel in 2012 and ⁠later joined Chelsea. He also had brief stints at Fiorentina and Roma between 2015 and 2017 ​before joining Liverpool.

Trabzonspor – generally ​considered to be the fourth-biggest team in Turkey after Istanbul ​sides Fenerbahce, Galatasaray, and ‌Besiktas – finished third ​in the Super Lig ​last season and will enter the Europa League playoffs.

Salah had been close to joining the Istanbul club Besiktas, whose football director Onder Ozen said negotiations had stalled over financial and image-rights demands, according to local media.

Sports.title: ‘Punch to the gut’: Indian football thrown into chaos with Jamshedpur withdrawal from ISL | John Duerden
Sports.content:
“Please don’t let this be the final whistle for Jamshedpur FC,” the defender Pratik Chaudhari said, looking into the camera as teammates looked on disconsolately. “We would like to say on behalf of all the players, please do rethink about this. Because if this happens, this is not just a loss for Indian football … this is a big loss for all of India.”

In addition, fans of the Indian Super League club marched in protest, petitions were launched, and the Indian football legend Sunil Chhetri said it was a “punch to the gut” and joined others in begging for a rethink.

The target of all these pleas was the Jamshedpur owner Tata Steel, which surprisingly pulled the plug on the club on 31 July. After the problems of the 2025-26 campaign, which started five months late and lasted just 13 games, the new season’s big kick-off on 4 September was to be a new start. The positivity and optimism before the new season, fragile though it was, disappeared along with JFC.

And understandably so as it is a huge blow, for players, staff and fans but also for the league. Jamshedpur had solid support and won the ISL shield in 2022, five years after the club was formed. Steve Coppell was the first head coach with Scott Cooper, Aidy Boothroyd and Owen Coyle all following in his footsteps.

Baljit Singh of Inventive Sports was the agent who took Coppell to the city in the eastern state of Jharkhand. “To be quite frank, after all the uncertainty Indian football has faced over the last couple of seasons, Jamshedpur FC would have been one of the last clubs I expected to pull out,” he told the Guardian.

The club was founded by the Tata Group, which has been involved with Indian football at various levels for decades. “When an institution with that history decides it can no longer continue at the highest level, it says something very serious about the current state of the game,” Singh said.

The league is also losing a major corporate backer, one which insists, however, that the decision is not about money. “At Tata Steel, sports have never been evaluated through a profit-and-loss lens,” the company’s vice-president and the club’s chairman, Sundara Ramam, told the Guardian.

View image in fullscreen Jamshedpur FC won the Indian Super League shield in 2022 Photograph: Courtesy of ISL

“Our decision to exit professional club football has nothing to do with Tata Steel’s financial position. In fact, the resources that would have been spent on the club will continue to be invested in grassroots sports development. Our sports budget is not decreasing. It will continue to grow. As chairman of Jamshedpur FC, I can say clearly that this decision was driven by our desire to focus more intensely on grassroots development and not by financial considerations.”

Yet if others follow suit then there may not be much of a professional pathway for young talent. This latest episode shines a light on the league once more. In the club’s original letter sent to the All India Football Federation, concerns were expressed about the financial model of the ISL, which recently changed. Reliance Industries was the federation’s commercial partner from 2010 but, when that agreement expired in 2025, a new deal was not made and a new partner not found, hence the shortened season.

This time, the FA looks after governance and administration with the clubs taking on the commercial and marketing side. “The old model meant clubs had very little say in how the league was packaged and sold,” Ravi Puskur, the chief executive of Goa FC, said last month.

“Now the clubs hold the broadcast and sponsorship rights directly. It puts the incentive to grow the league’s commercial value in the hands of the people who are most invested in it growing.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

A member of Jamshedpur’s staff told the Guardian that the decision was because of concerns over the new arrangements. “I believe Tata are not interested in the club-led model,” he says. “There had to be a commitment of four years and the AIFF was asking for an initial payment of around £43,000 from all 14 clubs to be made by 31 July. Tata might have thought it’s better to stop rather than get dragged into unknown waters.”

View image in fullscreen The former Crystal Palace manager Steve Coppell was the club’s first head coach in 2017. Photograph: The India Today Group/Getty Images

It is a worrying exit as this is not the only corporate departure from Indian football of late. “Reliance stepping away from its central role was significant,” Singh says. “City Football Group leaving Mumbai City was another warning.” That happened in December, in the middle of the problems last season. “Tata now withdrawing from Jamshedpur FC feels different again because of the group’s deep-rooted history in Indian football. These departures have happened for different reasons, but collectively they represent a major loss of confidence in the professional game.”

Now there is fear that others may follow and there will be some relief if all 13 remaining clubs kick off the season. “Indian football can recover, but we should not underestimate the scale of the challenge,” Singh says.

“The priority now must be the people affected, followed by urgent clarity over the league’s structure and future. Players, staff and supporters cannot continue living from one period of uncertainty to the next. They deserve much better.”

There is still hope that Tata could have a rethink. “I understand that some tough decisions in sport are down to what makes sense in the boardroom,” Chhetri said. “But I can only request and hope that the thinktank at Tata picks their heart over head and reconsiders this call. It might be a poor business decision, but it will be the one Indian football needs the most at this hour.”

Sports.title: Continuity, chaos and Rodman: how Washington Spirit are thriving in NWSL
Sports.content:
The National Women’s Soccer League is just past the midway point of its 14th regular season, with 12 of 30 games remaining in the regular season (though half the league’s teams have one or more games in hand).

Despite a number of developments in 2026 – including two new expansion teams and the Utah Royals on a historic tear – some things have stayed consistent. At the moment, that includes a third consecutive season featuring the Washington Spirit as a top-two team. With the business end of the season looming, the mark of success is twofold: maintain that consistency through the end-of-year melee and into the playoffs (easier said than done) and, importantly for the Spirit, level up with a first-place finish in the table and/or a Championship trophy.

Continuity at the top doesn’t come easy in a league such as the NWSL. Over the years, the league has earned its reputation as a parity-based competition where – whether it be a weekend upset between teams at either end of the table, or a “worst-to-first” scenario from one season to the next – anything can happen. Teams have had years-long runs of dominant results. Most notably, the North Carolina Courage finished the regular season in first place for three consecutive seasons from 2017 to 2019, while also winning the NWSL Championship twice in that time. But over the course of 14 seasons the NWSL table has been famous for fluctuations.

Some early new trends have emerged in recent seasons. Teams such as Gotham, San Diego, Kansas City, Orlando and Washington have had a steady presence in the playoff spots (notable by NWSL standards), but their places in the top eight have varied, as has their success in the playoffs.

And yet while teams around them have had their highs and lows throughout the table (including a mercurial Gotham, one of three teams to beat Washington this season, who moved ahead of them into first place on Sunday) the Spirit have been, well, consistently good. And they’ve been good despite navigating myriad changes, including the departure of the former NWSL rookie of the year Croix Bethune – who now plays for Kansas City – and two key starters in the run to the championship last season (Aubrey Kingsbury and Casey Krueger) on maternity leave.

View image in fullscreen Croix Bethune, seen here surging away from Gotham FC’s Esther González, left Washington Spirit and joined Kansas City Current. Photograph: Reed Hoffmann/AP

“Turnover is normal in this league, so we do not take continuity for granted,” says Haley Carter, Washington’s president of soccer operations – a former player, coach and executive who most recently played a key role in Orlando Pride’s historic championship-winning season in 2024.

Describing the importance of adding the right players to a strong foundation, Carter says: “We try to be thoughtful about who joins the club. When we sign a player or hire on the sporting side, fit is one of the first things we look at, because we are trying to build an environment and not just a roster.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The Spirit have done a commendable job with talent identification in recent years, and have folded international talents from a large swath of countries into the spine of their team. Last June, Sofia Cantore became the first Italian in NWSL (she finished with four goals and one assist in 12 games, and has the same number this season). They also signed the league’s first Paraguayan, the 18-year-old Claudia Martínez, who has three goals in an impressive rookie campaign.

With the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (Wafcon) ongoing, the Spirit have six players there representing Nigeria, Algeria, Côte d’Ivoire, Cameroon and Burkina Faso. (It’s a nod to the team’s depth that they’ve managed reasonably well without them.) Importantly, with Kingsbury out, the 28-year-old Scottish goalkeeper Sandy MacIver has stepped in with aplomb, setting a team record for consecutive clean sheets (four) and has the fourth-best save percentage in the league.

Of course, in addition to the Spirit’s impressive cadre of international talents, one of the NWSL’s most marketable names, Trinity Rodman, is pivotal to their past success and ongoing hopes of winning more trophies. Rodman’s 13 goal contributions in 18 games are the team’s most amid an in-form season. Her ability to press a backline, create space, take on defenders and link with teammates such as Cantore or the Colombian midfielder Leicy Santos has been inseparable from the side’s consistency this year.

View image in fullscreen Trinity Rodman (centre) slots the ball past the Houston Dash keeper Jane Campbell to score one of her two goals in Washington Spirit’s 2-1 victory in July. Photograph: Scott Taetsch/NWSL/Getty Images

With interest from abroad, Rodman’s contract was so important to the team and league that (with the investment-happy support of the team owner, Michele Kang) the NWSL created a new “high-impact player” policy to help keep her stateside. The so-called Rodman rule allows teams to spend $1m outside the standard salary cap for players who meet certain criteria.

Kang, who has made news in recent weeks because of a $400m lawsuit with John Textor, is one of the most well-known figures in women’s football, as the owner of three clubs in three countries (the Spirit, OL Lyonnes and London City Lionesses). According to Carter, collaboration among the trio is indeed under way. It is “one of the most exciting parts of what we are building” and “is more structured than people might assume”.

Rather than reinvent the wheel, the three clubs collaborate across medical, performance and technical departments, and use “shared themes, shared processes, and increasingly shared software platforms for talent identification, performance management, athlete wellness, and operational efficiency”.

While things are looking bright for the Spirit at the moment, the remainder of the regular season and the playoffs just beyond will be the final proving ground for the theme of their season thus far: despite changes and good old NWSL chaos, the Spirit can be reliably good.
