Sports.title: Fifa accused of using ‘blackmail’ to force support for Infantino’s re-election bid
Sports.content:
The Jordan Football Association president, Prince Ali bin al-Hussein, has accused Gianni Infantino’s administration of “blackmail”, claiming that Fifa threatened to withhold financial assistance from his federation if it refused to back the president’s bid for re-election.

In a major intervention Prince Ali, who ran for the Fifa presidency against Infantino in 2016 and finished third, listed a number of problems dogging the global governing body and said Jordan’s players have not yet been paid for appearing in the Arab Cup last year. Prince Ali is head of the West Asian Football Federation, which includes influential states such as Qatar and the United Arab Emirates that have thus far backed Infantino to stay on.

It came on a day when Infantino’s authority was dealt a further blow as two more key allies distanced themselves from his failed World Cup private investment plan. His No 2, the Fifa secretary general, Mattias Grafström, was revealed to have called the botched Fifa Forward Enterprise a “sad and reproachable series of events” in an email to the organisation’s staff. Meanwhile the former Arsenal manager Arsène Wenger, who is now Fifa’s chief of global development, said the project’s withdrawal was “absolutely necessary and beyond question”.

Infantino is steadily losing backing from countries who previously had sent letters to endorse his continuation for a fourth term in charge. It is understood that Greece is the latest federation to have pulled its support, following the lead taken by countries such as England, Wales, Finland and Serbia. More European federations are expected to follow in the coming days, while a number of nations in Concacaf – the North and Central American and Caribbean confederation – are also giving serious consideration to withdrawing their backing.

Prince Ali’s statement, published on X, painted the picture of a small country facing a litany of roadblocks when it came to receiving help from the global governing body. Jordan competed in their first World Cup this year but he explained some of their fans had not received visas, despite purchasing tickets, and expressed anger at being taxed by the US for being based in the country.

“We have been waiting for reward money for our players since December for the Arab Cup in Qatar, which is a Fifa event,” his statement read. “The money our team should receive for having reached the final has not been delivered yet, while at the same time Fifa brags about how many billions they have in reserve.

View image in fullscreen The Fifa president, Gianni Infantino (centre), and secretary general, Mattias Grafström (right), with Arsène Wenger during the 2026 World Cup. Photograph: ANP/Shutterstock

“It is clear the problem really is with leadership. For months, Fifa has been refusing to help us on any of these or other matters – until it was verbally communicated to me during the World Cup that if I endorsed Infantino it would go a long way to helping our FA out.

“We pride ourselves in Jordan in upholding ethical values. We did not endorse him before and certainly will not now. But the whole situation amounts to blackmail and we refuse to give in to that.”

Other countries are understood to have been put under concerted pressure to formally back Infantino before the Fifa election in March, although details of how it was applied remain unclear in those cases.

Grafström’s email had urged Fifa staff to keep morale high after what was perceived to be a successful World Cup. His message stopped short of criticising Infantino by name and promised to shield colleagues from the strife enveloping their organisation.

“A sad and reproachable series of events – which were thankfully concluded with the FFE project permanently abandoned – for as much as we feel dismayed by them, should not overshadow this reality,” read a section of the email.

11:54 Is Gianni Infantino’s time up as Fifa president? - The Latest

He referred to “a turmoil, which is difficult to comprehend and accept” and said: “Individuals, unstable moments and unfortunate episodes come and go. The institution, its mission and its responsibility towards world football continue, and that is why we should always keep our professionalism, sense of perspective and composure.”

Wenger, who assumed his current position in November 2019, confirmed he had been among the many senior Fifa staff sidelined by Infantino’s plan. “I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports,” he said.

“The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent Fifa that serves our game with commitment, transparency, and integrity.”

Fifa was contacted for comment regarding Prince Ali’s accusations.

According to reports, Infantino has called Fifa staff to a crisis meeting in the Moroccan capital, Rabat, on Wednesday as he tries to cling to his position.

Sports.title: Arsenal agree £75m fee with Newcastle for Bruno Guimarães as clubs reach compromise
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimarães is set to leave Newcastle’s pre-season training camp in southern Spain and fly to London before a £75m move to Arsenal. The out-going Newcastle captain is scheduled to undergo a medical in north London in the next couple of days after the two clubs finally compromised on the fee.

While Arsenal had initially wanted to pay no more than £60m for the Brazil midfielder, who turns 29 in November and has two years remaining on his contract, Newcastle demanded a minimum of £80m.

Having sold Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali to Barcelona and Tottenham respectively earlier this summer, Newcastle had no need to sell Guimarães and would have preferred to keep a key player who was integral to their 2025 League Cup triumph.

Since the Brazilian’s arrival from Lyon in January 2022, Newcastle have struggled to win games without Guimarães on the pitch. In his 153 League appearances he scored 30 goals, contributed 26 assists and, as Eddie Howe’s former team twice qualified for the Champions League, became an enduring crowd favourite. The loss of Guimarães is likely to hit Newcastle fans appreciably harder than even Alexander Isak’s defection to Liverpool last year.

Guimarães though was determined to join Arsenal even before Howe stepped down as manager last week. He flew to La Manga to meet the club’s in-coming manager, Matthias Jaissle on Monday but is understood to have told Jaissle he wanted out and could not be persuaded otherwise. The parting is believed to have been cordial and in marked contrast to Isak’s acrimonious exit last summer.

Lyon will receive a windfall in the region of £7m due to a sell on clause that stipulates they are entitled to 20% of any profit Newcastle make on the sale of Guimarães.

Arsenal, who have sanctioned the sale of Christian Norgaard to Everton for £7m in anticipation of bringing in Guimarães, are now expected to step up their attempts to sign a defender and another forward before the end of the transfer window. They could face competition from Liverpool in their attempts to sign Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa due to concerns over William Saliba’s back issues that will see him miss “an extended period”. It is thought that Villa want £60m for the England defender but Arsenal are unwilling to pay that much for a player who has less than two years of his contract remaining.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Arsenal have also registered their interest in signing Guimarães’ Brazil teammate Vinícius Júnior but are looking at alternatives should he decide to stay at Real Madrid. Barcelona’s sporting director, Deco, is expected to hold talks with Atlético Madrid over Julián Alvarez on Wednesday in a bid to seal a deal for the Argentina forward but Arsenal are hoping that the 26-year-old could yet be persuaded to join them. Mikel Arteta’s side have also been linked with Paris Saint-Germain’s Bradley Barcola, who is wanted by Liverpool and valued at around £145m by the European champions.

Sports.title: Transfer roundup: Coventry to make Yirenkyi new record signing, Crystal Palace to swoop for Gozo
Sports.content:
Coventry are set to break their transfer record for the fourth time in this window after agreeing a £23m fee with Danish side Nordsjælland for the Ghana midfielder Caleb Yirenkyi.

The deal for Yirenkyi, who impressed during the Black Stars’ World Cup campaign and scored the winning goal against Panama in the group stage, is set to be a record for the Danish top flight and comes after Coventry have already spent almost £60m on the winger Loum Tchaouna, the defender Aurèle Amenda and the goalkeeper Carl Rushworth. Yirenkyi, who was named young player of the year in the Danish league last season, will travel to Coventry in the coming hours to complete his move.

The 20-year-old is a product of the Right to Dream academy in Ghana and has been with Nordsjælland since 2024. It is understood that the Coventry manager, Frank Lampard, has spoken to his former Chelsea teammate Michael Essien, who is now working as a coach at Nordsjælland, about what Yirenkyi could bring to his newly promoted side. Brighton and Everton have also been linked with him in the past.

Elsewhere, Crystal Palace are closing in on the signing of the USA youth international Zavier Gozo as their new manager, Pierre Sage, attempts to strengthen his squad ahead of the new season.

Gozo, a 19-year-old who plays for Real Salt Lake in MLS and has represented the USA at various youth levels up to under-23, is expected to complete an £11m move to south London after he was left out of his side’s game on Tuesday night owing to an “excused absence”.

It is understood Palace have tracked Gozo’s progress at Real Salt Lake – who are part-owned by David Blitzer, the American who is one of Palace’s co-owners – for some time and view him as a potential successor to Daniel Muñoz at right wing-back. Palace need cover after Nathaniel Clyne’s departure at the end of his contract and selling Danny Imray to Wrexham for a fee that is thought to have been in the region of £5m last week.

View image in fullscreen Zavier Gozo is seen as a potential successor to Daniel Muñoz at Selhurst Park. Photograph: Anne-Marie Sorvin/USA Today Sports

Sage is also hoping to bring in several more players before the end of the transfer window as Palace prepare to juggle their Premier League challenge with a Europa League campaign, with a particular focus on replacing Maxence Lacroix after the France defender’s departure to Chelsea. Axel Disasi, who spent the second half of last season on loan at West Ham, is one option, while Palace have also been in talks with Brest over the teenage centre-back Raphaël Le Guen. Negotiations with Augsburg – the German club where Blitzer also owns a stake – over the French defender Chrislain Matsima broke down last week.

Palace are also thought to be targeting another forward and midfielder but are determined not to sell any of their leading players, including Adam Wharton, who has interest from Chelsea. The former Arsenal defender Takehiro Tomiyasu has been training with Palace in pre-season as he aims to earn a move after leaving Ajax, with his fellow Japan international Daichi Kamada signing a one-year contract extension last month.

Palace are also expected to offer Ismaïla Sarr a new deal to ward off interest from Fenerbahce in the Senegal forward, who scored 21 goals last season. Club Brugge have had an initial offer for Romain Esse rejected but the Belgian side are expected to return with an improved bid for the England Under-21 forward.

Meanwhile, Chelsea are close to agreeing a £16.3m deal to sign the defender Pep Chavarría from Rayo Vallecano. The 28-year-old, who was part of the team that reached last season’s Conference League final, is a left-sided defender and will provide competition for Jorrel Hato following the departure of Marc Cucurella to Real Madrid.

Manchester United are selling Radek Vitek to Middlesbrough in a deal worth up to £14m as his fellow goalkeeper Altay Bayindir prepares to join Celta Vigo on loan.

Michael Carrick’s side are in the process of shaping their squad for the new season, with their No 1, Senne Lammens, joined by the summer signing Karl Darlow in a new-look goalkeeping department. Vitek is on the verge of joining Boro, the defeated Championship playoff finalists, following an impressive season with Bristol City.

Sports.title: Which footballer made the biggest leap in competitive levels between games? | The Knowledge
Sports.content:
“Malachi Fagan-Walcott’s final game of last season was for York City against Rochdale in the National League. His first competitive game of 2026-27 season was for Hearts against Sturm Graz in a Champions League qualifier. Has a player ever made a bigger leap in competitive levels between consecutive club games?” asks Tom Reed.

Does a jump from the Welsh League to the FA Cup count as a bigger leap? Probably not, but this was an FA Cup semi-final, rather than a Champions League qualifier, and it’s a cracking yarn regardless. “I’ll nominate Gary Plumley,” writes Russell Connor. “Gary made almost 200 appearances for Newport County in four separate spells over the course of a decade but by 1987 he had effectively retired and was running a wine bar while making occasional appearances for Ebbw Vale in the Welsh League.

“In the build-up to the FA Cup semi-final in 1987, Watford found themselves short a goalkeeper after both Tony Coton and Steve Sherwood broke a thumb and finger respectively. As luck would have it, Gary’s dad Eddie was chief executive of Watford at the time which led to Gary being signed by the club to play in the game.

“Watford lost 4-1, and by all accounts Plumley didn’t cover himself in glory. His reward was a cheque for expenses, which he used to buy a fridge. The family referred it to as the Watford Fridge. Here’s an interview with Plumley about the game.”

You can also read read this from the Guardian archive.

View image in fullscreen Glen Hoddle is mobbed by Spurs fans after their FA Cup semi-final victory against Watford in 1987. Photograph: Colorsport/Shutterstock

“Erling and Alf-Inge Haaland bought the only surviving copy of the first printed edition of Snorri Sturluson’s medieval history of Norwegian kings and donated it to their hometown of Time in Norway,” writes Kári Tulinius. “Have other footballers bought and donated rare books or other antiques?”

“In 2017, the then Spurs midfielder Mousa Dembélé bought a 700-year-old building in Antwerp which he began converting into a hotel,” writes Tom Reed. “During the renovations a treasure trove of 18th-century porcelain, glass, pottery and tableware was discovered. Dembélé donated a portion of the treasure, reportedly valued at over £1m, to the local museum and the rest went on display in the lobby of the newly renovated hotel which he (perhaps optimistically) named De Gulde Schoen (The Golden Shoe).”

Poachers turned gamekeepers

“On Sunday, Sean Murdoch was the referee for St Mirren v Dunfermline in the Scottish League Cup. Murdoch was previously a goalkeeper and played for Dunfermline. Are there any other examples of a former player refereeing a match for a club they had played for?” asks Ian Golightly.

We had this question in 2010, when the answers included:

Steve Baines, the only referee in the English professional leagues to have had significant experience as a player.

Dick Jol, who refereed the 2001 Champions League final between Bayern Munich and Valencia.

Ben Haverkort, who as a player received 73 yellow cards and six reds, many for verbally abusing referees.

View image in fullscreen Gillingham players remonstrate with the referee Steve Baines during a match against Norwich. Photograph: Christopher Lee/Action Images/Reuters

There is a more recent example in the women’s game: Cheryl Foster MBE, who won 63 caps for Wales and spent most of her club career at Liverpool. She then retrained as a referee; within three years of playing her final game, she was on the Fifa international list. Foster became one of the world’s best referees and took charge of the 2023 Women’s Champions League final between Barcelona and Wolfsburg.

View image in fullscreen The referee Cheryl Foster (centre) on duty for a Women’s Super League match between Manchester City v Arsenal. Photograph: Mike Egerton/PA

“There’s a picture of me picking the ball out of the little Jeep that drove the ball on to the pitch and I had the biggest smile,” Foster said when she retired last year. “To describe those feelings of doing major tournaments and a big final is incredible.”

The oldest goalscorers in town (II)

In the Knowledge last week we looked at some of the oldest goalscorers in football history. But we missed one that was scoring in plain sight. You missed the second oldest goalscorer, 58-year-old Mykola Lykhovydov from Real Pharma in Ukraine,” writes Mykola Kozlenko. “There was even an article about him in the Guardian last year. He will not beat the new record though, as his club was relegated from professional football this summer after finishing last for two seasons in a row. At least unless they get promoted back and he is still around 60 ... ”

And though it wasn’t at first-team level, Tom Weir points out that, in 1992, the former Scotland manager Ally MacLeod scored a penalty for Queen of the South reserves at the age of 61.

Knowledge archive

“In the preliminary round of the English League Cup, Rochdale beat Tranmere 2-1 in a penalty shootout. Is this the fewest goals scored in such a shootout?” asks Paul Gage.

double quotation mark We had a similar question in 2008, when Mike Gibbons asked about the worst penalty shootouts. Here’s what we said back then: As Bill Martin, Florian Kinast and Paul Fields all point out, the shootout in the 1986 European Cup final takes some beating. Barcelona and Steaua Bucharest had played out 120 of the most tedious minutes of football witnessed in a major final, and with the score at 0-0 the game went to penalties, at which point both teams missed their first two. The Romanians then found their shooting boots and knocked home their next two, but Barça, then managed by Terry Venables, twice more failed to beat Helmuth Duckadam in the Steaua goal. Duckadam, who became known as “the hero of Seville”, had saved all four spot-kicks from José Alexanko, Ángel Pedraza, Pichi Alonso and Marcos Alonso, enabling Steaua to run out 2-0 winners. Sadly Duckadam, who at 27 was reaching his peak years as a goalkeeper, was forced to retire shortly after his finest hour. “Just a few weeks after his epic moment,” writes Florian, “Duckadam’s career came to an end due to a rare vascular disease in his right arm.” Florian also points to Thailand’s 1-0 win on penalties against Bangladesh in the 1973 Merdeka Tournament, in which Singapore also beat Cambodia 1-0 in a shootout. The world record for the worst penalty shootout, however, is held predictably by a pair of English sides. In January 1998 the under-10 sides Mickleover Lightning Blue Sox and Chellaston Boys met in the Derby Community Cup. The game finished 1-1 and the Blue Sox won 2-1 on penalties, though not until a remarkable 66 spot-kicks had been taken. Thanks to Paul Haynes for that one. All these and many other penalty-related facts, including the best shootouts, can be found at the ever-marvellous rsssf.com

View image in fullscreen The gloves Helmuth Duckadam wore to save all four penalties for Steaua Bucharest against Barcelona in 1986. Photograph: Lucian Alecu/Alamy

Can you help?

“Mikel Arteta (one title) is the only manager with title-winning experience (in England) heading into the new season. Is this the only time since 1889-90 that there is only a single title among the managers at the start of the season?” wonders Jeremy Finch.

“Kerim Alajbegovic joined Leverkusen on 1 July after his buyback clause from Salzburg was activated for €8m. He’s currently in the process of moving to Juventus for €37m, meaning Leverkusen will profit to the tune of around €1m per day Alajbegovic was at the club. Has any player ever provided a greater ratio of profit per day than this?” asks Richard Wilson.

“As a fan of the Liga MX club Tigres UANL, it’s great to see them enter the record books (or trivia nights, at least) by having the shortest professional player in the world: 5ft 1in Diego ‘Chicha’ Sanchez,” begins Steve Smith. “Not only that, but he scored an excellent goal against San Luis on Saturday. Made me wonder: just how short are the shortest goalscorers for the top division leagues in Europe?”

“Which footballer has played for the most clubs?” asks Paul Gage.

“I’ve driven through the North East on many occasions, and have regularly gone past Gateshead FC’s home (Gateshead International Stadium) and Newcastle United’s St James’ Park on the same journey,” writes Jack Birch. “Google Maps suggests the distance between these is 3.5 miles (or 2.3 miles if you are walking). Are there a combination of towns that beat this?”

“The Wrexham defender Max Cleworth had the letters of ‘Wrexham’ within his name,” notes Mark Lumby. “Have any other players had their club within their own name?”

Sports.title: Luis Figo blasts Gianni Infantino and demands he resigns – ‘Most deceitful and cravenly self-interested behaviour’
Sports.content:
Luis Figo has called for FIFA president Gianni Infantino to resign in an explosive open letter.

Infantino is desperately fighting to save his job after his bungled FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan was exposed, paving the way for a tsunami of missteps which resulted in multiple governing bodies threatening tournament boycotts.



3 Figo held nothing back in a ruthless column

The fall-out has been so significant that several nations, including England and Wales, have withdrawn their support for Infantino's re-election bid.

Infantino has even been accused of 'blackmail' from the president of the Jordan Football Association, underlining his desperation to hold onto power.

The FIFA president has since called a meeting in Rabat, Morocco for crisis talks as he attempts to cling on to his job.



A string of senior FIFA officials, including general secretary Mattias Grafstrom, are expected to attend the meeting.

Yet it may be a summit that only delays what appears to be the inevitable, especially now that Figo has added to the chorus of criticism via a stinging column in the Daily Mail.



What did Luis Figo say about Gianni Infantino?

"I have loved football all my life," Figo wrote.

"I was a professional player for 20 years. And believe me, I have met some rogues in my time in the game.

"But what I have seen exposed in the last 10 days is the lowest, most deceitful and cravenly self-interested behaviour I have ever witnessed."



Figo, who was a candidate for the FIFA presidency in 2015, only to withdraw and throw his support behind Infantino, accused the Swiss of overseeing a 'reign of terrible self-interest.'

"Infantino has debased the office of FIFA President that he promised to elevate," Figo added.

3 Infantino's presidency has turned on its head in the last week Credit: AFP

"He has lied, deceived and tried to feather his own nest at the expense of the game he is supposed to serve."



Figo's scathing assessment of Infantino's FIFA presidency represents a complete 180 given he trumpeted the Swiss official's qualities prior to succeeding Sepp Blatter.

"His (Infantino's) experience, competence, capacity for work and his honesty make him the best candidate for the presidency," Figo said in 2015.

"Gianni represents a new generation of leaders who put football first. He has a new style, a new approach to a procedure in need of transparency and an idea debate instead of political manouevering and personal attacks."

Wen in doubt

Figo is not the only famous football figure to have changed their tune on Infantino in recent days.



Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, who had been criticised for his initial silence on Infantino's sinister FFE plot, has since distanced himself from the failed proposal.

3 Wenger was quick to absolve himself from any blame for Infantino's FFE plot Credit: Getty

In a statement, Wenger said he had been left in the dark over the FFE fiasco and said the decision to pull the plug on it was 'absolutely necessary and beyond question'.

Infantino has also been desperately attempting to rally support from FIFA Legends, former internationals who are paid to appear at various events, but his efforts have proved futile thus far.

Sports.title: Jim Ratcliffe fired investment warning over £10million Manchester United decision
Sports.content:
Marc Skinner’s Manchester United exit shows Jim Ratcliffe’s priorities are elsewhere - unless he thinks he's smarter than every WSL owner.

That is the verdict of talkSPORT's Women's football correspondent Angelina Kelly, who believes there's little to prove that INEOS really care about the women's team at Old Trafford.

7 Ratcliffe previously referred to the women's team as 'girls' and 'an opportunity' Credit: Getty

The Red Devils lost their manager just a month before the new season due to a lack of resources and investment from the hierarchy.

It is the second successive women's head coach who has had issues with recruitment, with his predecessor, former England defender Casey Stoney, quitting in similar fashion in 2021.

How big of a shock was Skinner's departure?

Kelly told talkSPORT's Darragh MacAnthony and Alex Crook: "It was 50-50 because I think when you look at Marc Skinner's time at Manchester United, it has been quite turbulent.

"On one hand, you look at it and think he has actually overachieved because the amount of money that he has to play with versus Arsenal, Chelsea, and Manchester City is significantly less.

"He got Manchester United Women their first piece of silverware ever in the FA Cup, got fourth, third, fifth, second, fourth, got them into the Champions League for the first time in their history.

"So on one side, you have to say he did overachieve. However, on the other side of the coin, people were frustrated.

"The fans weren't his biggest fan. People were quite critical of the choices that he was making.

"They got to four domestic cup finals in total, won one of them. The other three they lost on aggregate to Chelsea 6-0. So it's not great in that sense.

7 Marc Skinner departs Man United Women with a win percentage of just over 60 per cent Credit: Getty

"His departure is kind of similar to the Eddie Howe situation," Kelly continued. "I think that you're looking at a manager who, within his world, is very well respected; ex-professional footballers that I speak to speak very highly of Marc Skinner.

"Whenever I've spoken to him, he's always been very polite, very respectful, etc. And I think he's looked at this and thought, this club are not willing to invest in this women's team.

"And going into a new season - The issues last season were lack of squad depth and wanting big stars that can show up on the big stage. He hasn't got that. A lot of players have been sold. The squad depth is less.

"He's looking at it and thinking, I'm not going to be able to do anything with this team. And I think for his own reputation part, partly he's thought, I need to walk away from this.

"In a sense, it is kind of similar to the Eddie Howe situation. The powers that be aren't backing you.

"I think the key difference is that Newcastle perhaps couldn't spend money. Manchester United Women won't spend money."

7 Skinner led the team to their first major trophy with victory in the Women's FA Cup final in 2024. Credit: Getty

On Jim Ratcliffe's comments

Man United Women appeared to be investing more in their squad the summer before Ratcliffe’s arrival in 2023.

Alessia Russo and Ona Batlle both departed on free transfers, but Brazilian forward Geyse was signed for a then club-record fee, in addition to Melvine Malard, Hinata Miyazawa and Irene Guerrero.

However, Ratcliffe faced backlash for his comments on the women's team a year later, while he was also left red-faced when he asked then-captain Katie Zelem what her role was at the club during a visit to the training ground.

Peterborough United chairman MacAnthony told talkSPORT: "Nobody wants to disrespect the female team in any football club.

"But at the end of the day, the team that's bringing in the mass amount of revenue into Manchester United worldwide, and I don't want to be unpopular saying this, is the men's team."

7 Ratcliffe was unaware of who United captain Zelem was when they crossed paths Credit: Getty

Kelly replied: "Definitely. I just think it doesn't help matters when you don't even know who your women's team captain is. You don't even know her name. It's going to come across as a bit disrespectful.

"And I do take your point in that sense. But when you look at the other big teams, you look at Arsenal, you look at Chelsea, you look at Brighton, you look at a lot of different teams that have men's and women's sides. They are pumping money into the women's side. And they're not turning a profit on that.

"Manchester United just about turned a profit last season. More or less, it was closer to breaking even, to be completely honest.

"But other clubs, they aren't making money on this. However, they are continuously pumping money into the women's side because they see this as an investment.

"I would ask you guys, Tony Bloom, a good owner, a smart businessman? Tony Bloom is pumping money into Brighton women.

"He is building a stadium in Brighton just for the women, not just an extra stadium, but specifically designed for women."

7 Brighton's purpose-built women's stadium will be within walking distance of their Premier League ground Credit: brightonandhovealbion.com

Sustainability with homegrown players

Man United Women have fallen behind their rivals in the market this summer, with Lyon defender Alice Sombath joining Tottenham.

Meanwhile, London City Lionesses, who finished sixth last season, signed two-time Ballon d'Or winner Alexia Putellas.

United, however, have sold Malard to Chelsea for £850,000, and their new strategy is to build a squad around home-grown youth players.

Kelly added: "I think the issue is that sources are claiming that the club feel that spending is not sustainable in the women's academy.

"So the focus is on sustainability with homegrown players, which is understood to fit the identity of developing youth, etc. And they want to go down this route."

When pressed on whether homegrown players are just code for doing it on the cheap, she continued: "And this is my opinion in that if you want to bring in young homegrown talent, you need to have something to show.

"At the moment, they have absolutely nothing going into this new season.

7 Putellas has dominated the top honours in the women's game Credit: AFP

"They have a fantastic goalkeeper. They have a captain who is a wonderful centre back in Maya Le Tissier. They have Ella Toone, who is the biggest star at Manchester United. And they have Jess Park, who has been wonderful, who came over from Manchester City.

"Minus that, they have that one spine of decent players. There is nothing else to show that they really care about this club and that they are building around those players to actually achieve something, because the way things are, London City Lionesses are spending a lot of money bringing in a two-time Ballon d'Or winner.

"So the thing is either Sir Jim Ratcliffe is going down this sustainable route as far as we understand, and he believes he is smarter than the Arsenal owners, than Tony Bloom, then Michelle Kang, etc, etc.

"He genuinely believes he's onto something, or perhaps this is a situation where they realise that they don't want to put the money into it.

"It's not viable in Jim Ratcliffe's mind at the moment, and he just wants to cast it to the side.

"The senior women's side has only been established since 2018. A lot of young female players were at Manchester United, but then they got to the end of the road, and it was see you later.

'Struggle to understand what the plan is'

"Even someone like Ella Toone, she had to play football when she was younger at Blackburn and Manchester City because it [the pathway at Old Trafford] wasn't there.

"So I just struggle to understand what the plan is at Manchester United.

"I would love to know to make sure that this youth system is going to be so seamless that it can compete with Arsenal, with Chelsea, with these other big clubs.

"I'm just not too sure how they're going to do that, and when you think about it, what Manchester United Women would need - About 10 million, which is what? Less than Mason Mount earns a year?

7 Toone has received an MBE for the role she played in aiding the Lionesses to back-to-back European Championships Credit: Getty

"And I understand you can't just get rid of Mason Mount and take that money. But what they're asking for isn't hundreds and hundreds of millions. It's nothing on the men's side.

"That would make such a massive difference to make Manchester United Women be able to compete so that they are competing with Arsenal, with Chelsea.

"So you're bringing those fans in because young fans now, it's not always the club sometimes - It's the players.

"There will be people that supported Man United Women when Alessia Russo was there. Now she's at Arsenal. People switch gears.

"And I just think that in order to carry on pushing this, you still need to be bringing in big players.

"You still need to be putting on a little bit of a show, and the way that things are going...To have a couple of decent players, and that's about it; I don't know how they're going to even hold on to the fan base that they've got."

Sports.title: Leicester set to sign Premier League winger with medical imminent
Sports.content:
Leicester City are set to sign Wes Burns as the Ipswich Town winger prepares for a medical with the League One club.

Burns helped the Tractor Boys to a second promotion in three years, but he is free to leave, and the Foxes are believed to be close to his signature.



4 Burns has been with Ipswich for five years since joining from Fleetwood Town Credit: Getty

The Daily Telegraph reports that Burns will be leaving Ipswich ahead of the new Premier League season to join up with Russell Martin's men.

He's not the only new addition with Admir Bristric also joining Leicester.

The 23-year-old striker currently plays for Olimpija Ljubljana after returning from his loan spell with fellow Slovenia side Bravo.



The striker is a former Bosnian Under-21 international with six goals in 14 appearances.

He scored 13 goals last year and strengthens a position that Leicester desperately needed bodies.



After the arrival of Conor Chaplin, once Bristric signs, Leicester will have two strikers.

Burns, meanwhile, is set to become just the third senior winger in the squad as Leicester look to bounce back from two consecutive relegations.



The Welsh international is a League One veteran, having made 260 appearances in England's third tier.

In that time, he has 43 goals and 34 assists, adding some much-needed experience and goals to this Leicester side.

4 Martin is trying to assemble a squad capable of stopping the rot at Leicester Credit: Getty

Leicester transfers so far

After demotion to League One, there has been a huge swathe of changes to the Foxes squad.



Abdul Fatawu has left to join Ipswich in a deal worth around £20million.

Manchester City beat Arsenal to the signature of talented teenager Jeremy Monga in a £12.5million deal.

And Bilal El Khannouss has completed a permanent switch to Stuttgart.

Victor Kristiansen has departed on loan, while Patson Daka has joined Hamburg on a free after his contract expired.

Harry Winks also left for an undisclosed fee.

4 Leicester fans consistently fell out with Winks Credit: Getty



Ricardo Pereira, Asmir Begovic, Jamaal Lascelles, Jordan Ayew and Jannik Vestergaard have all left too.

In their place, Leicester haven't spent a lot.

But they've managed to convince striker Chaplin to drop down from the Premier League to League One.

Experienced goalkeeper Alex McCarthy has arrived from Southampton.

Liam Cullen has left the Championship and Swansea City to play for Martin again, having worked together while in Wales.

Wout Faes and Woyo Coulibaly are also back from their respective loans.



They start their campaign off in the Carabao Cup against Northampton Town, and you'll be able to keep across that action on GameDay Live with Adrian Durham, Micky Gray and Ben Mee.

They then start the League One season off the following week away to Notts County.

4 Watson is one of many players to arrive at Leicester so far Credit: Getty

Positive

Ahead of the new campaign getting going, Martin is happy with the work Leicester have put in.



Speaking after a 1-0 defeat to Genoa, he said: “I thought we played brilliantly tonight.

“I really enjoyed it. We were really dominant, had so many chances and up to about 70 minutes, they only had one shot on goal. We limited them to not much at all. I’m disappointed with the goal we conceded, but it’s pre-season.

“They brought on 11 fresh faces [in the second half] and we had the same team on, so it changes the game a little bit. Because we had a game today as well, we’re making subs with really young guys who did brilliantly and they’ve done great in pre-season.

“They did us proud. The team showed the identity we want. They’re so hungry to run, are brave on the ball and show real aggression out of possession and with the ball. We should have scored a fair few goals tonight, so I’m disappointed about that, because we had some brilliant chances.



“We’re playing against really top opposition, the same against Coventry today at the training ground. We’re playing against two top-flight sides and both teams, all the players involved, were fantastic.

“It has been great. On the whole, I’ve been really happy. The players are in a good place. Hopefully the fans enjoyed the performance. Obviously, a disappointing result [to end] pre-season, but hopefully they saw enough to be really excited, because I’m excited about this team and what it can produce.”

Sports.title: Rafael Leao offered to shock Premier League club this summer
Sports.content:
Leeds United were sensationally offered the opportunity to sign AC Milan winger Rafael Leao.

Leao went public with his desire for a 'new challenge' in June and said he'd be 'very happy' if a Premier League club came knocking for his services.



3 Leao has made nearly 300 appearances for Milan since joining Credit: Getty

Such was Leao's desire to play in the English top flight, talkSPORT reporter Ben Jacobs revealed his agency put out plenty of feelers to a number of clubs, one of which was Leeds.

"Rafa Leao was actually offered, believe it or not, to Leeds United along with Manchester United and Arsenal," Jacobs said on talkSPORT's White and Jordan with Adam Catterall and Carlton Cole.

"The magnitude of the deal, the finances, the appetite and all of that, it doesn't appear that anything is going to advance. My expectation at the moment is Leao might end up in Turkey.



"But there was basically a ring-around from Leao's agency to several Premier League clubs, and Leeds were one of them."

Turkish giants Galatasaray and Fenerbahce have both been recently linked with a move for Leao, who has been at Milan since 2019 and has two years remaining on his deal.



Riff Raf

In his time with the Rossoneri, Leao has been named in the Serie A Team of the Year on three occasions and was declared the competition's Most Valuable Player for the 2021/22 campaign, coinciding with Milan winning the league.

Despite being a winger by trade, Leao predominantly featured as a centre-forward last term for Milan, registering nine goals and three assists in 31 appearances.



But the club record arrival of Goncalo Ramos from Paris Saint-Germain would likely see a return to the wing for Leao under new manager Ruben Amorim, who takes over from Massimiliano Allegri.

And Amorim has wasted little time in warning Leao that the grass isn't always greener on the other side amid the Portugal international's desire for a fresh start.

"I have the feeling that all the players are working very well," Amorim said.

3 Leao is away with Milan on their pre-season tour of Australia Credit: Getty



"Rafa is lucky to be at a club like Milan, so he must be happy.

"I feel he is happy and motivated."

Who else could Leeds look to sign this summer?

Although Leeds may not have the financial capacity to fund a deal for Leao, Jacobs confirmed the club are still active in the market.

According to Jacobs, Leeds have 'looked at and held some talks' with Marseille forward Igor Paixao, although Aston Villa are also understood to be interested.

"Leeds could look for another number nine, a source of goals," Jacobs added.

One player who could fit the bill on that front is Chelsea striker Liam Delap, who may be available just one year on from joining the club.



3 Daniel Farke will look to build on Leeds' 14th-place finish last term Credit: Getty

Jacobs noted Leeds made an enquiry for Delap last summer but were beaten to his signature by the Blues.

He added no formal talks between Leeds and Delap have commenced this summer, with Everton and Newcastle believed to be sniffing around the striker.

Leeds have already recruited Harry Wilson and are poised to land goalkeeper James Trafford from Manchester City.

Sports.title: Liverpool can register two PSG stars with one non-homegrown slot thanks to loophole rule
Sports.content:
Liverpool can register two PSG stars with one non-homegrown slot thanks to loophole rule

Liverpool are eyeing an audacious double transfer raid on Paris Saint-Germain for wingers Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye.

The Reds are in need of reinforcements in attack due to Trabzonspor-bound Mohamed Salah's exit and Hugo Ekitike's serious injury issues.



2 Liverpool are hopeful of completing a double deal for PSG pair Barcola and Mbaye Credit: Getty

Ekitike remains absent for the foreseeable future after rupturing his Achilles during a Champions League match against PSG in April.

Liverpool have now turned to the Frenchman's former side to strengthen their forward options under Andoni Iraola.

The Spaniard has already overseen the signing of his compatriot Victor Munoz, while he continues to eye a bumper move for Barcola.



talkSPORT understands Liverpool are also pushing to sign Mbaye, with the PSG teammates scoring their first World Cup goals in the same game when France beat Senegal 3-1 in June.

Reds fans will be acutely aware that Iraola only has one more available senior non-homegrown slot, with the Premier League allowing a maximum of 17 in each club's 25-man squad.



How Liverpool can register both Barcola and Mbaye without sales

While Barcola would take up the 17th and final senior non-homegrown slot if he arrives at Anfield, his 18-year-old teammate would be able to be registered immediately as well.

An Under-21 loophole exists in the Premier League's rules that means Liverpool can bypass the 17-player non-homegrown cap.



Players who were born on or after January 1, 2005 will count as U21 for the 2026/27 season, which includes new signing Jeremy Jacquet.

Jacquet became Liverpool's second-most expensive defender ever after a £60million package was agreed with Rennes.

2 Mbaye (left) wouldn't take up a non-homegrown slot while Barcola would Credit: AFP

Liverpool's new No.5 is expected to play a huge part for the club this season after Ibrahima Konate left on a free transfer to Real Madrid.



However, the 21-year-old will join Rio Ngumoha and Trey Nyoni on the unrestricted Under-21 list, as would Mbaye if he arrives at Anfield.

In fact, the latter wouldn't even have to be registered as a senior player in Liverpool's Premier League squad until 2029/30.

By which time, Mbaye, assuming he does join Iraola's side this summer, would even count as a homegrown player.

The Premier League's regulations stipulate that a HG player counts as anyone who registered to any club affiliated to either the English or Welsh FA for a period, continuous or not, of three entire seasons, or 36 months, before his 21st birthday, or the end of the season during which he turns 21 - regardless of nationality.



This loophole is why Jeremie Frimpong, who was born in Amsterdam and is a Netherlands international, counts as homegrown thanks to the years he spent in Manchester City's academy.

Liverpool's homegrown players Joe Gomez Curtis Jones Harvey Elliott Conor Bradley Stefan Bajcetic James McConnell Vitezslav Jaros Jeremie Frimpong Freddie Woodman

Liverpool's non-homegrown players

The 16-man list includes both of Iraola's first two goalkeepers in Alisson Becker and Giorgi Mamardashvili.

Captain Virgil van Dijk leads a pool of four defenders: Kostas Tsimikas, Milos Kerkez, and Calvin Ramsay.

Wataru Endo, Florian Wirtz, Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexis Mac Allister, and Ryan Gravenberch are the non-homegrown midfield options.



New signing Munoz has taken up one of the slots in attack, alongside Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo, Federico Chiesa, and Ekitike.

Sports.title: Forgotten Manchester United duo set to leave club this summer
Sports.content:
Manchester United are set to make a major profit on what they paid for goalkeeper Radek Vitek as part of a double departure.

The shot-stopper is close to sealing a permanent transfer to Championship side Middlesbrough.



2 Vitek is set to be the starting goalkeeper for Boro Credit: Getty

The 22-year-old is set for a switch to Teesside in a deal that is worth an initial £6million but could reach as much as £14m.

The Red Devils also have a buyback clause inserted into the deal for Vitek.

And it's a big profit for Man United.

Manchester United paid a minimal undisclosed fee to sign Vitek from Olomouc in 2020.



He has since had loans with Accrington Stanley, Blau Weiss Linz and Bristol City.

Last year for Bristol City, Vitek made 41 Championship appearances, conceding 54 goals and keeping 12 clean sheets.



The 22-year-old is set to undergo a medical with Boro later this week before completing the permanent switch, having never made a senior appearance.

Not the only one

Vitek doesn't appear to be the only goalkeeper leaving Old Trafford this summer.



Altay Bayindir is set to join Celta Vigo on loan for the upcoming season.

The 28-year-old Turkish international will also have an option to buy for just shy of £3.5m in the deal.

Should that deal go through, it would bring an end to Bayindir's time at Old Trafford.

2 Bayindir replaced Andre Onana in the 2024/25 season, but he never fully convinced Credit: Getty



Bayindir joined Man United in the summer of 2023 from Fenerbahce.

Overall, he's played 17 first-team matches for the Red Devils, including ten in the Premier League.

His record in the Premier League saw him keep just one clean sheet and concede 21 goals.

And after featuring just six times last year, he looks to be moving on.

Goalkeeping department revamped

Senne Lammens is the undisputed Man United number one after an impressive debut season in the Premier League.



Bayindir would have thought he'd be number two, but Karl Darlow has arrived from Leeds United.

The Welsh international left Leeds at the end of last season with the expiration of his contract, and he's been snapped up.

Tom Heaton will likely be third choice, and Michael Carrick did need to make room in that department.

Bayindir and Vitek could end up bringing in decent fees, and these moves give them the chance to play first-team football.



You'll be able to catch Vitek's Middlesbrough debut on the talkSPORT network later this month.

Sports.title: Tottenham told key reason why they should reject Nicolas Jackson transfer from Chelsea
Sports.content:
Tottenham told key reason why they should reject Nicolas Jackson transfer from Chelsea

Alan Brazil believes Tottenham Hotspur should swerve Nicolas Jackson because he can't finish in big games.

Spurs have been linked with a move for Jackson, who is free to leave Chelsea and is valued at around £65million.

2 Jackson joined Chelsea in June 2023 and has made over 80 appearances Credit: Getty

But Brazil, who made his long-awaited return to talkSPORT Breakfast on Wednesday, hopes the north London outfit spends their money elsewhere.

When asked about whether he'd take Jackson at Tottenham, Brazil replied: "No, not for me. I hope he proves me wrong.

"I don't think he can finish. In big, big games, I don't think he can finish.

"I'm not overly excited. But I wish him well, I really do."

In the Nic of it

In Jackson's last full season with Chelsea, he missed a total of 19 big chances, the fifth-most in the Premier League, per FotMob.

However, Jackson boasted the worst shot conversion rate of that top five, which consisted of Ollie Watkins, Mohamed Salah, Erling Haaland and Jean-Philippe Mateta.

Jackson's shot conversion rate stood at 13.2 per cent, with Watkins the next-worst at 19.1 per cent.

The Senegal international also scored the fewest goals from that group, netting only 10 times in the league.

In comparison, the other forwards all scored 14 goals or more.

Jackson faces an uncertain future following Chelsea's acquisition of veteran striker Danny Welbeck from Brighton.

2 New Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso is looking to trim down his squad ahead of the new season Credit: Getty

The Blues also added Dutch international Emmanuel Emegha from sister club Strasbourg this summer.

With Joao Pedro to reprise his role as Chelsea's main man up top, Jackson is at risk of being squeezed out.

Liam Delap, who only joined last summer from Ipswich Town, is another who is no guarantee to remain at Stamford Bridge.

Hey, big spender

As for Spurs, it's already been a summer of heavy spending having broken their transfer record twice.

Mateus Fernandes' £85m arrival from West Ham set a new bar, only for it to be passed by Sandro Tonali days later as he joined from Newcastle for £100m.

Jan Paul van Hecke was another significant signing earlier in the window, moving from Brighton for £52m.

Spurs also acquired Andy Robertson, Martin Dubravka and Marcos Senesi on free transfers.

Sports.title: National League owner praised for his ‘cojones’ after rejecting seven-figure record bid for star
Sports.content:
National League owner praised for his ‘cojones’ after rejecting seven-figure record bid for star

Boreham Wood chairman Danny Hunter has been praised for turning down a non-league £1million bid for star man Abdul Abdulmalik.

Swedish side Djurgardens have tabled two bids for the best player outside the EFL - the second of which matched the seven-figure fee Fleetwood received from Leicester for Jamie Vardy in 2011.

3 Abdulmalik is regarded as the top prospect in English non-league football Credit: Getty

Abdulmalik, who came through the academy ranks at Championship club Millwall, only signed for the Hertfordshire club in July 2024.

The 23-year-old enjoyed a breakout season in the fifth tier last season as Boreham Wood narrowly missed out on promotion.

Abdulmalik scored 18 goals and provided ten assists across 56 games last season to help The Wood to the National League play-off final.

At Wembley, the winger was involved in both of his side's goals in their 2-2 draw against Rochdale, scoring one and assisting the other, but was powerless to prevent a heartbreaking defeat on penalties.

Abdulmalik has since been pursued heavily by Swedish side Djurgardens, who produced Tottenham star Lucas Bergvall and faced Chelsea in the Conference League semi-finals in 2025.

However, Boreham Wood have stood firm in beating away offers for the National League Young Player of the Season, who is also the cousin of Torino midfielder Tino Anjorin.

Boreham Wood reject £1m bid for Abdul Abdulmalik

Referencing Boreham Wood chairman, Peterborough United owner Darragh MacAnthony told talkSPORT: "I love Danny's 'cojones'.

"Danny's the owner. Barry [Fry - the Director of Football at Posh] goes back a long way with him. I've met him. Runs a brilliant club.

"I think he wants his son to have that club in the EFL. Hence why Danny's a very wealthy man. Hence why he can say no."

3 Djurgardens have had two offers rebuffed for Abdulmalik Credit: Getty

3 Leicester made Vardy the first £1million non-league player Credit: Getty

Abdulmalik is the best player by a country mile at non-league

"He's having a right go," MacAnthony continued to talkSPORT's Alex Crook on Boreham Wood chairman Hunter.

"So the flip to that would be that obviously the boy is turning, I think, [24] this season - obviously he's been the best player by a country mile in non-league.

"And the player seems to be pretty calm about staying, which is fascinating nowadays because 9 times out of 10, the player is aggressively pushing to move out of there and go upwards.

"So you want Boreham Wood to win promotion this year. They were very unfortunate last year. I was gutted for them.

"For Danny, and for what he's done for his club and put the time in.

If that's his last hurrah to win promotion to the EFL and then hand it to a family member, that would be wonderful for him."

Sports.title: Aston Villa braced for fresh Arsenal bid for Ezri Konsa, Mikey Moore set for Cologne loan... and Mo Salah jets in to Turkey: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Aston Villa braced for fresh Arsenal bid for Ezri Konsa, Mikey Moore set for Cologne loan... and Mo Salah jets in to Turkey: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Melia hopes to impress at the Imps

Tottenham’s teenage striker Mason Melia has undergone his medical at Lincoln today ahead of finalising his loan move. The 18-year-old is a Republic of Ireland international.

Spurs' Moore set for Germany

Tottenham winger Mikey Moore is poised to accept a loan move to Cologne in Germany.

The 18-year-old spent last year on loan with Rangers.

Villa working on £14m Ruggeri deal

Aston Villa are continuing to discussing a £14m deal with Atletico Madrid for Italian left-back Matteo Ruggeri but they are awaiting approval from the 24-year-old. Daily Mail Sport reported their interest yesterday.

Atletico looking to utilise funds towards their planned bid for Cristian Romero at Tottenham.

Burnley go for keeper Amos

Burnley have signed free agent goalkeeper Ben Amos.

The 36-year-old had taken part in the PFA training camp for free agents this summer after leaving Port Vale at the end of last season. He has signed a one-year deal with Burnley.

Amos has over 360 appearances with a host of EFL clubs after beginning his career at Manchester United.

Ben Amos spent time at Charlton, among several EFL clubs

Chalobah arrives for Como medical

Chelsea defender Trevoh Chalobah has arrived in Italy for his medical with Como. The deal is worth an initial £25.7m plus a further £5.1m in potential add-ons.

Trevoh Chalobah is closing in on a move to Como

Coventry aim to break transfer record AGAIN

Coventry are attempting to break their transfer record for the second time this week after offering nearly £26million for Ghana star Caleb Yirenkyi.

The midfielder, who plays for Danish club Nordsjaelland, represented his country at this summer’s World Cup as they drew 0-0 with England and exited at the first knockout stage.

Back in the top flight for the first time in 25 years, the Sky Blues have already signed goalkeeper Carl Rushworth for £22.5m as well as defender Aurele Amenda and winger Loum Tchaouna. They have also turned on-loan midfielder Frank Onyeka’s move from Brentford into a permanent switch.

TOM COLLOMOSSE

Caleb Yirenkyi featured for Ghana against England in the 0-0 draw at the World Cup

Arsenal set to come back for Konsa

Aston Villa are braced for a fresh bid from Arsenal for England defender Ezri Konsa amid attempts to tie him to a new contract.

Daily Mail Sport reported last month that Konsa was the Gunners’ top target for central defence though their initial proposal was well below Villa’s £60million valuation of the 28-year-old.

Konsa has remained on Arsenal’s radar since. He has two years remaining on his current deal at Villa Park and the club would like him to sign a new one.

Having already seen key men Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans depart this summer, and with Lucas Digne poised to join Paris Saint-Germain, Villa boss Unai Emery would have an even bigger rebuilding job were Konsa to depart.

Having recouped more than £140million for Rogers, who joined Chelsea, and Tielemans, who signed for Manchester United, Villa are not under financial pressure to sell Konsa and are unlikely to do so without a high-level replacement lined up.

But along with Bruno Guimaraes and Vinicius Junior, Konsa is a key target for Arsenal – especially with William Saliba facing a lengthy injury absence – and they are unlikely to give up hope.

TOM COLLOMOSSE

Ezri Konsa would join England team-mate Declan Rice if Arsenal can pull off a deal

Come in No 61! Salah on his way to Turkey

Mohamed Salah is travelling to Turkey ahead of negotiating final details to complete his free transfer to Trabzonspor.

The Turkish club have posted pictures and videos on social media of the former Liverpool forward in a Trabzonspor shirt wearing No 61 while on their private plane.

Salah is scheduled to arrive in Istanbul shortly before heading to Trabzon later on today.

Read more on this story HERE

Mo Salah is pictured in a Trabzonspor shirt ahead of his move to Turkey

£14m Vitek set for Boro

Manchester United have agreed a deal worth £14million with Middlesbrough for goalkeeper Radek Vitek.

The fee is inclusive of bonuses for the highly-rated 22-year-old and there is also a 35pc sell-on clause plus matching rights and a buy back option for the Czech.

Tottenham defender Ashley Phillips, 21, is also in talks over a move to Boro.

Kim Hellberg has brought in seven signings so far this summer, including Will Lankshear from Spurs in a deal worth up to £20m.

Meanwhile, two Boro players are due to have medicals ahead of moves away. Delano Burgzorg is heading to Preston in a £2m deal and Kaly Sene is joining Young Boys in Switzerland.

Bruno set for £75m Arsenal move

Arsenal are set to complete their protracted £75million move for Newcastle United captain Bruno Guimaraes.

Full agreement is now almost done, with the clubs agreeing a compromise to end the saga.

Guimaraes is waiting for permission to leave Newcastle's training base in La Manga, in Spain, to finalise the formalities of his move to Emirates Stadium.

Read more on this story HERE

Bruno Guimaraes is set to wave goodbye to Newcastle after four years at the club

Swansea's Wilson heads to Gent

Swansea City forward Kyrell Wilson has joined KAA Gent for an undisclosed fee, subject to the relevant clearance.

The 21-year-old former Chelsea academy graduate impressed on loan at Falkirk last season and links up with the top-flight Belgian side who secured European qualification last term.

Swansea, meanwhile, are close to agreeing a deal worth £5.2m for Valencia attacking midfielder Andre Almeida.

Talks are focusing on an initial fee of £3m, plus £2.2m in add-ons as well as a sell-on clause.

Almeida, 26, was left out of Valencia’s training yesterday and has still to agree personal terms with the Welsh club.

Kyrell Wilson (left) in action for Falkirk last season - he will now head to Belgium

Altay's off to Spain

Manchester United goalkeeper Altay Bayindir has been given permission to travel to Spain and complete his move to Celta Vigo.

As Daily Mail Sport reported on Saturday, the Turkey international is joining on an initial loan with option to buy around £3.5million.

Vigo will cover Bayindir salary in full and there are various performance-related bonuses.

Sports.title: Serena Williams, 44, steps up surprise tennis return ahead of US Open as she confirms doubles date with sister Venus, 46
Sports.content:
Serena Williams is putting her Wimbledon injury behind her to once again step up her surprise return to tennis at the ripe old age of 44.

The American icon, who has 23 majors in an incredible career, has confirmed she will participate in the women's doubles alongside her sister Venus, 46, at the upcoming Cincinnati Open.

Organizers of the event announced this week that the legendary pair have been given a wild-card entry into the doubles field of the event which takes place in Ohio next week.

Serena's return to the court increases the possibility that she will appear at another US Open this year, with that tournament taking place in New York later this month.

Venus and Serena last played a doubles match together at the 2022 US Open, and this will be their first time teaming up in the hard-court tune-up tournament in Mason, Ohio.

The Williams sisters received a wild-card entry to play doubles at Wimbledon in June, but an injury to Serena prevented that from happening. They have won 14 major titles and three Olympic gold medals in doubles play.

Serena (left) and Venus (right) Williams, pictured in 2022, are returning to the court together

Serena played at Wimbledon but injury forced her to pull out of the doubles with sister Venus

Venus Williams, 46, is also set to play mixed doubles at the US Open later this month alongside Alexander Bublik.

Serena's grass-court comeback earlier this year consisted of only three matches: a first-round win in the doubles at Queen's with Victoria Mboko – after which they had to pull out because the 19-year-old Canadian suffered an MCL knee injury – a defeat in Berlin alongside Karolina Muchova, and then a 6-3, 6-7, 6-3 loss to Maya Joint on Centre Court in the Wimbledon first round.

It was in the latter of those matches that Serena suffered a knee injury which ended any hopes of her playing alongside Venus in the women's doubles.

'I’m heartbroken to have to withdraw from doubles,' she said in a post on Instagram. 'Coming back to compete again has been a gift, and the opportunity to play alongside Venus once more meant the world to me. I did everything I could but unfortunately my knee just isn’t ready to compete.

At 44, a new-look Serena is making a surprise comeback to the top level of professional tennis

The superstar pair hug on the court after losing their first-round US Open match back in 2022

'I’m especially grateful to tournament director, Jamie Baker, and the entire tournament team for giving me every opportunity to recover. Thank you to the fans for your incredible support and for making this comeback so meaningful…All I can say is stay tuned to a city near you…'

The post was accompanied by a video of the 23-time Grand Slam champion limping along with her right leg heavily bandaged, with her daughter Olympia playing with her walking stick.

There were also pictures of Williams receiving medical treatment, and Serena's post added: 'The photo of the syringes is the fluid they drained from my knee after my singles match - yikes! The good news is that my knee shouldn't swell or collect that much fluid again. The bad news is that, as hard as I tried, I wasn’t able to be ready for doubles.'

There was a very mixed reaction to Serena's decision to pull out, with some sympathetic and others furious that she had taken away other, younger, players' opportunities to compete in the prestigious tournament.

Sports.title: British boxer Raven Chapman, 32, rushed to hospital and put in medically-induced coma after training incident in Denmark - as family start fundraiser to return her to the UK
Sports.content:
British boxer Raven Chapman, 32, rushed to hospital and put in medically-induced coma after training incident in Denmark - as family start fundraiser to return her to the UK

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

British boxer Raven Chapman is recovering after undergoing emergency brain surgery and spending almost two weeks in an induced coma following a serious injury sustained during sparring.

The 32-year-old collapsed after a training session in Denmark on July 24 and was taken by air ambulance to hospital, where doctors diagnosed a brain haematoma and cerebral oedema.

Chapman underwent emergency surgery to stop the bleeding and reduce swelling before being placed in an induced coma to aid her recovery.

In an update released by her team, doctors have now started reducing her sedation as treatment continues.

Plans are also being made for her to be transferred to a hospital in the UK, where she is expected to begin what is likely to be a lengthy rehabilitation.

A statement from her team said: 'Doctors are doing everything they can to support her recovery, and we remain hopeful as she continues to fight through this incredibly difficult time.

British boxer Raven Chapman is recovering after undergoing emergency brain surgery and spending almost two weeks in an induced coma

The 32-year-old collapsed after a training session in Denmark on July 24 and was taken by air ambulance to hospital, where doctors diagnosed a brain haematoma and cerebral oedema

The GoFundMe Link can be accessed here.

'Raven's family are in Denmark supporting her during this incredibly difficult time. We kindly ask that their privacy is respected.

'At this stage, this is the only update we are able to provide. If there are any significant developments, we will share further information when it is appropriate to do so.

'Thank you for your continued support. Please keep Raven and her loved ones in your thoughts during this challenging time.'

A fundraising page has also been launched to help cover the costs of Chapman's rehabilitation and ongoing care. More than £46,000 has already been donated towards a £80,000 target.

Several stars from the boxing world have donated, with the likes of Nakisa Bidarian, Terri Harper, Ellie Scotney and Skye Nicholson among those to have contributed.

Former promoter Frank Warren shared the appeal on social media, writing: 'Raven is fully in my thoughts this morning, I'm really hoping she can pull through and get home safely.

'Everyone at Queensberry is behind you Raven, we're all hoping you can pull through this.'

Queensberry also issued its own statement, saying: 'Everyone at Queensberry is devastated to hear about our former fighter Raven Chapman. We're all hoping for a full recovery.'

Queensberry Promotions also donated £20,000, while Eddie Hearn contributed £5,000.

Chapman, from Norwich, has a professional record of 10 wins and two defeats. She challenged for the WBC featherweight world title in 2024, losing on points to Skye Nicholson in Riyadh.

Sports.title: Manchester United star and former Wales manager Mark Hughes' son died of sudden adult death syndrome after being found by his children, inquest
Sports.content:
The son of Manchester United striker and former Wales manager Mark Hughes died tragically from sudden adult death syndrome, an inquest has found.

Alex Hughes, 38, collapsed on the floor of his bedroom where he was found by his two sons at 7am on June 19, a coroner was told.

Mr Hughes' oldest son, Sebastian, 11, carried out CPR but his father, the head of player recruitment at League Two Grimsby Town FC, could not be revived, the inquest heard.

Cheshire Coroner's Court heard the cause of death was found to be Sudden Adult Death Syndrome (SADS).

Today's hearing in Warrington heard that the condition usually occurs in young men and there are around 800 cases per year in England.

Area coroner Victoria Davies gave the cause of death as sudden adult death syndrome and concluded that the death was down to natural causes.

She said: 'A post-mortem report showed there was no signification result of toxicology. There was no alcohol or drugs or prescription drugs.

'A cardiac pathology report showed sudden death with a normal heart.

'There were no other significant findings.

'SADS deaths occur predominantly in young males. There were are around 800 cases per annum in England.'

Mr Hughes' Manchester United legend father had announced the tragedy in an emotional statement, saying it had left his family 'totally heartbroken'.

Alex Hughes, 38, was head of player recruitment at League Two Grimsby Town FC

The former Wales, Blackburn, Manchester City and Stoke City boss carried his son's coffin at the funeral last month as he paid his final respects.

In a statement via the League Managers Association at the time of his son's death, Mr Hughes senior said: 'Jill and I are totally heartbroken by the sudden and unexpected loss of our beloved son Alex.

'Alex was a wonderful son, brother to Curtis and Xenna, devoted husband and father to Jessica and their two beautiful children Sebastian and Leonardo.

'Alex was Player Recruitment Lead at Grimsby Town FC, and had many good friends and colleagues.

'He will be so deeply missed by us all.'

Leading sports figures joined mourners for the funeral at St Peter's Church in Prestbury, Cheshire, last month.

Mr Hughes' wife Jess, whom he had known since school, was accompanied by their sons, Sebastian, 11, and Leonardo, 9.

Former Manchester United manager Sir Alex Ferguson attended the funeral along with stars including Bryan Robson and Ryan Giggs.

Mr Hughes' father Mark was among pallbearers at the father-of-two's funeral last month

Mr Hughes's father-in-law, David Pollock, gave a moving eulogy, explaining how he was proud of his boys, who had begun pointing to the skies after scoring goals.

Born in 1987, while his dad was contracted to Barcelona, Mr Hughes had a brief football career in Wales before moving into a variety of behind-the-scenes roles.

He earned his stripes as a match analyst at Blackburn before Man City took him on as a scout.

Mr Hughes, who lived at a £1.2m home in Prestbury, then worked as chief analyst at another of his dad’s former clubs, Fulham, before forging his own path with advisory roles at 1860 Munich and Reading.

In 2024 he took over as director of football at AFC Fylde before returning to prominent scouting roles at Morecambe and Grimsby.

Dad Mark Hughes, now 62, had a distinguished playing career with United, including helping win their first two Premier League titles in 1993 and 1994, Barca, Bayern Munich, Chelsea, Southampton, Everton and Blackburn.

He then became a mainstay in club management after five years in charge of the Welsh national team between 1999 and 2004.

Hughes was most recently in charge of Carlisle United but left after suffering defeat in the National League play-off semi-finals last season.
