World.title: IMA threatens nationwide strike over Maharashtra move to register CCMP-trained Homeopaths
World.content:
IMA Headquarters termed the governmentâs August 3 Government Resolution (GR) âillegalâ.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Indian Medical Association (IMA) has threatened a nationwide strike if the Maharashtra government does not withdraw its recent decision permitting registration of BHMS graduates (Homepathy) who have completed the Certificate Course in Modern Pharmacology (CCMP) with the Maharashtra Medical Council (MMC).In a letter to Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Wednesday, IMA Headquarters termed the governmentâs August 3 Government Resolution (GR) âillegalâ and urged its immediate cancellation, arguing that it undermines medical education, violates established legal principles and poses a risk to public health.The controversy centres on the stateâs decision to allow CCMP-qualified BHMS doctors to register with the Maharashtra Medical Council. The IMA has objected both to the CCMP course and to what it calls âdual medical council registration.ââThe CCMP course has not been approved by the erstwhile Medical Council of India (MCI), the National Medical Commission (NMC), or the National Commission for Homoeopathy (NCH). Such a course cannot be considered valid and should be discontinued immediately,â the association said in its representation.The doctorsâ body also argued that allowing practitioners to hold registrations under two different medical councils is unprecedented in India and could mislead patients regarding a doctorâs qualifications and scope of practice.The IMA further pointed out that the issue is already pending before the Bombay high court in a petition challenging amendments to the Maharashtra Medical Council Act. It said the government should not proceed with registrations while the matter remains sub judice.Questioning the stateâs justification of addressing rural doctor shortages, the association claimed the circumstances have changed significantly since similar provisions were introduced over a decade ago.âThe Maharashtra government has already done away with the compulsory rural bond system for MBBS graduates because of the non-availability of vacant posts, indicating that there is no longer a shortage of qualified allopathic doctors,â the letter stated.The association also said equating MBBS graduates, who undergo years of full-time medical education, with CCMP-trained practitioners who complete a part-time course would be unfair to students pursuing modern medicine.Citing the Supreme Courtâs landmark judgment in Poonam Verma vs Ashwin Patel (1996), the IMA reiterated that practitioners registered in one recognised system of medicine cannot prescribe medicines or practise another system without recognised qualifications and valid registration in that system.The IMA warned that if the GR is not withdrawn and the CCMP course is not discontinued, it will call for a nationwide strike involving doctors of modern medicine, including medical students, resident doctors and interns across the country.Copies of the representation have also been sent to the Prime Minister, Union Home Minister, Union Health Minister and the Chairperson of the National Medical Commission.

World.title: Nearly 2,000 RSS volunteers assist over 40,000 flood-affected families in Assam
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) on Wednesday said its volunteers, along with affiliated organisations, have been carrying out rescue and relief operations in flood-hit parts of eastern Assam, claiming to have assisted more than 40,000 affected families across three districts.

1,912 volunteers have been engaged in rescue, relief, temporary shelter construction and post-flood cleaning work in Sivasagar, Charideo and Jorhat districts, which have been among the worst affected by the recent floods.

The organisation claimed its volunteers had extended assistance to 40,168 families across 378 villages in the three districts.

Rescue, food distribution and relief efforts

Nearly 200 people from villages including Kakati Gaon, No. 2 Konwar Gaon, Nepali Khuti, Bihubar and Chetia Koibarta in Sivasagar district were rescued and shifted to safer locations.

Stranded residents in Sundar Pukhuri, Bamun Pukhuri, Geleki and Rajabari were provided with cooked food, drinking water, medicines, clothes and other essential supplies.

Relief operations were also carried out in several flood-affected areas of Jorhat district, including Elengmora, Katiram Chuk, Kulai Chuk, Nalia Chuk, Shenchowa Chuk and Charighoria Chuk.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Relief materials distributed included rice, sugar, porridge, dry food, baby food, biscuits, salt, drinking water, potatoes, clothes, bedding, candles, soap, alum, medicines and mosquito-repellent coils.





Medical camps and rehabilitation work

The RSS said its volunteers, in collaboration with the National Medicos Organization (NMO), organised more than 50 medical camps in flood-affected areas.

Volunteers initially used small boats to reach stranded residents with food and drinking water before evacuating elderly people, women, children and patients to safer locations.

The organisation also claimed that volunteers are currently helping families with post-flood rehabilitation activities, including cleaning houses, providing cattle feed and medicines for livestock, and assisting farmers in paddy transplantation after floodwaters receded.

World.title: Congress vs Congress in Punjab: With 'sleeper cell' warning, party puts Channi camp on notice
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Will the

crack the whip against dissidents in Punjab? With differences between state president Amarinder Singh Raja Warring and former chief minister

becoming an embarrassing public spectacle, the Congress has sent out a strong message to disgruntled leaders in Punjab, warning of action against "sleeper cells" within its own ranks in the poll-bound state.

"We have to identify and fight the sleeper cells inside the Congress. A strong organisation at the booth level is the key to victory," said AICC general secretary and Punjab in-charge Bhupesh Baghel, in a clear message to those who have raised a banner of revolt against the leadership. Baghel declared that the Congress was fighting a "multi-cornered battle" not only against political rivals but also against those within the party allegedly working for opponents.

Taking forward Baghelâs message, state Congress chief Amarinder Singh Raja Warring declared that no party ticket would be given to anyone found operating as part of "sleeper cells." "While the high command will decide the candidates, I will ensure that no person working against the party gets a ticket. Loyalty to the Congress is non-negotiable," the Punjab Congress chief asserted.

Warring also targeted former state Congress chief Sunil Jakhar, who is now with the BJP, accusing him of betraying the Congress during the 2022 assembly elections.





Warring alleged that Jakhar had worked in tacit understanding with the BJP despite heading the Congress campaign committee.

Congress message for Charanjit Singh Channi?

While Baghel and Warring did not take any names, their target was obvious. The dissidents in Punjab are backing former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi, who has been unhappy after being denied the post of state Congress chief in the organisational reshuffle that was announced on July 1.

The move triggered a storm that continues to rock and embarrass the party even a month later.

With Warring retained as state Congress chief by the party high command, Channi and his supporters have missed no opportunity to show their âdissentâ and openly challenge the partyâs decision. Even the presence of Baghel in the state has not helped to ease tempers. From poster war to sloganeering at party meetings - hereâs how the open show of defiance has played out.

While "Go Back Baghel" poster surfaced in Muktsar, another poster surfaced in Ferozepur showing Channi wearing a vest with "RSS" printed on it.

Supporters of Channi have indulged in sloganeering at party programmes attended by Warring and Bhupesh Baghel in Patiala and Sangrur.

In another event in Sangrur town, activists of both camps clashed in the presence of senior leaders.

Channi's camp, comprising several state leaders, has been demanding the replacement of Warring by citing specific instances on how the state chief had created divisions within the party leadership.

Last month, they even gave an open ultimatum to the central leadership to make Channi, the Congress MP from Jalandhar and a prominent Dalit face, as state chief saying that under Warring's leadership the Congress cannot come to power.

Channi from 'chosen one' to âdissidentâ

Interestingly in 2022, Channi was the chosen one as the Congress grappled with intense internal fighting between the then chief minister

and his challenger Navjot Singh Sidhu.

With the two senior leaders engaging in open power tussle, Congress sidelined both and picked Channi to lead the state and the party in the 2022 assembly elections.

But under Channi, the Congress was decimated and reduced to 18 seats from the 77 it had won in 2017 under Captain Amarinder Singh.

Channi, who has now been made the head of the Congress campaign committee, has dropped enough hints that he does not accept the leadership of Warring.

Why Congress is backing Warring

And that brings us to the present Punjab Congress chief Amarinder Singh Raja Warring, who was handed over the reins of the party by Rahul Gandhi in 2022 after the humiliating defeat in assembly elections.

Warring, who has faced sloganeering from supporters of Channi during recent party programmes, has refused to step down. He has said that if the party high command decides to replace him, he would continue to work to strengthen the organisation.

"I have no desire to be the chief minister. I will better retire than leave the Congress. Rahul Gandhi also knows that Raja Warring can die, but never compromise with the BJP," he said in one of his speeches.

Warring has cited Congressâs 2024 Lok Sabha performance - when it won seven of 13 seats - to justify his efforts at reviving the party.

In a highly emotional speech at his hometown in Muktsar recently, Warring had said: "Everyone is after my life. Akalis, BJP and the broom (AAP) and even some of our own are after me. I have not committed any sin and my only sin is that when we came from 80 to 18 I was handed over the reins of the party."

Maintaining that he started from the scratch when the morale of the party's rank and file was low and some leaders preferred to stay abroad for months together, Warring said he led from the front.

Warring played down the slogans raised by Channi's supporters during party events and said, "People oppose those who are successful. Those 20-25 poor souls who come, one doesn't even know how they are brought in or what they are told.

I actually feel sorry for them; this sort of thing has been happening for ages. The event went well; people listened to the speeches, and there was a huge crowd. People do these things; it doesn't matter.

I have been in politics for 25 years."

So, what should be the way forward?

Former Punjab minister Razia Sultana called upon the party high command to take strict action against all those who were indulging in indiscipline and damaging the party. She warned that if timely action was not taken, the party could suffer major damage.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"Nip the evil in the bud," Sultana remarked.

But can the Congress do that? Theoretically yes, but practically we havenât seen the grand-old-party take clear leadership decisions, except perhaps in Karnataka. For the Congress high command, the standard playbook for handling leadership tussles in states has been âambiguity is the best policy.â

And Punjab has been no different. One can only hope that the Congress acts before it is too late. The strong warning to dissidents is a welcome first step, but it remains to be seen if the party high command can follow this up with action without being scared of the consequences.

World.title: 'Orchestrated spectacles': India rejects Pakistan's 'Youm-e-Istehsal' on revocation of Article 370
World.content:
"World not fooled by orchestrated spectacles": India slams Pakistan for statements on 370 abrogation, violence in PoJK

August 5 decisions an internal matter: India

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

'Stop bloodshed, dismantle terror networks'

NEW DELHI: India on Wednesday strongly rejected Pakistan's observance of the so-called "Youm-e-Istehsal", calling it a "political absurdity" and accusing Islamabad of spreading malicious propaganda against the country.In a statement, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the Union Territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh "are, have always been, and shall forever remain an integral and inalienable part of India."The MEA said the constitutional changes introduced on August 5, 2019 were entirely India's internal matter and had led to "unprecedented socio-economic development, good governance and democratic empowerment" in the region."Pakistan has no locus standi to comment on matters that are strictly internal to India," the spokesperson said.The government said Pakistan's attempts to raise the issue were aimed at diverting international attention from its own human rights record and its alleged support for terrorism.The MEA also alleged that the international community was witnessing the suppression of fundamental rights in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK), claiming Pakistani security forces had resorted to "lethal violence, targeted killings and draconian bans" to suppress peaceful civil rights protests in the region.Calling Pakistan's actions "hypocritical", India urged Islamabad to stop the alleged bloodshed in PoJK, take "credible, verifiable and irreversible" action against terror networks operating from its soil, and vacate Indian territories under what it described as Pakistan's "illegal and forcible occupation.""Instead of engaging in predictable diplomatic theatre, Pakistan would be well-advised to stop the bloodshed in PoJK, take credible, verifiable, and irreversible action against terror networks operating from its soil, and immediately vacate all Indian territories under its illegal and forcible occupation. The world is not fooled by these orchestrated spectacles," the MEA said.

World.title: Sambhal violence 2024: Probe panel claims unrest 'pre-planned', links Samajwadi MP, MLA
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Judicial commission report on the 2024 Sambhal violence claimed that the unrest was "pre-planned" and mentioned the role of

(SP) MP Zia ur Rahman Barq, SP MLA Iqbal Mehmood's son Suhail Iqbal.

"False information was spread among the Muslim community over survey. The report also states that the bullet which caused deaths were not fired by the Police, and that hooligans nad attempted to loot Police weapons," reported news agency ANI citing the report, which was tabled on Uttar Pradesh assembly on Wednesday.

Last year in August, Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath had highlighted that the report, which the judicial commission had submitted, revealed how a conspiracy for riot unfolded in 2024.

The three-member panel had met the CM and submitted its report concerning the violence that erupted near the Shahi Jama Masjid on November 24 in 2024 during an ASI-monitored survey of the mosque. The unrest resulted in four fatalities and injuries to several others. In the document, a sharp demographic shift is observed.

Highlighting major demographic shifts in Sambhal, the report notes that the Hindu population declined from 45 percent at the time of Independence to 15 percent currently, while Muslims now constitute 85 percent of the population.





Speaking at the inauguration and foundation-laying ceremony for various development projects in Sambhal, the UP CM asserted that the state is transitioning from "appeasement" to "satisfaction," leaving no room for any demographic shift. Adityanath linked the violence to a history of âtargeted actionsâ against Hindus under previous state governments.

According to the PTI, the panel traces Sambhal's history of communal strife to a 1953 Shia-Sunni clash, with major riots occurring in 1956, 1959, 1962, when Jan Sangh MLA Mahesh Gupta was stabbed, 1966, and 1976, when a mosque committee dispute and the murder of a maulvi triggered temple attacks and curfews.

World.title: Jharkhand recruitment protests: CM Hemant Soren says 'action soon'; CJP extends support - top developments
World.content:
Jharkhand chief minister Hemant Soren (picture credit: PTI)

Students demand cancellation of JPSC exam, CBI probe

Hunger strike continues; student leader ends water boycott

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

CID probe underway into alleged exam irregularities

BJP demands CBI inquiry

NEW DELHI: Jharkhand chief minister Hemant Soren on Wednesday said his government would "soon take action" over the ongoing protests against alleged irregularities in state recruitment examinations after meeting Governor Santosh Kumar Gangwar."I met the Governor today and discussed the situation; it is being looked into, we will soon take action," Soren told reporters.The protests began after the results of the 14th Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) Combined Civil Services Preliminary Examination were declared on July 5, with aspirants alleging irregularities in the recruitment process. Students have since been holding round-the-clock demonstrations and an indefinite sit-in, demanding transparency, accountability and reforms in the state's recruitment agencies.The protesters are seeking cancellation of the 14th JPSC Combined Civil Services Preliminary Examination, a CBI probe into alleged irregularities in JPSC and JSSC-CGL recruitment examinations, and the public release of OMR sheets and answer scripts. A section of the protesters has warned of gheraoing the Jharkhand Assembly on August 6 if their demands are not addressed.Student leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who has been on an indefinite hunger strike over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC), consumed water on Wednesday, the fourth day of his fast.Mahto said he decided to drink water after climate activist Sonam Wangchuk appealed to him to do so during a video call. However, he said the hunger strike and the ongoing satyagraha would continue until the government addressed the students' demands.The state's Criminal Investigation Department (CID), which is probing the alleged examination irregularities, has conducted raids at multiple locations across Jharkhand. Officials have seized laptops, mobile phones, bank documents, carbon copies of OMR sheets and other materials, which are being examined as part of the investigation.The opposition BJP has also stepped up its attack on the state government, with leader of opposition Babulal Marandi and other party leaders demanding a CBI probe, strict action against those responsible for any wrongdoing and immediate acceptance of the students' demands.

World.title: Aadi Thirukalyanam festival commences with flag hoisting at Sri Ramanathaswamy Temple
World.content:
The Aadi Thirukalyana festival commenced on Wednesday with the flag hoisting at the Rameswaram Sri Ramanathaswamy Temple.

As the 17-day festival would continue until August 21, on the first day of the Aadi Thirukalyana festival the temple doors of the temple were opened at around 4 a.m., and Spadilinga Puja was performed.

Following the evening worship (Sayarakshai Puja) and regular morning pujas, Ramalakshmi, the temple elephant of Rameswaram, paraded around the four chariot streets carrying the flag.

At around 10 a.m., Goddess Parvathavardhini Amman, adorned in special decorations, arrived at the Navasakthi Mandapam.

Subsequently, the flag hoisting ceremony was conducted at the golden flagstaff inside the mandapam during the auspicious Kannya Lagna, amidst the chanting of mantras by Vedic scholars, marking the commencement of the Aadi Thirukalyana festival. A large number of devotees participated in the event.

The 17-day festival features a series of prominent events, beginning with Aadi Amavasai on Wednesday, August 12, followed by the Chariot Festival on Thursday, August 13. The celebrations continue with Aadi Pooram on Friday, August 14, Aadi Tapasu on Saturday, August 15, and the main Thirukalyanam ceremony on Sunday, August 16.

The festival will officially conclude following the procession to the Gandamadana Parvatham mandapadi on Friday, August 21.

World.title: MCC clears encroachment of footpaths on Sayyaji Rao Road
World.content:
Resuming its footpath clearance drive, the Mysuru City Corporation (MCC) authorities on Wednesday carried out a footpath encroachment clearance drive on Sayyaji Rao Road.

MCC personnel from Abhaya led by officials went about clearing the encroachment on the footpath on both sides of Sayyaji Rao Road.

The MCC staff began the drive from K.R. Circle by appealing to the vendors through a public address system to immediately vacate the footpaths and warned them that their materials will be taken away if they failed to abide by the directions.

Most of the footpath vendors obliged by removing their items including garments, footwear, plastic items, fruits, bangles etc.

The MCC authorities had begun a footpath clearance drive to ensure free movement of pedestrians in line with the directions issued by the Supreme Court.

Some of the vendors on Sayyaji Rao Road said they were using only two feet of the footpath and were not hindering the free movement of the pedestrians. They, however, pointed out that some of the shopkeepers were using a portion of the footpath to display their wares.

They said they were doing business on the footpath without affecting the pedestrians. “We barely earn ₹500 a day to feed our families. Most of our customers are also poor people,” said a footpath vendor.

A vendor said he had been doing business on the footpath for three decades now and some of them had even been given valid ID cards by the MCC authorities.

World.title: Tirur Bar seeks modern court complex to replace century-old building
World.content:
The Tirur Bar Association has demanded a new court complex at Tirur, citing the limitations of the existing facility, which was established in 1910.

The present court complex has served the region for over a century, but it lacks the infrastructure needed for the growing number of cases and modern judicial requirements, said Bar Association officials.

More than 500 lawyers currently practise under the Tirur Bar Association, but the complex does not have enough space for offices, a library or consultation rooms.

Hundreds of litigants, police personnel, witnesses, and court staff who visit the court daily also face a shortage of waiting areas, sanitation facilities, and parking space.

The existing building does not have adequate facilities for digital courtrooms, e-filing, secure record storage, and accessibility for senior citizens and persons with disabilities.

The Bar Association has demanded a centenary court complex with courtrooms, conference rooms, a legal library, waiting areas, digital display systems, and other public amenities under one roof.

It has urged the Central and State governments, elected representatives, and judicial authorities to provide financial and administrative support for the project.

K.M. Saleem, former treasurer of the Tirur Bar Association, said it was time for the authorities to consider a new court building for Tirur.

World.title: Ramanathapuram pushes toward 2030 carbon neutrality goal with decarbonisation action plan
World.content:
A district-level consultation meeting regarding the Carbon Neutral Hub initiative by the Department of Environment and Climate Change was held here on Wednesday.

The meeting brought together key stakeholders to anchor the district’s comprehensive Decarbonisation Action Plan.

The initiative forms a core part of the State government’s broader strategy to combat climate impacts and secure sustainable, long-term growth across selected regions.

Deliberations centered on actionable interventions required to hit the district’s carbon neutrality target by 2030.

Key proposals highlighted during the session included the promotion of electric vehicles and green transportation, widespread roadside afforestation, the vital protection and expansion of local mangrove ecosystems, an accelerated shift toward renewable energy sources, and optimised solid waste management.

Cross-departmental feedback formed a crucial part of the roadmap, with local officials pooling recommendations to tighten environmental protection frameworks.

District Collector M. Sivaguru Prabhakaran, Chief Executive Officer of the Tamil Nadu Green Climate Company (TNGCC) Bagan Jagadish Sudhakar, District Forest Officer Akhil Thampi, among others were present during the event.

World.title: Muthalappozhi harbour: Kerala Chief Minister promises urgent decision
World.content:
As safety-related concerns over the Muthalappozhi harbour in the district persist, Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on Wednesday promised an “urgent decision” with respect to the harbour.

While briefing the media on the Cabinet decisions, Mr. Satheesan said the government has scheduled a meeting next week. He indicated that the government has short and long-term measures in mind with respect to the harbour which has gained notoriety as a death trap for fishers.

Short-term measures that are required will be implemented soon, the Chief Minister said. “There are measures that need to be implemented in the long term as well,” he said. Mr. Satheesan’s assurance comes even as search operations are still in progress for two fishermen who went missing after a boat capsized on July 31 in the area.

The Indian Navy, Coast Guard and Marine Enforcement are continuing their search operations in the area to trace the missing fishermen, Mr. Satheesan said. The search has been extended to the sea off Colachel in neighbouring Tamil Nadu as well, he said. “It is unfortunate that they have not been traced yet,” he said.

Representatives of the Latin Archdiocese of Thiruvananthapuram had met the Chief Minister on Tuesday, seeking a lasting solution to the issue. Fr. Eugene Pereira, Vicar General, who was part of the delegation told The Hindu that over 80 fishers have died at Muthalappozhai since 2008.

The delegation had urged the government to redesign the harbour mouth in consultation with the local fishers. It also called for the introduction of a rapid response mechanism in the event of accidents.

Design flaws

The channel leading off the harbour has proved treacherous for fishing vessels. The local fishing industry attribute the recurring accidents to design flaws in the harbour groynes. Over the years, the region has also witnessed several bouts of protests demanding lasting solutions to the problem.

In August 2023, the Union Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Parshottam Rupala also had visited the harbour region and promised measures to address the issue. Mr. Rupala had said that said that all steps necessary would be taken to make the Muthalappozhi harbour accident-free.

World.title: Advocacy programme on mental health for BDOs held in Madurai
World.content:
M.S. Chellamuthu Trust & Research Foundation, in collaboration with the Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Department, organised an advocacy programme on mental health for the staff of the District Rural Development Agency (DRDA), which included Block Development Officers (BDOs), engineers and other stakeholders.

The programme was organised to commemorate the 25th anniversary of Erwadi fire accident that claimed the lives of several persons with mental disabilities.

S. Satheesh Kumar delivered the felicitation address and emphasised the importance of strengthening mental health awareness at the grassroots level through the Rural Development Department.

C. Ramasubramanian, founder and senior consultant psychiatrist of the trust, delivered the special address on the importance of mental health in society.

He explained that mental illness could affect anyone regardless of age, gender, education or social status.

Quoting national statistics, Dr. Ramasubramanian stated that nearly 10.6% of the Indian population was affected by mental health disorders and emphasised that all mental illnesses were treatable, manageable and preventable with early identification and timely psychiatric consultation.

He urged the officers to create awareness in villages, help people overcome stigma, encourage those in need to seek treatment, and make use of the trust’s mental health helpline.

He also highlighted the increasing incidence of addiction among young people and stressed the importance of community support in identifying and referring affected individuals for treatment.

K.S.P. Janardhan Babu, director – programmes, shared inspiring success stories of homeless persons with mental illness who were rescued from the streets, provided psychiatric treatment, reunited with their families, and successfully rehabilitated through employment with the support of the district administration.

World.title: Cyberabad Municipal Corporation considers dedicated grievance mechanism for SC/ST communities
World.content:
The Cyberabad Municipal Corporation (CMC) is considering setting up a dedicated mechanism to address grievances of Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) communities, as part of a series of welfare and development measures reviewed by the civic body on Wednesday.

The proposal was discussed during a meeting with Telangana State Commission for SCs and STs Chairman Bakki Venkataiah, CMC Commissioner G. Srijana, zonal commissioners, heads of departments and other officials concerned.

Among the issues discussed was the development of SC/ST colonies through focused sub-plans, including the provision of basic amenities. Officials also reviewed the provision of facilities and approach roads to burial grounds and the development of multipurpose function halls.

Welfare measures for sanitation workers and street vendors also figured in the discussions, which included support for street vendors, provision of personal protective equipment (PPE) kits and insurance coverage for sanitation workers, and health insurance for permanent and outsourced employees.

Scholarships and livelihood opportunities for members of SC/ST communities were also discussed alongside the proposed dedicated grievance redressal mechanism.

The meeting also reviewed reservation provisions for SC/ST communities in development works and tenders, backlog vacancies, compliance with reservation rosters and financial allocations. The need for effective implementation, monitoring and coordination among departments was also discussed.

World.title: TN-SHORE project offers fillip to mangrove afforestation and restoration in Kanniyakumari
World.content:
Under the TN-SHORE project, the State government is set to undertake the initiative of mangrove afforestation and restoration of degraded mangrove forests in Kanniyakumari, as announced by the State Finance Minister N. Marie Wilson, in the maiden budget of the TVK led coalition government on Wednesday.

Mr. Wilson has said that the project would be implemented over 2,500 hectares in Cuddalore, Villupuram, Chengalpattu, Mayiladuthurai, Nagapattinam, Tiruvarur, Thanjavur and Kanniyakumari districts.

In Kanniyakumari district, mangrove forests are primarily found in Manakudy and Rajakkamangalam. The mangrove ecosystem at Manakudy estuary is a vital ecological habitat, supporting a rich diversity of aquatic species while serving as a seasonal refuge for several local and migratory birds.

Siluvai Vaschian, founder of Heal Movement, who played a pivotal role in development of Manakudy mangrove forest in the late 1990’s, said the project presents an opportunity to expand the district’s existing mangrove cover.

He added that the district has mangrove wetlands only in Manakudy and Rajakkamanglam, where mangrove vegetation has already been established. The proposed initiative, he noted, could facilitate the expansion and strengthening of these ecosystems.

“Channels can be created within these wetlands and mangrove can be planted along both sides of the channels, enabling the forest to expand naturally,” Mr. Vaschian added.

Highlighting the spread of Prosopis juliflora in these mangrove forests, he stated that the periodic removal of these invasive species and ecological restoration of land are residential to sustain a healthy mangrove habitat.

Mr. Vaschian further said that mangrove afforestation and restoration would directly benefit the fishing community by enhancing the breeding and nursery habitats for fish, crabs and other aquatic species, thereby strengthening the coastal livelihoods while also improving the resilience of the ecosystem.

World.title: PM Shehbaz directs adoption of comprehensive strategy to attract investors for Discos' privatisation
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday directed relevant authorities to adopt a “comprehensive strategy” to attract international investors for the privatisation of state-owned power distribution companies (Discos) and complete the restructuring of the Privatisation Commission within one month.

“A comprehensive and effective strategy should be adopted to ensure the participation of investors meeting international standards in the privatisation of Discos,” the PM said while presiding over a review meeting in Islamabad, according to a statement issued by his office.

But, consumers’ interests should also be prioritised in the privatisation process, he instructed.

The premier further stated that all stages of the privatisation process should be completed within the stipulated timeframes and in accordance with established rules and international best practices while ensuring profitable outcomes.

He also expressed satisfaction over “successful roadshows” in Pakistan and abroad to attract investors, noting that the shows generated interest in the privatisation programme.

Officials at the meeting told the PM that the roadshows aimed at attracting investors for the Gujranwala Electric Power Company (Gepco), Faisalabad Electric Supply Company (Fesco) and Islamabad Electric Supply Company (Iesco) in the first phase of privatisation had been concluded, according to the PMO.

It added that the meeting was told that investor outreach activities and roadshows in Turkey, Saudi Arabia and China had produced encouraging results.

The meeting was also briefed on the progress of the first phase of Discos’ privatisation and efforts to strengthen the Privatisation Commission through institutional restructuring and the recruitment of skilled professionals.

Regarding this, the PM directed that the Privatisation Commission should strengthen its workforce by recruiting experts with qualifications meeting international standards in the fields of finance, law and information technology.

Their expertise would enhance the institution’s capacity and help attract greater investment, he remarked.

PM Shehbaz also directed relevant officials to ensure that recommendations from highly qualified professional consultants were incorporated in the privatisation process and all necessary legal arrangements and financial regulatory frameworks were completed in a timely manner.

Moreover, “consumers’ interests must remain a priority during privatisation and a comprehensive and effective grievance redress mechanism be formed for the consumers of entities being privatised”, he said.

Energy Minister Sardar Awais Ahmed Khan Leghari, Economic Affairs Minister Ahad Khan Cheema, Information Technology Minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja, PM’s Adviser on Privatisation Muhammad Ali and senior government officials attended the meeting, the PMO stated.

On May 19, the Privatisation Commission had invited expressions of interest from local and international investors for the much-delayed sale of Iesco, Gepco and Fesco.

The three are considered the most viable Discos among the 11 electricity distribution companies originally carved out of the Water and Power Development Authority (Wapda) in 1998.

The divestment is aimed at improving service quality through private-sector management practices. The transaction offers investors an opportunity to acquire between 51pc and 100pc shareholding, along with management control, in each of the three distribution companies.

The Privatisation Commission set July 7 for submission of expressions of interest (EoIs) for Fesco, August 24 for Gepco and Sept 7 for Iesco.

In June, Prime Minister’s Adviser on Privatisation Muhammad Ali told Dawn the first Discos in the country would be sold in 2026-27.

“We will run these three parallel transactions and hold bidding one after the other in October, November and December 2026,” he said, adding the transaction structures would have to be “corrected” before October and “we will do it”.

He said the Privatisation Commission had completed domestic soft marketing of three Discos of Faisalabad, Gujranwala and Islamabad in seven major cities, with chambers of commerce and industry and business houses and would now be expanding abroad mainly to Saudi Arabia, China and Turkiye and approaching other Middle Eastern capitals — Qatar, Bahrain, Oman and so on — virtually and through transaction advisers to tap in investors and technical operators.

The uniform consumer tariff will continue for the time being, but privatisation, resulting efficiency gains, and the absorption of surplus capacity would reduce the average uniform tariff, he hoped.

He said there was robust investor interest in the power sector. However, they wanted an 18pc dollar-based return, an end to uniform consumer tariffs, permission for self-power generation by new owners, freedom for the private sector to ‘buy and sell electricity’, and the government’s exit from the sector. They also wanted 8-10 year tariff visibility, including investment plans.

Ali said the government would not allow dollar-based returns at all. “We will provide rupee-based returns of 14-15pc plus key performance indicators (KPIs) that allow profitability of up to 18-20pc while sharing efficiency gains.”

Fesco, Gepco and Iesco collectively serve more than 14 million consumers across major industrial, commercial and urban centres of Punjab, the Islamabad region, and parts of Azad Jammu and Kashmir.

Their privatisation forms part of the government’s broader economic reform agenda aimed at improving efficiency, strengthening service delivery, attracting foreign and domestic investment, and promoting sustainable growth in Pakistan’s power sector, the Privatisation Commission has said.

Alongside these three transactions, the PM’s adviser had said that the Sukkur and Hyderabad electric companies would also be restructured and improved to complete their privatisation by August-September next year.

World.title: Search team reaches Broad Peak base camp with body of renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja
World.content:
A search team has transported the bodies of renowned climber Nirmal Purja and three of his team members to the base camp of the mountain where they were killed in an avalanche, the Alpine Club of Pakistan (ACP) said on Wednesday.

The avalanche struck on July 30, cutting off contact with the 10-member international expedition led by 43-year-old British-Nepali climber Purja on Broad Peak, one of the world’s highest mountains. His company confirmed there were no survivors.

“On behalf of the Alpine Club of Pakistan, it is announced with great sadness to confirm that, following an exceptionally challenging and technically demanding recovery operation on Broad Peak, the bodies of Nirmal Purja, Zhong Wang, Nima Sherpa, and Kilu Sherpa have been successfully recovered and have now arrived safely at Base Camp,” the ACP posted on social media, referring to a Chinese mountaineer and two other Nepali climbers.

“While today marks an important milestone, three climbers remain missing,” the club said.

“We remain committed to supporting all possible efforts to locate and recover them, whenever conditions allow, so that they too may be returned home to their loved ones,” it added.

The remains of three other members of the team — an American woman, an Omani woman and a Nepali man — had already been flown off the mountain to Skardu.

The bodies of Pakistani mountaineer Sohail Sakhi of Hunza and two Nepali nationals have not yet been recovered. Funeral prayers were offered in absentia for Sakhi in his hometown of Aliabad in Hunza on Monday, where hundreds of people paid tribute to the young mountaineer and offered condolences to his family.

Shock and grief have hit members of the alpine climbing community with the President of Nepal’s National Mountain Guide Association Tul Singh Gurung saying they had “lost a generation of accomplished mountaineers”.

The ACP said the recovered bodies of the four climbers would be returned to their families.

The club’s president, Major General (retd.) Irfan Arshad Khan, told Dawn that the deceased climbers would be airlifted to Skardu by helicopters, which had been unable to operate for the last three days due to adverse weather conditions.

“We hope this recovery brings them a measure of peace and the opportunity to lay their loved ones to rest with the dignity they deserve,” the club said.

It extended its gratitude to those leading and supporting rescue efforts — including the ground recovery team led by Mingma G and supported by Sirbaz Khan — as well as the dedicated Pakistani and Nepali recovery teams, the Pakistan Army, the governments of Pakistan and Gilgit-Baltistan, local authorities, the British High Commission, and the Embassy of Nepal for their invaluable support throughout the mission.

Nirmal’s business partner and Member of Nepal’s House of Representatives Mingma David Sherpa, who is currently monitoring the rescue and search operation, appreciated the “courage, professionalism, and selfless commitment” of the ground recovery team, saying, “We are deeply grateful to every member of the team for carrying out this mission under extremely difficult and dangerous conditions.”

“Our thoughts also remain with the families of the three climbers who are still missing. We remain committed to supporting every possible effort to bring them home when conditions safely allow,” he added.

Broad Peak is the world’s 12th highest mountain, located in the Karakoram range, and is regarded as one of the toughest and most technical climbs of all the 8,000-metre-plus ascents.

It was first summited in 1957 by an Austrian team.

World.title: ‘No sovereignty over East Jerusalem’: Dar condemns Al-Aqsa incursions by ‘extremist Israeli settlers’
World.content:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Wednesday said that Israel has no sovereignty over East Jerusalem and its holy sites, condemning the incursions into Al-Aqsa Mosque by “extremist Israeli settlers”.

Addressing the ministerial conference in Amman, Jordan, he said that the illegal actions of Israel — the occupying power in occupied Palestine — continued to threaten the sanctity and historical character of the holy sites in Jerusalem.

“They undermine international law, disregard UN resolutions, and further erode the prospect of a just, comprehensive and lasting peace.”

“Pakistan condemns in the strongest possible terms the continued incursions into Al-Aqsa Mosque by extremist Israeli settlers encouraged by senior Israeli ministers and carried out under the protection of occupying forces,” FM Dar stated.

By deliberately undermining the religious and historical status of Jerusalem, FM Dar emphasised that Israel was provoking the sentiments of billions of Muslims across the globe.

“This appears not only an attempt to undermine regional peace, security and stability but also to drag followers of various religions into a wider conflict,” he said, adding, “We cannot and must not allow that.”

“Pakistan condemns Israeli actions and provocations in the strongest possible terms,” he said.

He stressed that there should be no ambiguity that Israel has no sovereignty over occupied East Jerusalem and its Islamic and Christian holy sites.

“All measures seeking to alter its character and status are null and void and without any legal effect,” he added.

The foreign minister said Pakistan reaffirmed its support for the historic and special role played by Jordan and recognised the Jerusalem Endowment and Al-Aqsa Affairs Department, affiliated with the Jordanian Ministry of Awqaf and Islamic Affairs, as the legal authority with exclusive jurisdiction over the administration of Al-Aqsa Mosque.

Moreover, FM Dar said that Pakistan also remained “deeply concerned” over the continuous expansion of illegal Israeli settlements, the establishment of new settlements and the continued oppression of the Palestinian people.

“These policies violate international law and further entrench an unlawful occupation.”

In Gaza, he said that the humanitarian situation was extremely fragile.

“The ceasefire and the implementation of the elements of the Gaza Peace Plan have yielded some improvements; however, 59pc of the population still faces food insecurity and health crises,” FM Dar said.

Since the ceasefire, he said that over 1,100 Palestinians had been killed, which called into question the full and faithful implementation of the Gaza Peace Plan.

“Arab and Islamic countries must act with unity, resolve and collective action and should first reaffirm the protection of Jerusalem and the holy sites, demanding an immediate cessation of all violations against Al-Aqsa Mosque, preservation of the historical and legal status quo, and unrestricted access to the Old City of Jerusalem and the holy sites,” he said.

He said that Arab and Islamic countries should also reject “illegal Israeli settlement activities, annexation attempts, forced displacements, and demographic changes in the occupied Palestinian territory”.

“We should support the full and faithful implementation of the comprehensive plan to end the Gaza conflict and UNSC Resolution No. 2803,” the foreign minister said, adding, “We should also strengthen Arab and Islamic coordination and diplomatic efforts to ensure the protection of the Kashmiri people.”

Meetings on sidelines

FM Dar also held one-on-one meetings with the foreign ministers of Turkiye, Algeria and Egypt on the sidelines of the ministerial meeting on Jerusalem, the FO said.

In his meeting with Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, FM Dar “exchanged views on regional and international issues of mutual interest,” it said.

During his meeting with Egyptian Foreign Minister Dr Badr Abdelatty, Dar discussed Pakistan-Egypt relations, regional and international developments, and exchanged views on matters of mutual interest, the FO said.

Meanwhile, in his meeting with Algerian Foreign Minister Ahmad Attaf, FM Dar “discussed Pakistan-Algeria bilateral relations and explored ways to enhance cooperation in trade, investment, information technology, agriculture and other areas of mutual interest”.

Moreover, the foreign ministers of the R-4 Group, comprising Egypt, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, also met in Amman on the sidelines of the ministerial meeting on Jerusalem, the FO said.

“The ministers reiterated their unwavering support for the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people, including their right to self-determination and the establishment of an independent, sovereign Palestinian state on the basis of the June 4, 1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital, in accordance with relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions,” it added.

According to the FO, the R-4 Group’s foreign ministers reaffirmed that a “just, comprehensive and lasting settlement” of the Palestinian issue remained indispensable to achieving enduring peace and stability in the Middle East.

The ministers also reviewed the evolving regional situation and reaffirmed the importance of continued consultation and close coordination among the four countries in advancing regional stability, emphasising that dialogue and diplomacy remained essential to fostering stability and preventing further escalation in the region, the FO stated.

DPM meets Jordanian counterpart

Dar met his Jordanian counterpart, with the “deteriorating situation in the occupied West Bank” coming under discussion, according to the Foreign Office (FO).

The FO said Dar met Jordan’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates Ayman Safadi on the sidelines of a Ministerial Meeting in Amman to discuss the situation in occupied Jerusalem.

The FO said that the foreign ministers exchanged views on regional developments, in particular on the deteriorating situation in the occupied West Bank. Dar appreciated Jordan’s role in safeguarding the Islamic and Christian holy sites in Jerusalem and its support for the Palestinian people, it added.

“The two leaders welcomed the growing momentum in Pakistan–Jordan bilateral relations and reaffirmed [their commitment] to further enhancing cooperation across political, defence, economic, educational, cultural and people-to-people domains,” it added.

Dar and Safadi also discussed the situation in the region, including the recent developments in the conflict between the United States and Iran.

They underscored the importance of dialogue and diplomacy for de-escalation and reaffirmed their close coordination at bilateral and multilateral levels to promote peace and stability, including at the United Nations and Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, the statement added.

Separately, Dar also held a bilateral meeting with Abdisalam Abdi Ali, the Minister for Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Somalia. Alongside exchanging views on regional developments, the foreign ministers also reviewed the longstanding fraternal ties between the two countries.

According to the FO, they discussed ways to further strengthen cooperation in the “political, economic, defence, education, and capacity-building sectors”. They also reaffirmed their commitment to maintaining close coordination at multilateral forums, it added.

According to the FO, Dar is in Jordan to attend a ministerial meeting aimed at formulating a unified position on the situation in occupied Jerusalem.

It said that he would “reaffirm Pakistan’s unwavering support for the Palestinian people and their just cause” at the ministerial meeting bringing together foreign ministers from Arab League member states and a group of Islamic countries to discuss the deteriorating situation in occupied Jerusalem.

The foreign minister is also expected to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts on the sidelines of the meeting to exchange views on regional developments including Palestine.

The FO termed Dar’s participation in the ministerial meeting “a manifestation of Pakistan’s principled support for the Palestinian people” and its commitment to the establishment of an “independent, sovereign and contiguous” State of Palestine based on pre-1967 borders, with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital.

Pakistan and other Muslim countries have repeatedly condemned “continued incursions by extremist Israeli settlers” into Al Aqsa Mosque — Islam’s third-holiest site, located in east Jerusalem, which Israel captured in 1967 and later annexed.

The Al-Aqsa compound is a central symbol of Palestinian identity and also a frequent flashpoint. Under long-standing arrangements, Jewish people may visit the compound, but are not permitted to pray there. While Israel says it is committed to maintaining this status quo, Palestinians fear it is being eroded.

The foreign ministers of Pakistan and eight other Muslim countries in June expressed their “categorical rejection” of any attempts to alter the historical and legal status quo in Jerusalem and its Islamic and Christian holy sites.

World.title: Protest near KPC disrupts traffic in Karachi's Saddar area
World.content:
KARACHI: A protest near the Karachi Press Club (KPC) caused traffic disruptions across Saddar Town, leaving a large number of commuters stuck in long queues for several hours on Wednesday evening.

Roads near the press club were closed ahead of a planned protest by the PTI to mark three years since the imprisonment of party founder Imr­an Khan and demand his release.

A screenshot showing closed roads in Karachi’s Saddar Town area. — Screengrab from Google Maps

The PTI in a statement said it staged demonstrations in Karachi, Hyderabad, Mirpurkhas, Nawabshah, Umerkot, Mithi and other parts of Sindh, with participants demanding Imran’s release.

In Karachi, the demonstration was led by PTI Sindh President Haleem Adil Sheikh, Karachi President Raja Azhar, PTI Sindh General Secretary Dr Masroor Sial and Karachi General Secretary Arsalan Khalid. They and other party leaders led workers towards the Karachi Press Club, according to the statement.

“However, according to the party, police blocked all routes leading to the Press Club by placing containers and completely sealed the area to stop protesters from reaching the venue,” the statement claimed.

“PTI workers later held a peaceful demonstration near Zaibunnisa Street and Fawara Chowk in Saddar. The party alleged that police resorted to tear gas shelling and baton charge against peaceful protesters, leaving several workers injured,” it alleged.

PTI demonstrators face tear gas as they protest in Karachi’s Saddar Town area on August 5, 2026. — Photo courtesy PTI

The PTI alleged that the police arrested more than ten workers in the metropolis, including Sial. The party further claimed that six PTI workers were arrested in Pano Aqil and fifteen workers in Kandhkot, with cases also registered against them.

Addressing the protesters, Sheikh demanded the immediate release of Dr Masroor Sial and all detained workers in Karachi, Pano Aqil and Kandhkot, while Raza Azhar said the PTI “formally submitted an application seeking permission for the peaceful protest, yet police still resorted to unlawful use of force”.

Sheikh also took to X and claimed that the route to the KPC had been blocked by containers, slamming the PPP government for sealing off the area.

“The Karachi Press Club is neither a Red Zone nor a sensitive security area, yet the PPP government has blocked public access and trampled the constitutional right to peaceful assembly,” he wrote.

Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah took notice of the congestion and issued strict instructions to the Sindh inspector general and the Karachi additional inspector general to restore traffic flow.

“Traffic should be cleared from Sadar, Old City Area, MA Jinnah Road and Zainab Market immediately,” he was quoted as saying in a statement from his office. “Additional traffic police personnel should be deployed on the roads and a report should be submitted.”

He further ordered that queues of cars on Napier Road, Regal Chowk and Bolton Market should also be cleared.

Similarly, Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar sought details from the Karachi Traffic deputy inspector general (DIG) on the traffic jams in the city, with a statement from his office saying that the cause behind the disruption should be determined.

“District police should help traffic police in clearing the roads and highways,” Lanjar was quoted as saying. “The difficulties faced by citizens should be immediately addressed.”

He ordered that traffic police personnel should be stationed on all major arteries and pressure points to manage the flow of traffic, adding that they need to be cleared immediately to restore traffic flow.

“In case of traffic flow being affected, alternative routes should be arranged immediately,” Lanjar added. “Citizens should face minimum difficulties; traffic flow should be ensured at all costs.”

Imran — imprisoned since Aug 5, 2023, for concealing details of Toshakhana gifts — is serving a 14-year sentence at Rawalpindi’s Adiala jail in a £190 million corruption case, also known as the Al-Qadir Trust case .

While imprisoned, Imran has not met his family or party leaders since his sister Uzma Khanum met him last December, despite a court order from the Islamabad High Court mandating meetings on Tuesdays and Thursdays.

His sisters have staged regular sit-ins on Tuesdays, demanding meetings with the ex-premier and that he be treated for a severe eye condition.

His eye ailment — right central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) — came to light in late January and he receives government-provided treatment .

The government and the opposition have been engaged in a blame game , with the latter accusing the former of a lack of transparency in not ensuring appropriate treatment for Imran, and not allowing his personal physicians access to him. The government denies these allegations.

The opposition has also demanded that the former premier be shifted to Shifa International Hospital, be treated in the presence of his personal physicians and allowed to meet his family.

World.title: India panel warns Meta over Modi video removal
World.content:
An Indian parliamentary panel called on Wednesday for Meta chief Mark Zuckerberg to apologise for the temporary removal of a video of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

India, the world’s most populous country, is Meta’s largest market by users, with hundreds of millions of people using Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp.

Modi’s video, addressing students during youth-led protests on July 23, was briefly removed from Meta-owned Facebook and Instagram, but was later restored.

Meta has said it was caused by technical error.

Nishikant Dubey, who heads the parliamentary committee on communications and information technology, said the panel blamed Meta.

“Deleting the prime minister’s video was not the work of an intermediary, but that of a publisher,” Dubey said, a lawmaker in Modi’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). “Zuckerberg will have to apologise within three days.”

Joel Kaplan, chief global affairs officer at Meta, said he met with India’s Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Wednesday and apologised.

“I apologised to the minister on behalf of Meta for the error restricting PM Modi’s post,” Kaplan said in a statement.

India’s parliamentary standing committees scrutinise government policies and can summon officials and company executives to answer questions.

However, they cannot themselves impose penalties, revoke legal protections or direct prosecutions.

Any action against an online platform would have to be taken by the government or the courts under existing law.

Dubey said that the committee had written to the interior and technology ministries demanding action.

“If he does not apologise, then all the safe harbour protections that have been provided to his social media platforms should end,” Dubey told reporters.

Modi posted the vertical video, speaking directly to the camera, on July 23 — during the height of protests led by the online Cockroach Janta Party movement.

The demonstrations, which began in New Delhi, were sparked by anger over exam irregularities but grew into a wider movement over jobs, youth opportunities and what critics describe as Modi’s increasingly authoritarian rule.

Modi, a keen user of X, turned to Instagram — issuing his first vertical videos to tap into the youth medium of choice.

In the video, Modi assured students that the government would implement stricter laws and harsher punishments against paper leaks.

Zuckerberg apologises to India government over Meta content and errors, local media says

Zuckerberg has apologised to the Indian government over child sexual abuse material on the company’s platforms and for operational errors, local television channels reported on Wednesday.

Zuckerberg apologised for the presence of the material, as well as deepfake content and operational lapses on Meta’s platforms, financial news publication Moneycontrol reported, citing sources.

The publication added the apology was conveyed during a meeting between Meta executives and Indian government officials on Tuesday.

Meta, whose major social media apps include Facebook and Instagram, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

World.title: AJK elections: PML-N, PPP secure one seat each following delayed polls in Muzaffarabad constituencies
World.content:
MUZAFFARABAD: The PML-N and PPP have secured one seat each in the two constituencies of Muzaffarabad division where polling was held on Tuesday after being fully or partially deferred due to landslides and adverse weather that blocked roads and prevented the timely dispatch of polling staff and election material.

The contest was part of the second phase of elections in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), during which candidates vied for seats in Muzaffarabad division and 12 seats reserved for refugees from India-occupied Kashmir.

According to official results released by the AJK Election Commission, PML-N’s Noreen Arif bagged the LA-27 (Kutla) seat with 18,919 votes, beating first runner-up, Sardar Tabarak Ali of the Istehkam-i-Pakistan Party (IPP) by 298 votes. PPP’s Sardar Javed Ayoub was the second runner-up, with 18,037 votes.

Meanwhile, PPP’s Syed Bazil Ali Naqvi bagged 28,214 votes to win the LA-28 (Lachhrat) seat, where PML-N’s Chaudhry Shahzad Mahmood secured 26,866 votes to emerge as the first runner-up. The third runner-up, Syed Yasir Hussain Naqvi of All Jammu and Kashmir Conference, managed to get just 873 votes.

Along with these results, the Election Commission also notified the returned candidates for the rest of the seats that were up for grabs in the second phase of the elections.

The total number of seats won by the PML-N stands at 24 while the PPP has bagged 10.

The PML-N had secured nine of the 13 seats in the first phase of the elections in Mirpur division while the PPP had secured four. After Sunday’s and Tuesday’s elections in the second phase, the PML-N bagged 15 more seats, while the PPP managed to add just six more to its tally.

The third and final phase of the elections will be held in AJK’s Poonch division on August 10, during which 11 seats will be up for grabs.

Elections in AJK are being held in three phases over security concerns and amid protests by the now proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee.

Since early June, AJK has witnessed protests by the JAAC, which has been demanding the abolition of the 12 refugee seats in the AJK legislature. The protests have also been marred by violence .

World.title: Pakistan, US hold counter-terrorism dialogue, reaffirm commitment to combating terrorist groups
World.content:
WASHINGTON: The United States and Pakistan on Tuesday held the fourth counter-terrorism dialogue in Washington, reaffirming their commitment to combating terrorist groups and strengthening security cooperation at a time when regional tensions remain high.

The talks were led by US Coordinator for Counterterrorism Ambassador Gregory LoGerfo and Foreign Ministry Special Secretary Ambassador Nabeel Munir, a joint statement released by the US State Department said.

“The dialogue underscored shared interests in the US-Pakistan counter-terrorism partnership and the two countries’ determination to confront terrorism,” the joint statement said.

“Delegations exchanged views on the current threat environment, explored avenues to enhance collaboration, and discussed steps to strengthen border security and disrupt terrorist facilitation networks,” it added.

The statement specifically named ISIS-Khorasan (ISIS-K), Al Qaeda, the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), and the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) and its affiliates among organisations that both governments said posed threats to regional security.

“The US and Pakistan affirmed their joint resolve to confront terrorist organisations that endanger the safety of their citizens and the stability of the region,” the statement said.

“The two governments committed to ensuring their counter-terrorism collaboration to keep both of their nations safe and secure, and as part of an enduring vision of regional peace, prosperity, and stability,” it said.

Meanwhile, the Foreign Office said that the two sides held “extensive deliberations on the regional and global terrorist threat and pledged to deepen counter-terrorism collaboration both bilaterally and at multilateral fora”.

The renewed engagement marks a shift from the difficult period in US-Pakistan relations following the withdrawal of American forces from Afghanistan in 2021. Washington had expressed concerns over terrorists sanctuaries in the region, while Islamabad repeatedly highlighted the security challenges it faced from cross-border militancy and instability in Afghanistan.

In recent years, both countries have sought to focus on areas of mutual interest, including counter-terrorism, trade, investment, climate cooperation, and regional stability.

Pakistan’s strategic location and longstanding diplomatic links with neighbouring countries have also increased its importance in regional diplomacy. The country’s diplomatic role also gained renewed attention during the US-Iran conflict, as Islamabad has mediated between the two sides.

The improved engagement with the US also comes as Pakistan continues to face serious internal security challenges. According to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies, an Islamabad-based think tank, violence linked to terrorist attacks and counter-terrorism operations intensified sharply in July, making it the deadliest month of 2026, with 112 security personnel among 205 people killed.

Pakistan, US look to finalise reciprocal trade framework

While representatives from the US and Pakistan held counter-terrorism discussions in Washington, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb held a virtual meeting with United States Trade Representative Ambassador Jamieson Greer from Islamabad.

The meeting was held to review the progress of ongoing negotiations, which are focused on strengthening bilateral trade and economic cooperation between Pakistan and the US, a statement released by the finance ministry said.

The engagement took place roughly three weeks after the finance minister visited Washington, where he held talks with senior American officials on trade, tariffs, investment and economic cooperation.

During his visit, Aurangzeb held meetings with officials from the Office of the Trade Representative, the US Export-Import Bank (Exim), the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) and the International Monetary Fund.

The discussions focused on a possible bilateral trade agreement covering tariffs, market access, investment opportunities and wider economic cooperation. Separate talks with the Exim Bank and the DFC explored financing for infrastructure, energy and private-sector investment projects in Pakistan.

During the meeting on Wednesday, he recalled his recent discussions in Washington and “welcomed the steady progress made by the respective negotiating teams and appreciated the constructive engagement that has characterised the dialogue over time”, the finance ministry said.

It added that both sides noted that negotiations on the proposed reciprocal trade framework had advanced significantly and reaffirmed their shared commitment to conclude the agreement at the earliest.

“The finance minister highlighted the importance of maintaining the momentum of negotiations in view of Pakistan’s economic priorities.

“He emphasised that a strengthened trade and investment partnership with the United States would contribute to Pakistan’s export-led growth strategy, support economic resilience, and create greater commercial opportunities for businesses in both countries,” the statement read.

It further said that Aurangzeb also underlined the importance of continued collaboration with the Exim Bank to facilitate bilateral trade and investment.

According to the finance ministry, Ambassador Greer acknowledged Pakistan’s continued engagement throughout the negotiations.

He reaffirmed the United States’ commitment to “sustaining the positive trajectory of bilateral trade discussions and expressed confidence that the remaining issues could be resolved through continued technical engagement”, the finance ministry said.

It added that Aurangzeb also emphasised the importance of maintaining close coordination and accelerating technical-level discussions to build on the progress already achieved.

“Both sides expressed satisfaction with the progress achieved and agreed to continue working closely to finalise the remaining elements of the framework and agreed to continue regular engagement with a view to concluding the reciprocal trade framework soon, further strengthening the longstanding economic partnership between Pakistan and the United States,” the ministry’s statement read.

It added that Greer also “appreciated the progress made on labour and regulatory reforms, including measures relating to forced labour compliance”.

Pakistan is among the 60 countries on which the US imposed new import tariffs last month over what Washington said was their failure to effectively prohibit imports of goods produced with forced labour.

Pakistan was placed in the lower 10 per cent tariff category, alongside countries that had either adopted forced labour import prohibitions, committed to doing so under reciprocal trade arrangements, or had partial enforcement regimes.

The finance ministry said that Pakistan’s Federal Secretary for Commerce Jawad Paul and senior team members of the USTR also joined Wednesday’s meeting.

World.title: Strong El Nino could push 49 million more people into acute hunger, UN agency says
World.content:
A powerful El Nino weather event could push an additional nearly 49 million people into acute food insecurity across some of the world’s most vulnerable regions by the end of next year, the World Food Programme (WFP) said on Wednesday.

The UN agency said in a report that there was an 81 per cent chance of a very strong El Nino event, with sea surface temperatures at their warmest levels since at least 1982 and potentially making it the strongest such event since 1950.

El Nino, a periodic warming of ocean surface temperatures in the Pacific, alters global weather patterns and is often associated with drought in Southern Africa, delayed monsoons in parts of Asia and erratic rainfall elsewhere.

“These are events that in the past have triggered large-scale hunger,” Jean-Martin Bauer, director of WFP’s Food Security and Nutrition Analysis Service, told reporters.

Based on an analysis of 45 countries deemed vulnerable to the adverse effects of El Nino, WFP estimates that the number of people facing acute food insecurity could rise by almost 49 million to a total of 274 million people, an increase of 22pc, relative to the baseline population already experiencing crisis-level food insecurity or worse.

Central America and Southern Africa are expected to be among the hardest-hit regions, with the number of food-insecure people set to increase by 83pc in Central America and nearly 75pc in Southern Africa, the WFP report said.

Southern Africa as well as South America and the Caribbean could each see more than 12 million additional people fall into acute food insecurity.

Bauer said global food markets entered the El Nino period in a relatively strong position following good harvests in 2025, but warned that conflict in the Middle East and potential weather-related crop losses could put further upward pressure on prices.

While past El Nino events have not typically triggered major global food price spikes, regional shortages and higher prices could worsen food access for vulnerable households, he said.

Funding cuts from US and European donors in 2025 were also hampering efforts to monitor the developing crisis, with Bauer describing a growing drought of food-security data used to assess the impact of El Nino.

WFP conducted about 1.1 million household surveys in 2024, compared with about 800,000 in 2025, while data collection has fallen further this year due to funding restrictions.

“At a time when you have a risk like an El Nino, it is important to have high-frequency data collection,” Bauer said, warning that reduced monitoring could make it harder to identify emerging food crises quickly.

Early action required

WFP said current forecasts point to rainfall deficits in parts of East Africa, the Sahel, Central America and the Caribbean, while flood risks could rise in Somalia and neighbouring areas.

Significant impacts are also projected across South and Southeast Asia, where drought risks, uneven monsoons and localised flooding could disrupt agricultural production, the report stated.

The agency stressed that the forecasts remain uncertain and that impacts will vary across regions, but warned that governments and aid agencies needed to prepare.

Richard Choularton, director of WFP’s Climate and Resilience Service, said the agency had scaled up anticipatory action programmes in 18 countries, reaching more than 1.3 million people so far this year with cash and other assistance to help in the event of extreme weather.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.
