Tech.title: BenQ GV50 Review: Highly Portable, but With Quality Trade-Offs
Tech.content:
You can slide the projector up or down on the base for a vertical shift up a wall or ceiling. For a horizontal tilt, you can fold out the base’s two feet and point the projector at a slight angle on the ceiling. No matter the direction, it’s easy to slide around but also stays put.

The projector only has one HDMI port, which you can use for ARC 5.1 pass- through audio or connecting to another source, like a gaming console. There’s a USB-A port and a USB-C port, both for connecting a thumb drive or a hard drive (or charging a gadget), plus a 3.5-mm port. The GV50 does not have an Ethernet port and uses Wi-Fi 5, which is older and not as widely compatible or as speedy as modern standards like Wi-Fi 6E or Wi-Fi 7. I had some connection issues with my Google Nest mesh network where the projector couldn’t connect.

Photograph: John Brandon

Aside from needing to complete a system update that took about 45 minutes, setup was ultra-smooth and mostly involved using the Google Home app to scan a QR code and install the apps. The GV50 used auto-keystoning to map to my projector screen, and it worked well. When I used the projector on a wall and on the ceiling, the keystoning also worked—I only made a few minor adjustments to the size. The GV50 remote uses the typical, intuitive BenQ layout with a Home button in the center, a setup button that's easy to find, and shortcut buttons for Netflix, YouTube, and Prime.

Not only can the GV50 run on battery power, but it also has plenty of settings to manage its efficiency, including powering down automatically after a set period. I found Battery mode to be marginally helpful, since I use the device in my house, connected to a wall outlet, but the capability does add portability should you want to use the projector while camping or living anywhere else that outlets are sparse. You can use the projector on battery charge alone for a few hours, but the device will dim a little bit to save power.

Picture Quality and More

The GV50 is not trying to be a cinematic marvel by any means, but the projector failed my typical Spears & Muncil benchmark tests. I noticed the skin tone tests were about average for a midrange model like this, not showing much tonal variation. In the demo reel tests, the 1080p quality and lack of good contrast and brightness were much more obvious. A red cactus and yellow flower lacked vividness, and trees in the foreground of a mountain scene looked too dark and mixed into the inky black background. Butterflies that should have looked bright and colorful looked dull, flat, and a bit lifeless.

When I switched to streaming from my iPhone 17 Pro and an iPad 12.9-inch, the GV50’s slow processing speed became an issue. While both Google Cast and Apple AirPlay were functional, the playback was choppy and jittery. If I tried to fast-forward, the stream would pause or fail altogether due to the paltry 2 GB of RAM and 1.5-GHz processor.

Tech.title: Cougars Lower the Risks of Car Crashes by Hunting Deer
Tech.content:
If you’re worried about car accidents caused by deer, you might want to look into bringing some cougars into town.

A study published Wednesday in the journal Current Biology finds that car accidents involving deer in the US could go down as much as 76% in areas where there is a healthy population of the big cats. The presence of cougars around roads cutting through forests or around a development edging up to the woods, the researchers found, made deer avoid these areas, leading to fewer accidents.

Cougars—also called mountain lions, panthers, or pumas—are native to the Americas. But due to habitat loss and hunting their range in North America dropped off considerably following European colonization. Now, cougars are mostly found in the western US states and a small part of Florida.

Deer, on the other hand, have flourished. With fewer predators and limits on their hunting—as well as land being cleared for agriculture—their habitat and populations have greatly expanded across the US over the past century.

As deer populations have grown, though, so have traffic accidents. According to State Farm, there were 1.8 million auto insurance claims filed between 2022 and 2023 involving crashes with animals; deer are the most common cause. The Insurance Institute for Highway Safety, an industry nonprofit, tracks that deadly collisions with animals and cars have steadily risen since the 1970s; last year, more than 200 people died in car crashes involving animals. Deer are a hazard in part because there are so many of them and in part because they frequently forage on the side of roadways.

The new study looks at how mountain lions can play the role of a traffic cop, using data collected on the Olympic Peninsula, where the research team has run a cougar monitoring program since 2018. That work, run by the nonprofit Panthera, built on the work of tribal biologists who had been observing the cats for decades, says Justin Suraci, one of the study’s lead authors and a senior scientist at Conservation Science Partners, another wildlife nonprofit involved in the research. The study, he says, aimed to look at the “costs and benefits” of humans coexisting with predators. While the costs ranchers can incur when predators kill cattle and other economic impacts have been well-documented, the benefits have been less studied, says Suraci.

To look at how cougars affected deer behavior, the researchers compared data selected from more than 500 cameras across the peninsula with data gathered from a year of car accidents that involved deer. Cougars “are ambush predators,” Suraci says: “They prefer these sort of edgy, moderately fragmented habitats—roads cutting through the forest or lower density development, pushing up against a forested area.” This type of habitat “gives them opportunity to conceal themselves and attack the deer that's foraging just outside the forest.”

The deer, accordingly, have decided to stay away from those areas. “They're actually moving away from the habitat edges deeper into the woods and therefore are less exposed to the roads and development that would be associated with traffic and vehicle collisions,” Suraci says.

These avoidances can add up to safer conditions for drivers. The researchers found that deer were 15% more likely to avoid areas with roads where cougars were known to hunt, and were 86% more likely to spend time in more wooded areas. They were also more active during the day. The number of collisions in a five-year span was greatly reduced, going down more than 76% compared to areas with a low number of cougars.

Prior studies looking at how carnivore populations could affect deer-related traffic accidents helped the researchers develop their methodology, Suraci says , including one modeling potential cougar expansion and one studying the reintroduction of wolves into parts of Wisconsin. These enabled the team to look at behavioral patterns of deer in areas where predators hadn’t been newly introduced and helped to rule out fewer accidents due to the decline in deer numbers caused by cougars hunting them.

Tech.title: Gene-Edited Puppies Will Melt Your Heart—but Won’t Trigger Your Allergies
Tech.content:
Scientist Matt Walker always wanted a dog, but allergies prevented him from having one.

As an undergrad at Harvard and then a research associate at Columbia University, he was using Crispr, the Nobel Prize–winning gene editing technology, in lab experiments. He wondered, could he use gene editing to make allergy-free dogs—and help his pet ownership dream come true?

The answer came in beagle form. Bailey and Alfie are two young beagles that can do tricks like any other dog, but they lack the protein that causes sniffles. They’re the culmination of years of work at Kindred Companion Sciences, a biotech company Walker founded in 2020 that emerged from stealth this week with the two pups in tow.

In a scientific paper published on Wednesday in The Crispr Journal, Walker and his colleagues detail how they used gene editing to remove an allergy-causing protein in the dogs. The culprit for most dog allergy-sufferers is a protein called Can f 1, which is found in dander, hair, and saliva. It’s the most common dog allergen, causing reactions in more than half of people with dog allergies. (There are several other Can f proteins that can cause allergies.) Studies have found that even dog breeds labeled as hypoallergenic often carry equal or higher levels of these proteins compared to other dogs.

“This motivated the question of whether we could use gene editing to directly get rid of that allergen at its source,” Walker says.

The Kindred team used Crispr to knock out the gene that produces Can f 1 in skin cells taken from a female beagle. They then used a cloning method called somatic cell nuclear transfer to inject the edited cells into eggs from donor beagles. After creating 25 embryos with the Can f 1 gene edit, they transferred them to a surrogate. Two of the embryos developed to term, resulting in the birth of two puppies.

The dogs’ birth weights were normal, and they had no congenital abnormalities. But the team needed to know whether the allergy-inducing protein had actually been eliminated. First, they sequenced the dogs’ DNA to confirm that the edit was present. Then, they took samples of the dogs’ saliva and dander to measure levels of the Can f 1 protein. Testing showed no detectable protein compared to samples from non-edited dogs, including a beagle, poodle, and golden doodle, which had clear Can f 1 signals.

To make sure the dogs wouldn’t cause allergic reactions in people, Walker served as the guinea pig for a skin prick test, which involves applying small drops of allergens in liquid form on the skin and gently pricking the surface to see if there’s a reaction. Drops from the edited dog did not elicit a skin response ,while drops from a non-edited dog did.

Tech.title: No One Can Afford to Make ‘Myst’ Games Anymore
Tech.content:
In the 1990s, the puzzle adventure game Myst sold more than 6 million copies—so many that WIRED credited it with sparking the widespread adoption of CD-ROM drives. It remained the bestselling PC game of all time until 2002, when The Sims set a new record.

Last week—after four sequels, one spinoff, and five remakes—the creators of Myst released a trailer for a new game in the franchise. Codenamed Anglerfish, it’s a darker chapter in the Myst series where you, the player, are held hostage in a strange world. Your captor is a writer with a temper, voiced and motion captured in a stunning performance by Noshir Dalal, known for his work in Red Dead Redemption 2, Horizon Forbidden West, and Ghost of Yōtei. Reactions to the trailer on YouTube were ecstatic.

The only problem? Anglerfish died months ago when no one agreed to fund it.

“Even the publishers who felt passionate about the project couldn't get their higher-ups to let the money flow,” says Eric A. Anderson, creative director at Cyan Worlds, the oldest surviving independent game studio in America. After spending four months developing a fully playable demo, Cyan pitched the game to more than a dozen publishers at last year’s Game Developers Conference and the Design, Innovate, Communicate, Entertain (D.I.C.E) Summit, where Cyan’s recent remake of Riven: The Sequel to Myst was nominated for a D.I.C.E. Award for Outstanding Achievement in Game Direction.

Cyan hoped it would come away from the conferences with a funding agreement between $1 million and $10 million to finish building Anglerfish. But even though the demo was positively received by most publishers, Cyan went home empty-handed, put Anglerfish on ice, and soon laid off 12 people, roughly half of its staff.

“If we were pitching that game just a few years earlier, it would have been a no-brainer,” says John Eternal, the former global lead of partner development at PlayStation, who helped Cyan pitch Anglerfish. “But funding for double-A games has evaporated.”

Like movies and books, video games are currently facing a middle-market collapse. At the top, so-called triple-A studios like Rockstar (Grand Theft Auto VI), Naughty Dog (The Last of Us), and Bungie (Marathon) regularly spend more than $200 million to develop and market a single game. At the bottom, micro-indie studios usually spend less than $1 million.

Tech.title: Viral Mugshot Accounts Are Humiliating Women Years After Their Arrests
Tech.content:
About a month after Megan Davis’ biological mother died of a drug overdose in July 2025, she went out for drinks with a friend in Northgate, a cluster of bars in College Station, Texas.

She downed a couple of shots and got into an altercation with another group of patrons after bumping into them, according to Davis and body camera footage. Security at the bar kicked Davis out and called the police, who charged her with public intoxication, resulting in an overnight jail stay and a $450 fine.

“Right before my mugshot was taken, I had a panic attack,” says Davis, who was 23 at the time. “I knew I made a big mistake.” After being released the next morning, she set up a payment plan for the fine, and put the incident behind her.

Beginning the day of her arrest, on August 21, 2025, Davis' mugshot started going viral. It was first posted to the Facebook page SayCheese Brazos County Mugshots & Arrests, one of about a dozen Texas-specific mugshot pages under the SayCheese brand, then turned into a hoax on Facebook, alleging she was an Olive Garden waitress who’d been arrested for throwing breadsticks at a customer over tips. Then, on October 12, 2025, her mugshot appeared on Mugshawtys, a popular Instagram account that posts mugshots of young women, often framed as thirst traps.

Thousands of people have now commented—and harshly judged—Davis’ looks and character; when Mugshawtys reposted her photo in a roundup in June, a man wrote in comment on the post “I bet there [sic] parents are proud of them.” Davis replied underneath that her mother had died weeks before the mugshot was taken. “I hope she’s proud of what I’ve done to better myself since this happened,” she wrote.

Almost a year later, Davis is still wading through the fallout. “All that this has been for me is just being dragged through the mud,” Davis says, adding that she’s taken “full accountability” for the incident.

“I just don't understand where we are going to draw a line with social media and privacy.”

Mugshawtys was started around a decade ago by Josh Jeffery, a 31-year-old electrician in California. Up until very recently, it had about 1.8 million Instagram followers, including many loyal, mostly male fans—some of whom trawl arrest bookings and mugshot sites to send in submissions. The brand, which gained a million followers after being featured on Joe Rogan’s podcast last year, according to Jeffery, also had 19,000 Facebook followers and currently has nearly half a million on X.

Within the last week, in response to a list of questions from WIRED, both Meta and TikTok disabled Mugshawtys accounts on their respective platforms. A Meta spokesperson said the account breached multiple policies, pointing WIRED to its community standards page. A TikTok US spokesperson declined to comment on why the account was removed. Jeffery did not respond to a request for comment about the removals. X did not reply to a request for comment.

Jeffery says he’s friends with some of the girls he features on the page—and claims he’s not trying to exploit them. “A lot of them end up doing some form of OnlyFans or content creation or something,” he claims, adding that he encourages Mugshawtys followers to chip in for the women's bail or legal fees.

But the pages are rife with sexual fantasies and misogynistic jokes. “They don’t have to be old enough to drink, just old enough to swallow,” read one comment under an Instagram post featuring a woman arrested for underage drinking. Under carousel posts of mugshots, men wrote comments like “mid,” “that’s a man,” “6 at best,” sometimes ranking women in order of who they find attractive. Last summer, Mugshawtys’ Instagram account posted a photo of a woman who appears to be wearing an anti-suicide smock. The caption stated she had been arrested for alleged child endangerment. The gloved hand of a jail official is seen holding her head while she grimaces and pulls away from the camera. A comment underneath read "child abuse i hope the guards pushed her head to other places." The caption mislabeled the woman’s charges, and the case was ultimately disposed. But many commenters seem unaware that the existence of a mugshot is not an admittance of guilt.

Tech.title: 3 Best Tracking Devices for Your Keys, Wallet, and More (2026)
Tech.content:
Peak Design Beacon Finder Card for $40: At just 1.8 millimeters thick, this is one of the slimmest wallet trackers I’ve tested. It slid into my card holder without adding noticeable bulk, which is more than I can say for every tracker card. It’s also IP68 rated for dust and water resistance, making it one of the more durable cards. Setup took only a few seconds after its initial charge, and the rechargeable battery lasts about five months between charges. Unfortunately, it only works with Apple’s Find My network, so it’s not for Android users. If you own an Android, I’d recommend the Chipolo Card or the UAG Metropolis Dual Tracker Card instead.

Photograph: Adrienne So

Groove Smart Wallet Trace for $125: According to the company, the Groove Wallet is the first wallet with built-in Find My capabilities and a built-in battery. It blocks RFID transmission—although I feel obligated to remind you that there has never been a real-world case of RFID skimming—and is made from attractive aerospace-grade anodized aluminum. It fits up to six cards, which you can push out easily with a flick of the thumb. There's also a money clip on the back for your cash. I don't particularly like a hard wallet; it doesn't conform to your body, so it's uncomfortable to have it clank around in your pocket. It also doesn't have a zipper, so you can't stuff random receipts inside. Still, it's much more protective than a leather wallet. It's also only compatible with iOS, not Android. It has a 94-year warranty but a battery life of around two years, after which you need to contact Groove customer service for a $10 replacement. —Adrienne So

Life360 Tile Sticker for $25: Even as AirTags and other Bluetooth finders have become more popular, Tile trackers remain ubiquitous and come in a wider variety of forms. The latest models are even more durable and waterproof, and the batteries are replaceable. However, I still think the most useful form is the Tile stickers, which are great for remotes and the back of my Kindle Paperwhite. Each sticker is waterproof, has a three-year battery life, and offers a 150-foot range, which is pretty impressive for a tool so small. After a year, the small bump did get knocked off my much-abused Kindle; however, I still think this is a fair price to pay for being able to read my requisite soothing 10 to 15 pages of Naomi Novik before going to bed every night. —Adrienne So

Tech.title: 10 Handy Kitchen Tools That Will Keep You on Top of Your Wellness Goals
Tech.content:
Having the right tools in your kitchen will keep you on track with your health goals. Kathrin Ziegler/Getty Images

If you’ve set specific health goals for yourself this year, you need to make sure your kitchen is set up for success. Having the right cooking tools can make meal prep easier, which helps you stay on track. There is even some kitchen tech that can assist in making multiple dishes at once. A good chef’s knife and storage containers are also good to have on hand to make prep as quick as possible and for storing leftovers.

We spoke with dietitians and nutritionists to learn which kitchen tools you should invest in if you want to stay consistent with your goals. The right tools will help you establish healthy habits so you’re more likely to stick with them over time.

Pressure cooker

A pressure cooker is a useful tool to have in your kitchen if you’re short on time but still want readily available healthy meals. Abra Pappa, a licensed nutritionist, swears by her Instant Pot, saying, “This is a game-changer for busy home cooks because it allows you to make deeply flavorful, nutrient-dense soups, stews, beans and broths with minimal hands-on time.” Pappa recommends it to her clients who want healthy meals but don’t have the time to stand over the stove.

If you’re looking for a pressure cooker, these are our favorite Instant Pots.

Countertop air fryer

If you like fried foods but are trying to limit saturated fats, an air fryer is an appliance you’ll want to own. “The air fryer is one of the most practical tools for eating more vegetables consistently,” explains Pappa. “You can throw in fresh or frozen veggies, walk away and it automatically shuts off when they’re done — which is perfect for busy households.” What you end up with are perfectly roasted and crispy vegetables. Other foods you can prepare in the air fryer include meats, potatoes, hard-boiled eggs and even reheated leftover pizza.

“In my clinical work, the goal is always the same: reduce friction, shorten prep time and make healthy cooking feel easy and rewarding,” Pappa says. If you’re looking for air fryer options and don’t know where to begin, you can use our best air fryers list for guidance.

Best Air Fryers of 2026: We Put 20 Models to the Test and Found the 7 Best See at CNET

Cutting board

A solid cutting board is also key to effortlessly preparing your favorite health-conscious meals. You can pick from wood, plastic, stone or glass, depending on your preferences and needs. Wood and plastic tend to be the most popular options, but you also want to make sure your board is easy to clean.

Avoid cutting boards that aren’t stain-resistant and that have soft surfaces because a knife can penetrate them. Lindsey Schoenfeld, a registered dietitian and professional chef, relies on a dishwasher-safe cutting board. “The Epicurean Kitchen Series Cutting Board is lightweight, easy to store, protects your knife and can be cleaned in the dishwasher,” she says.

Chef’s knife

A chef’s knife can make or break your meal preparation. You want to invest in a quality chef’s knife because it makes your prep process more efficient. The last thing you want is a knife with a dull blade that leaves messy, uneven cuts in the food you’re chopping.

When choosing a chef’s knife, look for one that’s versatile enough to cut through meats, vegetables and herbs. Additionally, you want to research the different chef’s knives available and consider the blade, weight, handle and materials.

“I recommend the WüsthofClassic 8-Inch Chef’s Knife, but there are many to choose from,” Schoenfeld says. She advises choosing an eight-inch chef’s knife when shopping because “while it seems big, it’s efficient and still easy to maneuver for slicing and dicing.”

WÜSTHOF Classic 8 Inch Chef’s Knife,Black $170 at Amazon

Food processor

A food processor is helpful for chopping, grating and cutting up everything from meat and cheese to vegetables and more. It’s a handy, smaller alternative if you don’t have the counter space for a large blender. Devon Golem, a registered dietitian at The Nuanced Nutritionist, says the food processor is a must-have to get vegetables into your meals. One of her favorite mixes includes processing carrots, celery and onion together to elevate dishes from chicken noodle soup to pasta.

”Thoroughly blend any veggie with a food processor to make savory fillings for lasagna, sauces, stews, soups or smoothies,” Golem recommends. Simplifying vegetable prep increases the chances of including these antioxidant- and fiber-rich foods in your diet. These are our top picks, if you’re interested in purchasing a food processor.

Best Food Processors of 2026: KitchenAid, Cuisinart and More See at CNET

Garlic press

A garlic press will make prepping the base of your healthy meals easier. Instead of chopping and mincing garlic with a knife, a garlic press lets you crush it into a paste with a single squeeze.

Pappa regularly uses a garlic press in her kitchen. “This is one of my favorite ‘small but mighty’ tools,” she explains. “You don’t even need to peel the garlic — just press and go — which dramatically cuts down prep time and makes it far more likely people will actually cook with fresh garlic.” Pappa recommends the OXO Garlic Press for your cooking needs.

OXO Good Grips Heavy Duty Garlic Press $20.51 at Amazon

High-quality cookware

One of the best kitchen tools you can invest in is a decent cookware set. “One high-quality sauté pan will do more for your consistency in the kitchen than almost any gadget,” Pappa says. That’s because you’ll use it daily, and a solid cookware set will last you years. “They dramatically reduce friction around cooking — which is key for staying on track,” adds Pappa.

If you’re in the market for a set, you can start by checking out our favorite cookware sets.

Best Cookware Sets Available in 2026 See at CNET

Chef-grade blender

A chef-grade blender will make prep work for salsas, smoothies, batters or blending multiple foods together a breeze. A high-quality blender will last you years and is versatile for most recipes. Schoenfeld swears by her Vitamix for prepping healthy meals. “Its power makes healthy eating easier by effortlessly preparing smoothies, dressings, sauces and soups,” she says. Most store-bought items contain extra sodium, sugars and additives, but these foods can be easily made at home with fewer ingredients.

Schoenfeld also uses her Vitamix for other purposes. “Whether I need a smooth puree or chopped nuts — sometimes I skip my food processor — the Vitamix is] versatile enough for both.” Her favorite foods to make in the Vitamix include pestos, hummus, smoothies and soups.

If you want to invest in a chef-grade blender or similar, CNET tested and rated the best blenders available. There are plenty of options to choose from, whether you’ve been eyeing a Vitamix or prefer something more budget-friendly.

Best Blenders in 2026, Tested by CNET Experts See at CNET

Measuring spoons

Having measuring spoons on hand will make cooking easier since you’ll have a way to measure ingredients for the recipes you’re preparing. Some people instinctively know how much to add of certain seasonings, but for those who don’t, measuring spoons take the guesswork out.

“To watch my salt intake but still have well-seasoned food, I add a quarter teaspoon at a time and limit myself to a teaspoon of salt when cooking six servings,” says Golem. Opt for stainless steel measuring spoons for a dishwasher-safe option.

Sur La Table Spice Measuring Spoons See at Sur La Table

Glass storage containers

Once you’re done meal-prepping, it’s important to have reliable storage to keep your food fresh in the fridge. Glass storage containers are the best option because they won’t break down into microplastics like plastic containers and are easy to clean.

Registered dietitian Shaira Daya‘s favorite storage containers are the Pyrex glass food containers with lids. “I use the containers to hold marinades and pre-chopped ingredients, which help me save time on busy weeknights,” Daya explains.

Pyrex® Simply Store® 18-piece Glass Storage Set $45 at Pyrex

The clear glass containers also reduce food waste because you can see what’s inside as soon as you open your fridge. If you’re limiting plastics in your kitchen to avoid microplastics, glass containers are a solid option that last for years.

Tech.title: iPhone 20 Pro and Pro Max Might Get Bigger Screens in 2027
Tech.content:
Big anniversary, big screens? Apple might bump up the display size of the iPhone Pro and iPhone Pro Max next year as the company celebrates the 20th anniversary of the iPhone, according to an insider.

Digital Chat Station, an anonymous but well-regarded source of tech leaks, shared on Chinese social media platform Weibo that the iPhone 20 Pro could feature a 6.4-inch display, while the iPhone 20 Pro Max could come with a 7-inch screen. Although the account holder’s identity has never been publicly confirmed, Digital Chat Station has built a reputation for providing reliable information about upcoming devices.

Apple is expected to release those devices in September 2027, three months after the company celebrates the 20th anniversary of the iPhone’s launch on June 29, 2007. (For a blast from the past, check out CNET’s review of that legendary device.) Apple has not announced any official launch dates.

A representative for Apple didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

The latest versions of the iPhone Pro and Pro Max are a tad smaller — 6.3 inches for the iPhone Pro and 6.9 inches for the iPhone Pro Max.

The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, expected to launch next month, will also have 6.3- and 6.9-inch screen sizes. According to our roundup of reports and rumors about Apple’s upcoming products, the company’s next lineup could also include its first foldable iPhone, the Apple Watch Series 12, and the Apple Watch Ultra 4

Glass all around?

In addition to the larger screen sizes for the iPhone 20 Pro and Pro Max, the Digital Chat Station report also said the devices might have a quad-curved design and no bezel showing. If true, when you look at the front of those phones, you’ll only see glass that wraps around all four edges. You won’t see a bezel, the border that surrounds the screen, which is typically found on most smartphones.

Digital Chat Station said that, even with the bigger screens, the phones will maintain the same aspect ratio.

The last time Apple increased screen size was two years ago. The iPhone 16 Pro screen size increased to 6.3 inches (up from 6.1), and the Pro Max to 6.9 inches (up from 6.7).

Increasing screen sizes “makes sense” as people consume more content on their iPhones, says Austin Evans, who has been testing tech devices for years on his YouTube channel, which has nearly 6 million subscribers. He also likes the idea of the wraparound glass look on the front display.

“I’m excited to see what they put together for the 20th anniversary,” Evans said. “If they’re able to ship an iPhone with effectively zero bezels at all, it could really set the tone for what an iPhone can be for the next decade.”

What else have we heard?

According to the rumor mill, there could be several other upgrades and changes for the iPhone 20 lineup.

There might not be physical buttons for powering on, adjusting volume or controlling the camera. Instead, solid-state buttons might be integrated into the frame itself, enabling consumers to initiate actions by pressing lightly or firmly.

There might be a Face ID sensor under the main screen, according to some reports. The Dynamic Island might shrink, with the front camera reduced to pinhole size, although these changes might arrive sooner with the iPhone 18.

The iPhone 20 might also have a brighter, thinner OLED panel to reduce glare, increase brightness and use less power.

Internally, the iPhone 20 might be fitted with a second-generation 2nm chip for better efficiency and performance, as well as a pure-silicon anode battery.

Tech.title: T-Mobile Is Stretching Its Device Commitment to 3 Years with New Installment and ‘2.0’ Phone Plans
Tech.content:
In an environment in which everything costs more, the major wireless phone carriers have introduced plans to draw in customers who want to reduce what millions of people see as an essential expense. In recent months, AT&T introduced its modular Build-A-Plan, and Verizon cut prices and then rolled out its Simplicity plan.

Now it’s T-Mobile’s turn.

Starting Thursday, the company is adding a new installment plan for phone purchases, rebranding its slate of unlimited wireless plans and offering student plans with the option to add 5G home internet service.

An extended phone flex

Currently, when you purchase a new phone through T-Mobile, you can buy it outright or pay a monthly installment over 24 months. The new Equipment Installment Plan Flex 36 option lets you make those payments over 36 months, reducing the monthly amount.

What makes EIP Flex 36 different from the company’s EIP Standard plan (which remains an option as EIP Standard 36) is that all upfront costs are rolled into those three years of payments — the device, taxes and fees — making the initial cost zero. Even with most zero percent finance plans, customers must pay taxes on the cost of the phone and pay an activation fee.

T-Mobile’s press release says the EIP Flex 36 option for “well-qualified customers” has, “for a limited time, 0% APR.” When I inquired if “limited time” implied that the rate could go up, a T-Mobile representative confirmed the rate would remain the same during the life of the term. The fine print does note that the rate could be between 0 and 24% depending on a customer’s creditworthiness.

Going forward, the financing options for new customers will be to choose a 36-month EIP plan or pay the full cost of the device. If you want to pay off a phone earlier than the full term, that’s an option, too.

‘2.0’ unlimited plans (that feel more like 1.1)

In software, a full-number version increment implies an update that’s bigger than small tweaks; it’s why your iPhone was recently updated to iOS 26.6, applying fixes and security updates, while iOS 27.0 was just released in beta, with major new features — such as Siri AI — and is expected in September.

Along with EIP Flex 36, T-Mobile is updating its unlimited postpaid mobile plans to 2.0 versions: Experience Beyond 2.0, Experience More 2.0 and Essentials 2.0. (The company did not specifically call out the budget Essentials Saver plan, but I’m told that it will also get the 2.0 treatment.)

However, the 2.0 in this case appears to be a formality to pair with the EIP Flex 36 and EIP Standard 36 installment plans: The features and base pricing remain the same as the Experience Beyond, Experience More and Essentials plans.

T-Mobile says that customers already on those plans can stay where they are, or switch to the 2.0 versions if they want to take advantage of the 36-month financing option.

Student Perks plans

Now that it’s August, with the academic year about to begin, college-bound kids (and their parents) are likely figuring out what they need to pack for school — and that includes mobile phone plans. For those who want their mobile independence, T-Mobile has launched Student Perks discounts that can cost as little as $30 a month (for the Essentials Saver plan with AutoPay enabled). A limit of two students can be on the account.

And for those living off-campus in need of fast internet for all-night writing sessions, T-Mobile is offering a Student Perks bundle of 5G Home Internet for $30 a month. The deal also includes up to $200 back in virtual prepaid card credit when signing up for the service.

Tech.title: Telegram’s Brief App Store Removal Renews Questions About Apple’s CSAM Enforcement
Tech.content:
On Monday, Apple briefly removed the popular messaging app Telegram from the App Store for iOS devices after a report that a user was sharing illegal content. According to both Apple and Telegram CEO Pavel Durov, the app — which has more than 1 billion users — was restored on the App Store within hours. But Durov accused Apple of overreacting to a ransom attempt in a group chat.

In a Telegram post about the incident, Durov said a member of a public group chat edited a previously posted message and added what Durov called “AI-modified illegal content” to it in an attempt to get the group chat flagged, because its admins had presumably refused to pay a ransom. Instead, Apple removed the app from the Apple App Store entirely until the user was banned. Apple confirmed in an email to CNET that Telegram remained available in the separate Mac App Store and that users who already had Telegram downloaded were not affected.

“We briefly removed Telegram from the App Store after our review found content that violates our strict guidelines prohibiting child sexual abuse material,” Apple said in a statement. “The app was subsequently restored after the developer promptly removed the content and banned the user who posted it.”

Apple did not immediately respond to questions about why the Mac version of Telegram remained available for download while the mobile version was removed.

A representative for Telegram declined to comment directly, instead pointing to Durov’s post.

Telegram warns other app developers

Durov said that the extortionist manipulated Apple into an “overreaction” that led to the app’s removal, which he said occurred without warning. That could happen, he said, to other apps that include user content.

“If an app used by more than a billion people can be removed from the App Store without prior warning, any app can be,” Durov wrote.

Telegram’s official X account more pointedly criticized Apple’s actions in a series of posts and replies. In one, Telegram posted, “reports of my demise are greatly exaggerated,” followed by an apple emoji. In another that included a link to Durov’s post, Telegram wrote, “I’m sure this stance will be applied equally to all other apps in the store, in the future, right? @Apple.”

I'm sure this stance will be applied equally to all other apps in the store, in the future right? @Apple



(btw: https://t.co/ZRYqIGaxVH) — Telegram Messenger (@telegram) August 4, 2026

Telegram faces an ongoing dispute with Australian authorities over content related to terrorism and child safety. After Telegram was fined AU$1 million (roughly $700,000) for failing to respond to information requests, the government began pursuing additional penalties against the platform.

Durov is also a target of Russian authorities, who accuse him of facilitating terrorism through Telegram. He was arrested in France in 2024 in connection with an investigation into Telegram’s handling of alleged criminal activity on the platform.

In 2018, Apple temporarily removed Telegram and its experimental client, Telegram X, from the App Store after determining that “inappropriate content” was available through the apps. Telegram restored additional safeguards, and Apple reinstated both apps later the same day.

Tech.title: Pixel 11 Leak Shows a New HiLight LED Light on the Back of the Phone
Tech.content:
The official unveiling of the Google Pixel 11 series is just over a week away, and the leaks and rumors keep spilling out. The latest leaks show a new, multicolored notification light on the back of the phone next to the camera setup. Google has teased the new feature in short YouTube videos released previewing the official event, which is on Aug. 12.

This isn’t the first time we’ve heard of this feature, dubbed Pixel Glow in previous rumors, but the latest leak replaces that name in favor of the less interesting HiLight. The feature itself hearkens back to the old days when many Android phones and BlackBerry devices shipped with notification LEDs. This time around, Google’s putting a bit of a spin on the feature.

On Monday, Roland Quandt of tech site WinFuture shared a post on BlueSky with an image that appears to be official French-language marketing material, showing the Pixel 11 Pro Fold and detailing the new feature.

Pixel Glow is officially called HiLight, I'd say. — Roland Quandt (@rquandt.bsky.social) 2026-08-03T22:18:20.374Z

The text translates as, “When your smartphone is face down, HiLight lights up discreetly when your favorite contacts call or when you chat with Gemini.”

HiLight replaces the temperature sensor introduced in previous Pixel devices. While the earlier sensor saw limited real-world use, HiLight is better positioned as a feature users can benefit from more consistently in everyday use. Still, there’s a reason some people choose to keep their phone face down in public. It helps avoid distractions and prevents notifications from constantly demanding their attention. By making this feature a default part of the experience, Google effectively removes that option unless users can disable it entirely.

What is interesting about HiLight is that it appears to be a very small display rather than a static, multicolored LED. Many of the phones from Nothing Technology have LEDs that light up for notifications and timers, and perhaps HiLight will have its own customizations.

It remains to be seen whether HiLight will be able to work with other apps beyond favorite contact notifications and interactions with Gemini. Developers may have to provide support within their own apps for the feature to work, which could take time and adding support for a single feature on a single family of phones isn’t necessarily the most compelling reason for them to do so.

We’ll learn more about the Pixel 11 family and all of its new bells and whistles next week at Made by Google 2026. We can also expect the debut of the Pixel Watch 5, which has already been spotted in, of all places, the Caribbean Sea.

Tech.title: New DC Studios Show ‘Lanterns’ Is Out This August on HBO Max, Plus New ‘Hard Knocks,’ Conan and More
Tech.content:
HBO takes a lot of the credit for the rise of prestige TV. Shows such as The Sopranos, The Wire, Sex and the City and Game of Thrones were appointment viewing and that tradition lives on with newer series such as Industry, Euphoria and more. Its streaming service, HBO Max, is also the home of tons of great movies, live sports and excellent documentaries.

One of the things HBO Max does best is documentaries, and this August, there are two series we can’t wait for. First up is a new season of the great football series Hard Knocks, which focuses on the Super Bowl-winning Seattle Seahawks during its training camp this season. We’re also excited for Monsters of God, another series about a group of people obsessed with exotic animals from the same filmmaker who gave us Tiger King and Chimp Crazy.

Also arriving this month is the hotly anticipated new DC series Lanterns, which stars Aaron Pierre and Kyle Chandler as two members of the Green Lanterns, along with the third season of Conan O’Brien Must Go.

These titles and many others are out this August on HBO Max. Here’s what you need to know to tune in.

Aug. 4

HBO Max

Hard Knocks: Training Camp With the Seattle Seahawks (season 22)

Hard Knocks, the HBO sports documentary that gives an inside look at an NFL team during its annual training camp, will return on Aug. 4 for a new season. This year, the cameras follow the Seattle Seahawks’ preseason, as the team comes off its second Super Bowl win. The season will consist of five episodes, which will air weekly.

Aug. 6

HBO Max

Monsters of God (limited series)

Monsters of God is a docuseries from filmmaker Eric Goode, as he explores the world of exotic animal smuggling. The five-episode series, produced by A24, will introduce us to a motley crew of characters, many of whom are obsessed with rare animals and are willing to break whatever laws they need to in order to get their hands on them. (For a similarly shocking tale of animal obsession, check out Chimp Crazy, the 2024 docuseries also produced by Goode, which is one of those “truth is stranger than fiction” tales that takes viewers on a truly wild ride.)

Aug. 7

Lionsgate

The Strangers: Chapter 2

Renny Harlin directs The Strangers: Chapter 2, the second film in the new Strangers trilogy starring Madelaine Petsch as Maya Lucas, a young woman who is tormented and tracked down by three masked perpetrators known as the Strangers. The film picks up after the death of her boyfriend, Ryan, but the Strangers still have it out for Maya when they realize she’s alive.

Aug. 14

Normal

Bob Odenkirk has proven he can work in any genre. Comedy, drama, action — there’s nothing he hasn’t excelled at. After the success of his gruesome action thriller Nobody (and its sequel), he’s back for Normal, a neo-Western where he stars as Ulysses, the sheriff of a small Minnesota town called Normal. But after a bank robbery in town goes horribly awry, Ulysses learns that the town is mixed up with a whole lot of bad guys, including the Yakuza. The film costars Henry Winkler as the town’s crooked mayor, plus Lena Headey and Peter Shinkoda.

Aug. 16

Lanterns (season 1)

In the new eight-episode DC Studios drama series Lanterns, Aaron Pierre plays John Stewart, a newly recruited Lantern, the intergalactic peacekeepers of the DC Universe. Stewart works alongside Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler) as they investigate a murder in Nebraska that’s just a small piece of a wider mystery. Kelly Macdonald, Nicole Ari Parker and Nathan Fillion costar. The first episode of Lanterns arrives on Aug. 16, and new episodes drop weekly.

Aug. 21

HBO Max

Conan O’Brien Must Go (season 3)

For the past several years, Conan O’Brien has hosted his podcast, Conan O’Brien Needs a Friend, which features conversations with celebrities and fans of the comedian. In his travel series Conan O’Brien Must Go, O’Brien drops in on some of these fans (often to their surprise), imposing on them and insisting they show him around their home countries and introduce him to their cultures. It’s classic Conan, absurd and offbeat, blending travelogue with comedy, as he traipses all over the globe. This season consists of four episodes, which will arrive weekly.

A24

Mother Mary

In the A24 psychodrama Mother Mary, Anne Hathaway stars as a global pop icon who is about to return to the stage after enduring a tragic accident. With just three days before her major comeback performance, she has a meltdown and reaches out to Sam (Michaela Coel), her former collaborator and designer. The two women haven’t spoken in years, falling out after an intimate but contentious relationship. As Sam and Mary let each other back into their lives, they experience something altogether supernatural. The film arrives on HBO Max on Aug. 21.

Tech.title: Waymo Opens Up to All Riders in Dallas
Tech.content:
Waymo on Tuesday opened its doors to all public riders in Dallas, allowing anyone in the area to hail a fully self-driving ride, albeit with some restrictions.

The Alphabet-owned company began operating in Dallas with select passengers in February, amounting to nearly 150,000 people. Now, anyone can download the Waymo app and book an autonomous ride in the Jaguar I-Pace vehicles.

The self-driving service won’t be open to public riders at Dallas Love Field Airport or on freeways just yet, though Waymo says it plans to open up those routes after finalizing testing. Earlier this year, Waymo paused freeway rides in other cities after some of its vehicles struggled to navigate construction zones. It began resuming those routes last week.

With the Dallas launch, Waymo’s autonomous ride-hailing service is now available to the public in nearly a dozen cites. The company also operates in the San Francisco Bay Area, Phoenix, Los Angeles, Miami, Orlando, Nashville, Atlanta and Austin, and has a wait list for riders in Houston and San Antonio.

Waymo is also expanding to more than two dozen other cities across the country, including locations with more inclement weather like Chicago, Detroit and Minneapolis. To handle more variable climates, Waymo is rolling out its sixth-generation self-driving technology aboard its new Ojai vehicle. The latest tech can detect more details and gauge objects in a variety of lighting and weather conditions, according to Waymo.

Waymo is one of a handful of companies building out an autonomous ride-hailing service in the area. Late last year, Uber and robotaxi company Avride launched their partnership in Dallas. Amazon-owned Zoox, which currently offers rides in Las Vegas and San Francisco, also deployed its testing fleet in Dallas earlier this year, and is testing in several more locations.

A little further away, Uber, Lucid Motors and autonomous driving company Nuro are testing their joint Lucid Gravity robotaxi in Houston and the San Francisco Bay Area. May Mobility also operates fully autonomous rides in Atlanta through a partnership with Lyft.

Tech.title: Play Gears of War: E-Day Before Others With Xbox Game Pass
Tech.content:
Gears of War: E-Day is the first mainline entry in the popular sci-fi shooter series since the release of Gears 5 almost seven years ago. While the game won’t be released until Oct. 6, Xbox Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass subscribers can get early access to the game’s open beta two months early, on Thursday, Aug. 6.

Xbox Game Pass, a CNET Editors’ Choice award pick, offers a wide selection of games you can play on your Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S, Xbox One and PC or mobile device for as little as $10 a month. And with a subscription to the higher-tiered Game Pass Ultimate ($23 a month), you can access hundreds of games, including new ones the day they’re released, each month.

Here are all the games Xbox is bringing to Game Pass in August.

Gears of War: E-Day open beta early access

Coming to Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass on Aug. 6.

Grab your lancer and get ready to crush some grubs in the latest entry in the Gears of War franchise before the game’s October release. In the early access open beta, you’ll be able to play the new Horde Siege player-versus-environment game mode. This is a new take on Gears’ Horde mode that’s built for larger maps, more players and bigger battles.

Date Everything!

Coming to Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium and PC Game Pass on Aug. 11.

Dating simulator games can be fun, but they might feel limiting in some aspects. Yeah, you might love your bed, but does your bed share those same feelings for you? This game lets you explore that idea to its logical conclusion by letting you date almost everything in your home. Bed? Absolutely. Door? You bet. The overwhelming sense of existential dread? If that’s your bag, go for it! There are over a hundred items, each with a unique voice actor, that you can date in this game, so have fun!

Ball x Pit

New to Game Pass Premium on Aug. 12. Previously on Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass.

This game combines classic brick-breaking gameplay with the base-building, survival and roguelite genres to create something wholly unique. You’ll explore a bottomless pit of monsters on the hunt for treasure, armed with nothing but ricocheting balls. You’ll recruit fellow treasure hunters, tackle huge monsters and upgrade your arsenal as you plunge deeper underground.

Other games coming to Xbox Game Pass

Those are some of the games Microsoft is bringing to Xbox Game Pass soon, but the company is adding more to the service this month. Here are the other games you can try soon.

Monsters are Coming! Coming to Game Pass Premium on Aug. 6. Previously on Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass.

Powerwash Simulator 2: Coming to Game Pass Premium on Aug. 6. Previously on Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass.

Bounty Star: Coming to Game Pass Premium on Aug. 11. Previously on Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass.

Grounded 2 (game preview): Coming to Game Pass Premium on Aug. 11. Previously on Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass.

Cricket 26: Coming to Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium and PC Game Pass on Aug. 13.

Mio: Memories in Orbit: Coming to Game Pass Premium on Aug. 13. Previously on Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass.

Sandustry: Coming to Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass on Aug. 13.

Egging On: Coming to Game Pass Premium on Aug. 13. Previously on Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass.

Games leaving Game Pass on Aug. 15

While Microsoft is adding titles to Game Pass soon, it’s also removing a handful of games from the service on Aug. 15. So you still have some time to play these games for the first time, or finish your campaign, before you have to buy them separately.

For more on Xbox, learn what other titles you can play, plus read our Xbox Game Pass review and discover which Game Pass plan is right for you.
